en: The Baroque Theatre of Antonio Galli Bibiena inaugurated in the eighteenth century, where 14-year-old Mozart performed.

A karst system of 53 km of tunnels and wells, indicated as the largest in Italy and among the largest in Europe, with stalactites and stalagmites. The guided group tour lasts about two hours on about 2,000 meters of steel footbridge, plus an artificial tunnel of 170 meters; inside the temperature is 7 °C. The ticket includes the shuttle from Levigliani (581 m) at the entrance (850 m).
Mining village that in 1910 had about 3,000 inhabitants, with the Lamarmora washhouse built in 1897 above the sea.
Franciscan monastery of 1463 with belt and three towers, church with two naves and cloister with porch with upper loggia; from 1706 entrusted to the Reformed Fathers.
Contemporary art in a convent.
The parish, largely rebuilt after the earthquake of 1887, with mosaic floor and windows; the oratory with eighteenth-century stuccoes and a polyptych of 1544.
The village living room under the Sciliar.
A shovel from the Amaltheum and a Gothic façade.

The Church of the SS. Trinity is known for its medieval frescoes, that of St. Joseph for the late Baroque façade; the Church of St. Anthony, at the northern entrance of the village, has a portal coming from the cathedral.
Walk in the rock.

Opened in 2001 in Palazzo Martucci, it was born from the rich material of the long military tradition of the Martucci family: in 16 rooms it traces the main Italian wars, from the wars of Independence to the Second World War. The collection of Italian uniforms stands out, which follows the evolution of the uniforms from the Risorgimento to the grey-green and the battle dress of the army of the South Kingdom.
Two thousand years of history in one plain: Roman villa, necropolis and abbey.
Ponte di 275 metri a 15 arcate, started in the thirteenth century (Romanic the first two) and expanded until the seventeenth-seventh century.
The ducal palace with the clock tower.
Ascoli has been the bishop's seat since the 11th century: the cathedral, of Romanesque and Gothic origins, was renovated until the Baroque age.
Ancient and contemporary art in a historic building.

Ancient river port extended over the Panaro, wounded by the earthquake of 2012: the Cathedral of Saints Philip and James reopened in 2024, the ruins of the Castle of the Fortresses and the Tower of Modena became symbol of the earthquake, the Jewish cemetery and the oasis of the Meleghines.
center damaged by the earthquake 2016: check the status of the areas and accessibility of the monuments (Italia.it)
Small museum of peasant civilization and handicrafts, housed in the old Town Hall of Piazza Umberto I.
The Jewish Quarter and the House of Spirits.
The history of Abruzzo.
An unexpected museum of the sea in the Brescian plain.
The Callido organ of 1776.
The place of "The Storn Horse."
The Bourbon foundry in the woods of the Serre.

On the plateau of Lidana, about 8 km east of the village: church in granite cones rebuilt at the beginning of the twentieth century on a sanctuary existing at least from the middle of the sixteenth century, surrounded by horseshoe from the cumbessias, the houses of the pilgrims. To the south of the church knows Perda de sa Itria, granite monolith about 4 meters high; in the surroundings domus de janas, tombs of giants and menhirs. Feast on the last Sunday of July with novena and the palio on Palu de sa Itria.
The Aragonese watchman on the Strait.
Stadel Walser.
The castle that named the municipality.
The long pier in front of the square, where on November 3, 1918 he docked the destroyer Audacious; from here they photograph the square and the Rive.

The Duomo houses a Madonna of the wooden Mercy of the fifteenth century, called "La Madonna bella" and in the crypt the fourteenth-century Gothic sarcophagus of Saint Ansovino; in the Archbishop's Palace the Diocesan Museum.
A panoramic tour between the Sibillini and the sea.
A thousand years of pottery.
The ancient port-emporium of the city.

Gothic-Venice Palace built in 1411 by Nicolò Cavalli, captain of Soave, with trilobed windows with sharp arch, loggia and a Renaissance trifora with lizard and scorpion carved on the columns; the façade was frescoed by Giovanni Maria Falconetto with mythological scenes, today no longer visible. You only see it from the outside.
A pope's shoes.

It rises, according to the source, on a pagan temple dedicated to Isis and before even to Hera and the Dioscuri, was Christianized around the second century and in the fourth century was the city's mother church; dedicated to the Assumption in 1486, it was abandoned after the construction of the new cathedral and restored after 1824.
On the hill of San Nicola there are the remains of the medieval village of Albe and the Castle Orsini of the 14th century, destroyed by the earthquake of 1915.

Open-air art park of 16 hectares on the slopes of the Amiata, in the place called "the Paradise" for the mild climate: the Swiss artist Daniel Spoerri bought the estate in 1991 and exhibited his bronzes from the 1980s; monograph until 1996, open to the public in 1997, today has 113 installations of 55 international artists among trees, meadows and paths, curated by the Hic Terminus Haeret Foundation. The route takes about three hours; restaurant and accommodation on site. Seasonal timetables, to be checked on the site.

Victorian villa of the first half of the nineteenth century, the only example of English architecture of the territory, built by the English entrepreneurs who arrived to exploit the basin of sulphur; it is the seat of the archaeological-industrial Park established by the Region in 2010. On the ground floor the archaeological museum with Sican, Etruscan and Roman artifacts (also from Colle Madore), on the first floor the museum of the zolfare with finds, multimedia, virtual reconstructions and a room immersive on the life of the miners.
Nature, spa and contemporary art.
In the neighborhood of the same name, built around 1100 by the Norman king Ruggero to thank the Virgin for the victory over the Saracens.
The Head of State's Palace.

Almost two hundred tombs of the Iron Age and of the VII-VI century BC under mounds of circular or elliptic stones, excavated only partially by Paola Zancani Montuoro since 1963: ceramic and bronze sets, weapons for men of rank and imported objects, including a Phoenician cup and Corinthian ceramics. Free access, no defined routes.
The cradle of sparkling wine.
Handicraft workshop run by three generations of the Sandrini family, which creates wooden artifacts on its own design and restores wooden works.
A corner of Piacenza with a curious name.
The medieval walls of the village, to be walked along the ancient walk with a view of the countryside; the Porta Senese preserves the doors of the fifteenth century.

Baroque Church, Palatine chapel of the Princes Barberini at the end of the 17th century: it preserves a painting by Francesco Reali with Santa Rosalia defending Palestrina from the plague; in the Hall of Deposits stood the Pietà di Palestrina attributed to Michelangelo, today at the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence.
The little church on the border hill.
The Antonian devotion of Grimaldi.

The village of the Lucanian side called "Porta del Parco" of Pollino, founded in the 16th century by the Pignatelli as a fief of the State of Noia (now Noepoli); it preserves sixteenth-century churches and noble palaces, and from the village you can reach the lake Duglia, the opholitic storms and the source of the Catusa.

The fifteenth-century tower, perhaps on a defensive structure of Arabic age, linked to the Rocca family that named the village; in the eighteenth century it was a stop of the Grand Tour, after 1830 it had two high-pitched windows and battlements. Restored in 2000 and managed by the volunteers of the Literary Park, since 2023 it hosts a permanent exhibition on Quasimodo, which dedicated the poem  "Near a Saracen tower, for his dead brother" (1956), and during the year contemporary art exhibitions.
The art of water wrought iron in a real workshop.

The entire natural reserve of the Veneto Region of 113 hectares, wild wood of holm oaks, lauri and pine trees on dunes that in Roman times were part of a coastal cordon extended up to the Po and Ravenna. There live deer, heroes, badgers and hares, and birds like swamp hawks, common owls, herons and peaks; you visit with guided excursions.

City born in 1866 from the union of Serravalle and Ceneda along the Monticano, at the foot of the Treviso Prealps: the medieval village of Serravalle and, in Ceneda, the museum of the battle that closed the Great War in 1918.
Locomotives and heirlooms of steam trams.
Asger Jorn's house.
The fortress of Malvezzi-Campeggi, with furnished noble apartments and views of the hills.
The 17th-century building.

The village preserves the appearance of a medieval village surrounded by walls of the eighth century, covered by narrow 'vigoli , of the three original gates only the Porta del Cassero is well preserved. Rebuilt after the barbaric invasions under the name of Plebs Tuphiae, it was an autonomous commune from the 11th to the 14th century.
The fountain built in 1559 under the Serenissima and preserved under the porch of the Palazzo dei Trecento: during the celebrations it pined white and red wine.
Write in Morse on a rebuilt telegraph.
Built in 1812-14 and inaugurated on July 4, 1815 with the opera "Evelina" , now home to theatrical exhibitions.

On the ground floor of the rectory, in four rooms with works from the lower Middle Ages to the eighteenth century: sacred paintings, Baroque liturgical fabrics, Renaissance wooden sculptures, reliquaries and illuminated codes. The symbol piece is Chiavenna's "Peace" (Peace), one of the most important medieval jewels in Europe. Inaugurated in 1957, closed in 1981 after attempted theft, reopened on 3 May 1998.
The largest villa in Appia.
The crucifix of Brother Umile's school.
The gold mosaic in the sun.

Built by the Compagnia dei Disciplinati between 1845 and 1854, with decorations from 1907 by Lorenzo and Costantino Mossello and gilded by Bernardo Arduino; since 1910 it houses a cave of the Virgin of Lourdes. It was the church of the Servant of God canon Francis Church.
The basilica where, according to tradition, was announced the first crusade, with the dome frescoed by Pordenone and a 100 steps up to see it closely.
A sip at the spring before going up to Gavia.
The place of the first nativity scene in history.
A unique nave with three chapels and wooden ceiling inlaid with an eight-pointed star, a pilgrimage destination every 22nd October.
The art of crime in the Town Hall.

In the manor house of the late nineteenth century of the family of owner Massaiu, restored and on three floors: a path on the history of the four judged Sardinians with fortresses, wars and treatises, thematic maps of the Spanish coastal towers and strategic points of defense, photographs of the castles, an area on the peasant life, temporary exhibitions and a multimedia room on the about one hundred castles of Sardinia. From here a cobbled path climbs in a few hundred meters to the castle.

San Giuseppe has a white stone portal richly decorated with a chiaramontana inspiration; the church of the Conception has a palemontano portal with acute arches coming from the church of San Nicolò of the ancient farmhouse of Adragna and sculptures of the eighteenth century.
A stop in the hamlet of the twin bell towers, combined with the museum.
The most beautiful village in Italy, the centre of the Genoese Val Grue, with the Renaissance square of the Doria and the Bella di Garbagna cherries.
Fortified village that was autonomous republic from the 13th to the 15th century, with the 13th century castle and church of San Lorenzo in 1391.
A unique museum of its kind, in a former public slaughterhouse of the late nineteenth century, dedicated to the transformations of the landscape and the relationship between man and nature.

Remains of the lock on the Bruna river wanted by the Republic of Siena in 1462, designed in 1468 and finished in 1481 for the fish culture, considered the oldest brick closed entirely on a river; a flood destroyed it eleven years later. It is partly located in Roccastrada (123 m on the left bank) and partly in Gavorrano.

Frescoed by Sebastiano Taricco, the Sabauda residence where the peace of 1631 was signed, the Shroud was guarded in 1706 and Napoleon dictated the surrender to Vittorio Amedeo III; today it is the seat of art exhibitions.

On a small rock spur between the lagoons of Lesina and Varano, it is already mentioned in acts of Charles II of Anjou; the current structure, with a quadrangular base with a crown of five caditoias, dates back to the middle of the sixteenth century by mandate of the Viceroy Don Pedro of Toledo. It was garrison, telegraphic base for the Tremiti and barracks of the Guardia di Finanza; owned by the municipality, it was restored and opened in 2005 and houses a visitor center of the Park. From the terrace you can see the other coastal towers up to Molise.
The history of Rome in layers.
The village of the Sanctuary Regina Montis Regalis, a Baroque masterpiece with the largest elliptical dome in the world.

The valley, the ancient Transaquana Valley, stretches between woods and mountains of the Apennines on the border with the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, between 850 and over 1600 meters of altitude, with wide views and variety of flora and fauna.
Thermal plant a short distance from the country that uses oligomineral waters bicarbonate- sulphate-calciche.
Scientific disclosure for the whole family.

Built at the end of the sixteenth century and rebuilt inside in the eighteenth century, it has three Renaissance portals in sandstone and inside paintings of masters of the seventeenth century including Claudio Ridolfi and Giuliano Persciutti.

The Chapel of the Scrovegni of the lower Lazio, was built in the fifteenth century at the behest of Cardinal Pedro Fernández de Frías and preserves one of the most important late-Gothic cycles of Lazio, with scenes from the Old and New Testaments; sacristy, bell tower and hermitage were added between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Managed by the Regional Direction Musei Lazio, you can visit it on request through the Pro Loco.
The "granary of the Malatesta" with walls, alleys and squares.
The great wall of Piedmont.

Next to the archaeological area of the Fortress, it is dedicated to the patroness, who lived in the fourteenth century, who chose poverty while coming from a rich family. On the ground floor a fourteenth-century document on a hospital dedicated to her and the only painting that portrays her, from 1734, of the Florentine Baroque painter Bamberini; on the first floor an archaeological path with finds of the lower Valdarno from the Roman era to the Middle Ages. Open by reservation Tuesday and Thursday 9-13, Saturday 10-13.
Six-Seven hundred sacred in the center of the village.

Provisionally housed in two halls of the Municipal Library, it contains gravestones, coats of arms and works of the churches, convents and civil buildings of the Polistena destroyed by the earthquake of February 5, 1783, paintings and sculptures of local artists (including eighteen works by Francesco Jerace), a herbarium, fossil and archaeological finds also protohistoric with funerary furnishings, parchments from 1430 to the end of the eighteenth century, photographs of the late nineteenth-early twentieth century and tools of peasant and craftsman work.
Among the largest belt in the Italian world.
From Pontida Abbey to Pope John's places among the woods and vineyards of Monte Canto.
€5, reduced €3,70, family €10
In the center of the village, inside creates the optical illusion of three naves and preserves lateral altars with original stucco decorations and statues of saints.
MiC card (updated to April 2020) is closed every day, Italia.it open every day 9-sunset
A Gothic wooden sculptural group.

Fossil from Precambrian to Tertiary: a fragment of ancient earth's crust, a marine reptile of about 8 meters, a block with six eggs of dinosaur, great ammonites and the skull of a tiger with saber teeth.
Contemporary art in the house of Masaccio child.
Ogliastra country under the Taccu: the old village abandoned after the flood of 1951, the gorge of the Scala di San Giorgio and, at a thousand meters, the nuragic complex of Serbissi.
On the road of pilgrims.
The classic Bolognese walk, with views of the city and hills on arrival.
A 16th century canvas in the village.
The Doge's Palace overlooks Piazza del Popolo: renovated at the beginning of the 20th century, it preserves the chapel of the Annunziata and a hanging garden built with the reconstruction of 1630.
Opera season in a golden room.
The sanctuary is located in the former Friars Minor Observing complex, restored, and was built on the remains of a Roman villa of the first century.
The walk through the ancient palaces of the village.
A monastery-fortress of the thirteenth century.
Built by the Cajssotti at the end of the first half of the eighteenth century on a design by Juvarra.
The symbol of the High Country.
The Romanesque of the village.

Civic museum founded in 1991 in three buildings of the village with six rooms: the territory and the Tasso, the postal activity of the family, Bernardo and Torquato Tasso, the journey, the signs on letters, epidemics and disinfection, until the transmission of information from the nineteenth century, mail art and philatelia. It has a letter from 1840 freed with Penny Black, the world's first stamp, and a poster horn. Guided tour €3 per person; open from Thursday to Sunday (from April from Wednesday), 10-12.30 and 14.30-18 from March to October, 10-13 and 14-17 from November to February.
Guided visits
Three churches in a short tour of the village.
Grifoni and nature beside the nuraghi.
Open only by reservation (Aniene Turismo), without regular hours
The mountain villa of an emperor.
The Crucifix, which suded in 1738.
Center with two-storey houses in red trachite and murals on the walls depicting carpets and weaving.

Ancient hamlet of Gavardo at the confluence of the stream Vrenda in the Churches, lying on a rather steep slope: along the road towards Quarena you will find houses of medieval origin, and on the side you will find the picturesque nucleus of houses of Casalicolo.

Ring of about 39 km by mountain bike or e-bike (1,200 m in altitude, 365 to 1,560 m) that starts from the parish and rises between castle, mill, orchards, vineyards and chestnut groves, passes a dolmen, the quarry of Balma Oro and the large stone quarry of Luserna di Montoso up to Rucas, and then descend to the chapel of Madonna della Neve. Difficulty BC/BC+, for trained cyclists.

Fortified complex of the XI-XII century, of the Sarriod until 1923 and of the Region since 1970: the chapel has frescoes of the thirteenth century and the 'sala delle teste' a wooden ceiling of the late fifteenth century on 171 shelves carved with monsters and fantastic animals.

Ancient church isolated between woods and fields at the foot of the castle, with next to the cemetery; cited in a bull by Frederick I of 1155. The central nave is Romanesque, the Gothic right with hanging arches, the left behind 1460, the year of St. Christopher painted on the façade; portico of the seventeenth century, apse enlarged at the end of the eighteenth century. The restorations have brought to light late-Gothic frescoes among the best preserved of the Biellese.
Large karst dolina a couple of kilometers from the city, from which come the Neolithic finds exhibited in the diocesan museum.
The village that freed itself of its lords.

It is the first crack of the Spaccata Mountain, to the left of the entrance of the sanctuary: it descends for about 300 steps, secured, up to the reflections of light on the sea; according to legend it was a refuge of pirates. Opened in 2025 after ten years; times indicated by Visit Lazio: Tuesday-Sunday 9-12 and 14:30-17:30, free admission.
Five collections in a building.

Also known as Fortezza Giulia or Rocca Nova, it was wanted by Giulio II, who laid the first stone on 14 December 1508, and completed in 1537 under Paul III, on a structure of imperial age. Bramante worked on the project, then Antonio da Sangallo il Giovane, Michelangelo (since 1535, for a part) and finally Domenico Zanobio (1538-1539), who enlarged the mastium. About 100 × 120 meters, four corner towers of 21 meters in diameter and an octagonal mast over 23 meters high; underwent the Spanish siege of 1527, the attack of Barbarossa in 1544 and the bombings of the Second World War.

In the heart of the village, in Piazza Benedetto Croce, the church of San Martino houses the small altar of San Fedele, celebrated on April 24; not far away Palazzo Croce, residence of the family of Benedetto Croce, and the church of San Vito in Piazza De Thomasis.
Clean sea at the foot of the village.
From prehistoric origins to the castle in a single path.
The President's gift.

Opened in 2000, when Don Nanni (Giovanni) Guiso donated to Orosei the ancient residence of the noble Guiso, then barracks of the Royal Carabinieri, along with his collection: vintage theatres from all over Europe and theatre production from the eighteenth century to today, diorami and graphics of international artists including drawings of the Roman School of 1930-1945, ancient and rare books on Sardinia, dresses and costumes from 1880 to today and works of art from Sienese. From May to September open Monday, Tuesday and Friday 9-13 and Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 17-21; from October to April only by reservation.
From Noasca a route of about 3 hours leads to the royal hunting house of the Gran Piano, restored by the Park. The Gran Piano is a quiet area where you can see chamois and ibex grazing.
Fantoni and Sebastiano Ricci in a large baroque church.
The medieval origins of Montale.
€15, reduced €10 (4-11 years), senior €12
closed from November to March (open April-October), visible from outside
Church of Byzantine times, the only trace left of the ancient farmhouse of Miggiano; next is the Menhir Miggiano, about two meters high.
One of the Italian-Greek monasteries of Cilento.

About 200 m2 with more than 700 fire helmets from all over the world: collection pieces in leather, steel and brass, helmets from Egypt, Thailand, Guatemala and New York, and the French metal helmets, particularly elaborate and often decorated with feathers. Visits from 10 am to 6 pm only by telephone (+39 0474 504117).

The "Città dei Diari" in the upper Tiber Valley has been keeping since 1984 the National Diary Archive designed by Saverio Tutino, told in the Piccolo Museo del Diario at Palazzo Pretorio. Destroyed by the flood of 1855 and the Second World War, the town preserves the Town Hall, the Collegiate Church and the Sanctuary of the Madonna dei Lumi; in the territory the Hermitage of Cerbaiolo, the Lake of Montedoglio and the churches of the hamlets, while from here starts the Via di Francesco dalla Verna in Assisi.

About 4.5 km of concrete tunnels excavated since 1937 by Mussolini as an air raid shelter for the military leaders, disguised as a Breda weapons factory; since September 1943 for about ten months there was the headquarters of the South Command of Field Marshal Kesselring, and in 1967, in NATO, about 1.3 km became an anti-atomic bunker for government and President of the Republic. Recovered by the municipality, it has been a museum since 2003 and is visited as a "Memory Path" with guided tours of about two hours, including military means, radio and maps.
recorded by the MiC as an abandoned cultural heritage; status and accessibility not indicated
Blossoms from winter to autumn, among camellias and hydrangeas.

Medieval church with façade, single nave with wooden trusses and square presbytery with cruising vault, along the Path of the Wandering. The walls are covered by a unitary cycle of frescoes from 1475-1485 with an eschatological theme: the Crucifixion in the presbytery, Christ the Judge on the triumphal arch, the righteous welcomed in Paradise by Peter, Paul and the Virgin and, on the opposite wall, the damned in Hell.
Roman countryside in the city.
The peasant life of the valley in a convent on the old port.

Medieval village with castle and remains of the double walls, 1154 and 1190; the only access is the Porta, with all sixth arch surmounted by a crenellated tower. In the center is the parish church of Santa Maria, before 1400.

Country of the eastern foothills of Friuli at 195 meters, surrounded by the ruins of the upper and lower castles and the fortresses of Partistagno, Zucco and Cucagna; in the former dairy the medieval Archaeological Museum tells the daily life in the feudal castles between the 10th and 15th centuries.
Cumulative Home Christmas, Theatre and Casa Barezzi €11 whole (Ministry of Culture)

Borgo dell'Alta Valle del Tibere on the border with Tuscany, called the terrace of the Alta Valle del Tibere, is a medieval walk along the walls, underground cisterns, the Rocca with the round tower and the church of San Francesco with the Madonna and Child attributed to Donatello.
Spring water and legends of bears.
Can be closed for restoration
Municipality of the lower valley Arroscia, home of the workshop of the painters Guido da Ranzo, with the frescoed church of San Pantaleo and the ruins of the castle above the gorge.
The ancient Piazza d'Arme, with the cathedral and Via Grande, built in the time of Ferdinand I.
You get to the abbey on foot, with the view.
The largest plateau in the Apennines.
Art, faith and uphill panorama.
Romanesque-Sveva church.
Walk through noble palaces and baroque churches.

Ancient maritime republic and center of the Amalfi Coast, UNESCO heritage since 1997: the Cathedral of Sant'Andrea at the top of the stairs, the Cloister of Paradise and, behind the village, the Valley of Ferriere with the ancient paper mills.
Nature a few km from the Tower.
A 15th-century Madonna in the countryside.

From the 13th century, renovated in the 16th century, on Piazza del Plebiscito: it houses two works by Perugino, the Madonna with Saints (1514) and the Baptism of Christ (1510), a wooden Crucifix of the Giambologna school and frescoes by Pomarancio.
The view of the park and the reign of the royal eagle.

One of the Museums of the Food of Parma, set up in the cellars and in the ancient kitchens of the castle. The five-section route starts from the historical testimonies that bind Felino to salami, passes through the kitchens, the pork products and the production in the peasant houses, and ends with the current processing according to the traditional recipe of Salame Felino IGP.
In the high course of the Stilaro river, in the Folea valley: the highest water jump in Calabria and the southern Apennines, reachable by a trip that ends with a bath.
The street of the frescoed arcades.
Ruins on the valley with views from Gran Sasso to the sea.

Palazzo Carotenuto, from the late nineteenth century, was built by Don Ettore d'Alessio, who administered the goods of the princes of Marinis: it is a solid three-storey building with the facade divided into two symmetrical parts by a door, leading to the internal stairs and a back courtyard overlooking a large garden. Palazzo Giugliano also has a symmetrical façade, with two semicircular wings that seem to embrace the large square in front.
Low water and transparent for families.
The civilization of rice in a rural court with five churches.
The history of ancient Satrianum.

Castelseprio preserves the ancient Castrum Sibrium, a late ancient fortress and longobard destroyed by Ottone Visconti in 1287, today a state archaeological park. Castrum and village with the church of Santa Maria foris portas have been part of the UNESCO site since 2011. The places of power (568-774 A.D.)

Cuveglio, a long spiritual center of Valcuvia, preserves in Canonica the bell tower crenellated thirteenth century of the collegiate of San Lorenzo, ancient parish church of the valley; in the hamlet of Cavona there is an unusual museum dedicated to the Far West and the Indo-American civilizations.
A short tour of the Baroque palace and the painter's square.
Sculptures of the twentieth century in the open air.

Founded in 1998 on the banks of the Mincio, in the heart of the Riserva Valli del Mincio, it is set up in a typical fishing house partly recreated and hosts the Mincio Park Visitor Centre. It exhibits objects of everyday life and work in swamps collected by the inhabitants: tools for the cultivation of the marsh cane and of the carice, fishing tools and hunting, tools and domestic furnishings, with a space on flora and fauna of the protected area. Free of charge up to 5 years; open Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday with different times, other days on request.

Ancient parish church of the deceased village of Serzela, dating back to the 13th century and rebuilt in the 17th century; a stone in the country sanctuary recalls the destruction of the nearby village of Uras by pirates led by Barbarossa.
Low parking: the source recommends leaving the car in Praiano (2 km on foot) or using the Amalfi-Agerola bus with stop on the bridge
The tower facade of the baroque ibleo.
The mountain farmsteads of the Mòcheni Valley.
The Lingiardi organ and the Entierro tradition.
The pride of Antrodoco: over 300 head covers and relics of the world and colonial wars, with weapons, uniforms, bombs and a fully equipped base camp.
Lake Bolsena within walking distance.
the MiC card (updated 2021) indicates "closed" every day without timetable; tel. 0575 445302, biblio@civichiana.it

The building of 1559 in Caposeda, restored, which houses the International Atelier of Plastic Arts directed by Maestro Del Negro; in the mid-Twentieth century it was owned by Giovan Battista Meneghini, husband of Maria Callas.
View of Palermo and the gulf.

In the former Pretura, on about 300 m2, it traces the geological eras and the environmental evolution of Calabria with about 15,000 findings from the Paleozoic to the Quaternary collected by Demetrio Lo Giudice and acquired by the Municipality: a deer jaw of about 100,000 years old, skull bones of Pliocene whale found at 750 meters on the Aspromonte, a rib of sirenide from the Lazarus Stone. Open Monday-Friday 8-14, closed Saturday and Sunday.

The defensive tower with square base, about 24-26 meters high with blackbirds and trifore bell cell, is the only rest of the fortress, strengthened by Gonzaga and consolidated in 1844 by engineer Jacopo Martinelli; restored in 1987, houses the museum. The collection was born from the donation of lawyer Fosco Baboni (61 white weapons, 34 firearms) and today exceeds 400 pieces, from the Middle Ages to the Great War, Western and Eastern, in thematic rooms. Open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday 9-12.30.

The center has a heart-shaped plan and alleys called "Trevi"; the municipal path goes from Piazza della Libertà, with the elm symbol of the ancient Ulmeta, to the Ponte dei Corni linked to the legend of the castle Belisario, along Via Roma (covered with garlands of Mayciondolo for Corpus Domini), Piazza Nuova cobbolata and the gardens
The baroque cathedral of the port city.
The Dauni del Tavoliere and the archive of Andrea Patienza.
The historical and religious heart of the city, with the relics of two saints.
Designed for the Italian General Exhibition of 1884, it reproduces fifteenth-century buildings and furnishings of Piedmont and the Aosta Valley.

In an ancient salt plant next to the sixteenth-century Torrione, it collects about a thousand industrial finds (evaporigraphs, scales, scientific instruments, tools for salt collection and processing, samples and containers), copies of letters and documents of Vanvitelli, who designed the work of reclamation, and plastic of the organization of the work; outside working salt pans, machines, railway wagons, locomotives and generators. Unique of its kind in the Central-South.
The crater of the mine of 1916 and a panorama of the Val d'Astico.

A valuable structure of late nineteenth century, huge, with large lounges and a large park, the only green area of Turate according to the FAI; the activity began in 1898 hosting some garibaldini. Today it houses a museum with relics of the Risorgimento, including objects related to Giuseppe Garibaldi, and occasionally hosts events such as classical music concerts. Reported in the FAI census in 2003 , 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022.
Romanesque church of the first half of the thirteenth century with baroque bell tower.

Church and convent were started in 1456 and are among the oldest buildings in the historic center; from the seventeenth century they had various modifications, including the Baroque facade, while the ancient bell tower remained unchanged. The former Dominican monastery now houses the Town House and the Leoncavallo Museum. In the church an altarpiece with Dominican saints of Neapolitan workshop (XVII century) and an eighteenth-century painting of San Domenico resurrecting Napoleon Orsini.
The streets of the center with the characteristic portico of via Zeffirino Re, from the square to the cathedral.

Ring hike of 10 km (3 and a half hours, medium difficulty) from Piazza Garibaldi: Loveno, the Piamuro alpine pasture, the Galli furnace, the Chioderia (former mill and kiosk), the Carliseppi mill, the monolith Sass Corbée, the lime furnace and the village of Barna.
The feudal mansion.
An ancient corner of Rome.
The view on the plateau.

Valley between the territories of Oliena and Dorgali, the most accessible port of Supramonte: limestone crests with dolines, canyons and caves, holm oak woods, terebinth and age-old junipers, where you can meet mouflons and royal eagles. On its dirt paths you will find Sa Sedda 'e sos Carros and the caves of Sa Oche, Su Bentu and Corbeddu.

Borgo founded in 1188 as a defensive cornerstone of Cremona, Castelleone preserves the 12th century Torre Isso, the long Via Roma porticata, the Renaissance parish church of Saints Philip and James and, in the countryside, two Renaissance churches: the Sanctuary of Mercy and Santa Maria in Bressanoro.
Theatre in the medieval centre of Sirolo.

The colorful and painted facades of the center date back to the seventeenth century and testify to the prosperity of the city under the influence of Genoese; they are to be watched looking up as you walk. The route of the Municipality lists 42 stages, including the Collegiate Church, the Castle Tower, the Church of Sant'Andrea, the Oratory of the Disciplined of Santa Maria Maddalena, the Durazzo Palaces, Brignole (of the Customs), Spinola, Balbi and Pallavicini (seat of the Municipality), the Marenco Theatre, Porta Pozzolo and the Pieve of Santa Maria.

Already armory of the fortress of the Noble, lords of the country since 956: after the excommunication of Sixtus IV the main tower was demolished and the armory became a sacred place, elevated to collegiate in 1508 by Cardinal Colonna. The sixteenth-century portal was the entrance of the castle; inside, a single nave with frescoes in starry sky, a baptismal font of the fifteenth century with three carved fishes, an Annunciation attributed to Bartolomeo Torresani and, on the upper floor, the Chapel of the Rosary with portal of 1494 carved with reptiles and scorpions.
The dam that closes the valley.
In the Renaissance Palazzo Odasi, he tells Urbino's soul through history, ideas and identity, inviting him to continue his visit through the streets of the city.
The masks of the Commedia dell'Arte from their creators.
Four millennia of history of the Esaro Valley in a village museum.
Novilara's stalks.

12th century fortified village on the right of the Tenna, at the foot of the Sibilla and Priora mountains in the Sibillini Mountains National Park, with walls, towers and three original gates; in Palazzo Leopardi the Pinacoteca civica Fortunato Duranti, in the territory the Sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Ambro, the parish church of Sant'Angelo in Montespino and the Gole dell'Infernaccio with the hermitage of San Leonardo.
The Liberated Jerusalem painted.

It rises on the area of a Benedictine monastery, was rebuilt by the Barberini in the mid-17th century and assumed the present form with Clement XII around 1730-32. At the entrance there is the statue of St. Peter of Paolo Benaglia (about 1730), a holy waterworks made from an altar and a base of Roman statue, the altarpiece of Giacinto Gimignani of 1633 and, under the altar, the remains of Blessed Margaret Colonna.

The millennial village on the hill overlooking Savio, 7 km south of the city, autonomous municipality until 1926, with remains of the walls, the gate and the castle; it was almost destroyed by the earthquake of 1661. At Christmas it hosts a large human-sized nativity scene.
The city's mother church.
Lucan painting in a church in the center.
18th-century palace in Piazza Roma, next to the town hall, seat of the Fondazione's museum of contemporary art.

Oratory on the calle that descends from the castle, obtained in a tower-door of the Carrara walls (the Porta della Castagnera) and documented since 1544: it preserves the fresco of the Madonna of milk attributed to Giovanni Antonio da Meschio (a little after the half of the fifteenth century), with musical angels added by Francesco Beccaruzzi. Restored by the Alps in 1992; open on Sunday afternoon, other days by reservation.
Dinosaurs and nature for the little ones.
A cave-sanctuary on top of the hill, among fossils and frescoes.

There are still sections of the walls with the perimeter towers and an almost intact ogival arched door, before 1200. In summer, the centre hosts the Artistrada Colmurano Buskers Festival, an international street art festival.

Three megalithic belts of the V, IV and III century B.C.: the inner one about 2 km long, the outer one about 5 meters thick, 6-7 high and 3 km long. It includes a necropolis of more than 1200 graves, the Plinian Fountain, perennial source in a large karst cavity perhaps cited by Pliny in Naturalis Historia, and the small church of St. Peter Mandurino with a frescoed underground crypt.
The 17-step staircase to the sacred water.
Monastery of the thirteenth century, today a private residence, with cloister renovated in the sixteenth century and frescoes of the fourteenth-century school of Giotto in the church.
The system of walls and forts, with one of the longest belts in the world, is explored on foot or by mountain bike; the funicular Zecca's Righi leads to Peralto, leading to the fortifications.
The museum dedicated to mountain and smuggling.

The ancient market square with the arched arcades of the Podestà House and the church commissioned by Federico Borromeo in 1592, attributed to Pellegrino Tibaldi, with a staircase of Francesco Maria Richini.

Between the sources of the Livenza, at the border between Caneva and Polcenigo, it is among the oldest settlements in northern Italy, frequented by the Paleolithic; there were found tools in splintered stone, fragments of ceramics and wooden remains of the huts. It is one of the 19 UNESCO World Heritage sites of prehistoric alpine stilts; many finds are in the Archaeological Museum of Western Friuli.
The underground city of World War II.
The seaside village that resisted pirates.

The name derives from the Greek . ...Fulacterion , fortified village: born as a Byzantine fortification between the 5th and 6th centuries, it preserves the quadrangular plan of the late antique castra with perpendicular streets and central squares, still closed by the walls of the 17th century. In 1351 it was a market village on the Via Francigena, in the feud of Malgrate; in the seventeenth century it passed to the Ariberti of Cremona, which extended it with a wide central street, a square and a palace (the Borgo degli Ariberti) next to the church of Saints Jacopo and Antonio and the convent of the Fatebenefratelli, connected by suspended bridges and arches above the doors. In the ancient core narrow alleys, the Jewish Village and a large market square.
Fortress of the 12th century in the center of the village, municipal seat from the Grand Duchy, with a museum of history and art and the panoramic tower.
Museum and park of sculptures.
Here Mozart held his first concert in Italy in 1769; the dedication recalls the Venetian period.
The bishop's neighborhood.
The futurist decorations of Doctors.

Medieval village at the foot of the Treviso Alps, home to the Brandolini feud, dominated by CastelBrando; between Piazza Roma, the Loggia and the Via dell'Acqua, with the Forest of the Penne Mozze and Rolle among the hills of the UNESCO World Heritage Prosecco.

In Piazza del Popolo, the tower houses the Civic Museum that tells the story of Capena from the fall of the Roman Empire to today; the clock marks the hours to Italian, with a single hand that makes four laps in the twenty-four hours.
The great Franciscan Gothic started around 1240, transformed into a prison by Napoleonic troops and remained so until 1993; the restoration started in 2019 brought to light the frescoes.
Inaugurated in 126 A.D. under Hadrian and brought back to light around 1920, it is reached from the back of the Duomo through the district Triggio.
In Padulle, with the Dosolo case and the bathroom of the Renana Reclamation.

Built from 1757 to 1759 in place of the old fort of San Lorenzo sul Capo di Vado, started by the architect Antonio Federico Flobert and completed by engineer Decotte, who connected him to the fort of Santo Stefano with external walls and underground passages. It was used by Napoleon's French troops during the Alpine War and the first campaign in Italy (1792-1797).
The view of the Balze.
18th century sculpture in the hamlet of Ruginello: two panels carved with skeletons, one with the sickle and the other with the hourglass, on the sides of the entrance of the cemetery.
The hamlet of the blacksmiths on the hill.

Angevin summer residence of the 13th century, rebuilt by Charles III of Bourbon between 1765 and 1790 with English gardens; restored until 2009, from 6 March 2024 it houses the museum with 507 finds from the villas established: murals, marbles, ceramics and bronzes.
Alpine fauna and silence in the heart of the Park.

The main exhibition space of Vico, in a mill of the fourteenth century in the medieval village about 32 meters long: wooden presses, millstone and tools for oil and agricultural work, oil tank, warehouse, stable and a kitchen where the workers fed.
Rock with rock art of the Neolithic period, considered the oldest map of the territory; it is reached on foot from Sapiatti.
The fortress designed by Brunelleschi after the Florentine siege of 1406, with drawbridges, battlements and walkways; in the Palazzo Pretorio the finds of the excavations of Verruca.

Inaugurated in 2004 in the chapel and in two rooms of the former monastery, it exhibits liturgical furnishings and documents of the church of Santa Maria Assunta and of the Municipal Historic Archives: the "Presentation of Mary at the Temple" probably attributed to Luigi Crespi, the wooden choir of the late eighteenth century, silk and gold vestments, the silver monsory of 1663 by Paolo Laurentini, the processional cross of 1664 and the reliquary of the Holy Cross of 1722. The chapel has paintings of 1714-1718.
Caravaggio and Guido Reni.
Baroque, built between 1759 and 1789 on a project by Giovanni Antonio Borgese.

Just north of the village, with a large porch and attached to a former monastery, rises on the remains of a Roman villa: in the sacristy are visible mosaic floors. It houses terracotta figures of artists from the Abruzzi of the sixteenth century.

Set up by the Municipality in the premises of the former Pretura, it tells a tradition that in the early decades of the twentieth century counted about thirty goldsmith shops. It exhibits machinery, moulds and tools of the various phases of processing and jewelry produced in Cervaro between the end of the seventeenth and twentieth centuries, largely donated by families, with filigree works, mold and tunnel, caston rings and the typical rings with two braided hands; in a workshop rebuilt a craftsman shows the phases of the work. Not indicated hours: Inquire at the Municipality.

Parish of Romanesque origin, transformed at the beginning of the sixteenth century, mosaic styles: Baroque inside, Romanesque-modern outside, with Romanesque-Gothic bell tower rebuilt in 1900; side chapels of 1928 and 1950-51 and terracotta façade of the 1950s. It contains a Madonna with Child dated 1520, an Ecce Homo attributed to the Sodoma school, a Saint Anthony Abbot of the late sixteenth century and frescoes of angels and friezes re-emerged in the vault. Open by day.
A 19th-century theater hidden in the town hall.
A church in the medieval village.

The walls in large blocks of stone laid without mortar date back to the IV-III century BC and are covered by an urban trek signposted; of the six doors four are in use. Roman gate, the main entrance, has the sixteenth-century appearance in travertine with brick fallway and the vault frescoed with the city coat of arms.
Rocky detachment of January 19, 2017, probably due to water infiltration: the municipality inhibited access to the rock church; check if it was reopened
The gulf and the archipelago from above.
A stop in the historic center.
Sicilian embroidery and stretches.
The parish church is recognized from afar for the bell tower about 54 meters high, the third highest in the province of Cremona after the Torrazzo and the tower of Casalbuttano.
The Roman ships of the harbor, up close.
The Way of the Cross in the Rock.

Location of the Museum of the Territory of the Arroscia Valley . The faces of the Ubagu , is a route in five sections scattered in the country. The House of the Shepherd reconstructs on two floors a typical house: on the ground floor the stable with tools for cattle and cheese, above the kitchen with central fireplace and the room. The Old Prisons are two cells of the sixteenth century for prisoners awaiting trial of the Court of Pieve di Teco; the Sala di cartography historical exhibits reproductions of maps of the sixteenth-XVIII centuries from the archives of Turin, Genoa and Nice. The route is completed by an ancient forge with original mantle and a naturalistic laboratory with the fauna of the Ligurian Alps. Tel. Common 0183 328713.

It was built in 1874 as the main square of the city and enlarged during the police station of Giuseppe Grimaldi (1919-1920), when the Municipal Palace was built in Art Nouveau style that overlooks it together with the Duomo.
Borgo in the hills in the heart of the Maremma, with the thermal baths of Saturnia and the medieval village of Montemerano in its territory.
1,058 hectares of the extensive hunting estate, the last large planitial forest of the coast, where the deer of the dunes lives protected; three routes from one to three hours.
The rare "Cavallata dei Vizi" is frescoed.

It rises on the ancient Aequa, sung by Silio Italico for its wines, on a flat stretch of the tuff cliff: walled village of Angevin with the Gothic Santissima Annunziata overhanging the sea and the Castle Giusso, mineralogical and archaeological museums, the marines of Equa and Seiano, the scrajou with the sulphuric spring and the Monte Comune overlooking Positano and the gulf.
The artistic pearl of Tagliacozzo.
Medieval stone bridges with donkey back profile, among the olive groves around the village.
A fifteenth century Crucifixion attributed to Zanetto Bugatto.
An open-air trail through the mills.
At the Stelvio Pass, at 2,758 meters, tells the story of the pass: the construction of the road, the Great War, sport, mountaineering and glaciers.
Big yellow bench of the Big Bench Community Project in San Vincenzo di Civenna, overlooking the Lecco branch of the lake.
Public closed area for road access work
According to the municipality the trail is not always practicable in winter; ask for updated information from the competent authorities

Country mentioned already in 1231 as "Luparium" with a name linked to wolves that haunted woods and wilds; in the council hall of the Town Hall is the MACUA, civic museum of contemporary art dedicated to Umbro Apollonio and dedicated to the kinetic art and programmed of the sixties and seventies.

The capital rises on a sunny hill; the church of San Marcello has Romanesque façade and 17th century bell tower. Every September 8th, Santa Celestina, from the main square, launches the ball, a balloon of a 19th century tradition.

Mulattiere go up along the slopes to the places that marked the border between Italy and Austria-Hungary until 1918, with well preserved positions of the First World War; from San Michele and Bondo the paths lead to Tremalzo, towards the valley of Ledro.
The life of the fields of Lomellina, in front of the castle.

It was mentioned already in 1251, it collapsed with the earthquake of 1846 and was immediately rebuilt in a more central position, with simple facade and three naves inside. It preserves a relief in terracotta painted with the Madonna del Soccorso, the eighteenth-century altar of the Crucifix in polychrome marble, a Madonna of the Rosary of the eighteenth century and a San Lorenzo attributed to Luigi Secchi da Pisa.
Airons and swans in the low Modena.

It was already mentioned in a donation of 1085, the current church was built in 1772 with a single nave. It preserves a pulpit in wood carved with golden profiles and five altars in polychrome marble; two neoclassical altars of the mid-19th century preserve paintings of the Venetian Sebastiano Santi, and the fresco of the ceiling by G.B. Canal depicts the Assumption of Mary.

Behind the church of Saints Peter and Paul, the oratory is now a museum: there is the Crucifix on a shaped table of the Sienese Luca di Tommè (about 1360) and there are often works by Francesco Nasini and Sebastiano Folli.
The fish from the Adriatic told by the people who sell it.
A break in the green.

Tower of the 14th century at the other end of the village compared to the eptagonal tower, above the ancient gate of the castle, flanked by a loggia of the 16th century; its bell rings every day alternating with the large sixteenth century.
The carnival mountain painted by a son of the country.

Municipality in two centers, Borgio on the sea and Verezzi 200 meters on the basin of the river Bottasana, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: stone hamlets, the square of the Festival theater and the caves of the Quaternario.
A village of cumbessias that lives only for the party.
The mother church of the village and its bell tower.

In the palaces donated by Mgr. Pietro Faglia in 1776: the Morcellian Library (from the Morcelli legacy of 1817) with about 70,000 volumes, 58 incunabula, manuscripts and parchments, and the Repossi Art Gallery (legato of 1854) with paintings, sculptures, furniture and art objects from the 15th to the 21st century, for thematic itineraries; then gipsoteca, oriental icons and over 800 nativity scenes, many of the 18th century Neapolitan.
The square with the birthplace of the sculptor Italo Griselli and the Marchionneschi, Ridolfi and Guerrini palaces, today town hall.
In the former fish market there are traditional life-size boats and fishermen's tools.

The route in the center touches the monument to the fallen of 1925, the eighteenth-century church of St. Peter the Apostle, the porticos with frescoes from the late nineteenth century by the painter Diotallevi and the monumental school in Liberty style of the early twentieth century. From the village the view covers the gulf of Ancona, the profile of the Conero and the Apennines.
Gardens and water games.

In the hamlet of Santa Lucia (Sancto Lucio in Provencale), where since the 1950s the cultural association Coumboscuro has contributed to the rediscovery of Provencal culture in Italy; the museum presents local traditions and is considered one of the most interesting collections of the Alpine valleys. Every first week of September the village hosts the Roumiage de Setembre, preceded by the crossing of the Alps of the French neighbors.
Romanesque jewelry.
The arena inside the city.
The Bourbon prison on the island opposite.
200,000 shells.
Walk in the landscape of the first flying reptiles.
The Cave of Animals, just restored.
The treasures of the cult of St. Michael.
The place of the memory of the internship in Calabria.
Woods, dolines and a Roman road.
The "roof of the Marches."
The cathedral that gave the name to the modern city.
An easy walk with views of the Fortress.
Founded in 1737, it is the oldest opera house in the world still active.
The theatre wanted by Maria Luigia and inaugurated in 1829, temple of the Verdi opera, with the foyer, the audience and the Parisian chandelier from a ton.
€5 guided tour (Underground Rimini)
The memory of the immigrants of the Soana Valley.
Screws on doors and carved masks.
Renaissance church halfway between the castle and the square, built on a project by Giacomo Della Porta (Parchi Lazio the date to 1580).

Linked to the donation of Frederick II of Aragon to the Cistercians in 1306, it was renovated to three naves in 1774; it houses a painting by Vincenzo Manno of 1819. The week after Easter the feast is held with pilgrimage to torches and the canvas is taken in procession to Partinico, to return to the sanctuary in November.

Palazzo elegante, built in the second half of the 16th century by the brothers Guglielmo and Luigi Vertemate Franchi, rich merchants of Pirus: it is the only building of the family that survived the landslide of 1618. Behind a sober façade, the Renaissance interiors have walls and frescoed vaults with mythological scenes inspired by the Metamorphosis of Ovid, stüe and inlaid ceilings. Around, Italian garden with fish pond and double balustrade exedra, orchard, vineyard, chestnut grove, wine press, wine cellar, stables and glaciers; in summer it hosts outdoor concerts. Guided tours by reservation through the Valchiavenna Tourist Board.
A medieval Carthusian immersed in the Ernic woods.
The viewpoint on the Langhe.
Dinosaurs, whales, and a clairvoyant.
The Byzantines in Abruzzo, inside the castle.
The Postman bay in the volcanic rocks.

Small Roman farm of Sillan age discovered in 1977 and buried by the eruption of 79 A.D.: the fulcrum is the wine cell with 18 dolia underground, capable of up to 10,000 liters of must, with press, porch courtyard, triclino with paintings of III style, barn, cistern and barn. A Bacchus hermitage among the finds. Included in Pompeii+, Pompeii Plus and MyPompeii cards; closed on December 25 and January 1st.

Borgo dei Castelli Romani 26 km from Rome, redesigned between the Six and the eighteenth century for Pope Alessandro VII Chigi by Gian Lorenzo Bernini and collaborators: Piazza di Corte with Palazzo Chigi and the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Assunta, the monumental bridge over the Vallericcia, the Chigi Park and the IGP Porchette Fraschetta.
Fanum Fortunae and painting in one building.
Five-century beech trees on the Tolfa Mountains.
The bathroom in Lake Orta on a Blue Flag beach.
The small capital without car, with wooden houses and stone and narrow streets.
Venetian Rococo in the hills, with Guarana and Bonazza.
The nuns cookie.
The Lucanian city on the mountain.
The Moncalvo and the organ Serassi in the heart of the city.
The 15th-century tower-house dominates Piazza Oscar Molinari; once the seat of the magistrate's courthouse, it now houses the Ecomuseum of Terraces and Lives.
View of the Lunigiana to the sea on clear days.
From the Greek to the Latin rite.
The swamp of the valley floor.
Hunting residence of Cosimo I (1564-1566), with the Medici bridges attributed to Buontalenti, Medici portraits, tapestries and the story of Isabella de' Medici.
A large green lung born on the former industrial areas.
The center of the 19th century Livorno.
Close to the Botanical Garden, it houses the personal library of Professor Guido Chidichimo, his trophies and other materials.
Woods and views of the Gulf of Castellammare.

Established in 1995, it protects on 345 hectares, in nine stations distributed between Lugagnano and other municipalities, the sedimentary outskirts typical of Piacenzano, the geological plan of the Pliocene linked to the clays of Lugagnano.

Church mentioned already in 1181 and rebuilt between 1856 and 1866 on a project by engineer Cesare Costa; it preserves paintings by Adeodato Malatesta, including St. Celestine I of 1873 at the high altar and the figures of St. Louis Gonzaga and St. Anthony Abbot.

In the current layout of 1755, with a single nave, it preserves a painted wooden organ, five stone altars with rococo stuccos, seventeenth-century furnishings and a painting by Santa Margherita penitent; in the 18th century noble coats of arms cloister.

The old town is of medieval origin: in the small Piazza Umberto I there are the old Town Hall and the remains of the Palazzo dei principi Carafa, built between 1272 and 1337. Palazzo Vigna della Corte, from the 17th century, has four corner towers and, according to legend, a secret passage to the castle built by Frederick II, today destroyed.

Residenza di fine 18th century built by the Ceriani family, then by the Fountains and a religious institute that gave it the name of Villa San Giuseppe; today it is of the Municipality and houses the Municipal Library, the Civic Museum and various associations, surrounded by a romantic garden.
Frescoes of Meo da Siena in a castle.

The town of Garfagnana of seven hamlets, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1920 from which only the fifteenth-century cloister was saved; above the capital Corfino, at the foot of the Pania, with the Botanical Garden            .
The nineteenth-century Art Nouveau villa at the foot of Macugnano Hill, the summer residence of the poet Guido Gozzano.
The oldest building in Niscemi.
A hall of the 12th century.
€10 full day, €13 with reservation; reduced €3; €15 with the Garden Bardini (only in ticket office)
Lacco Ameno's postcard.

FVG tourism refers to the Porzûs mountain huts as a national monument linked to the massacre of partisans in 1945: according to the Ministry of Culture 18 men of the Osoppo formation were killed by partisans of the Garibaldi Brigades.
A Renaissance villa frescoed on the Adige, a few steps from Verona.
See closely the Apennine wolf.

It starts in front of the Museo Vivo del Mare di Pioppi and in about 2 km of easy path through woods reaches the waterfall of the Black Grape Well, so called for a nearby vine; from there about 100 minutes walk through woods and ridges lead to Celso. The path has been restored by Legambiente volunteers.
Visitable only by reservation
Founded in 1607 by the Camaldolese Hermits of Monte Corona and completed in 1613 with the church dedicated to San Romualdo; there is still a strict rule that does not allow women to enter.

Fort of the Austrian Quadrilateral built after the First War of Independence in two phases (1853-1859 and 1859-1861), designed for 612 men and 25 cannons; passed to the Kingdom of Italy in 1866, it was fortress until 1918 and ammunition storage until 1998. Well preserved and almost entirely original, exhibits artillery pieces from the sixteenth century to the Korean war; audio guide in three languages.
Information and paths.
The 32-metre sculpture of Arnaldo Pomodoro that dominates the area of Corso del Popolo, symbol of the industrial identity of the city.

Black basalt cliff shaped by the eruptions of Etna and the waves of the Ionian Sea, suitable for baths and snorkeling, along a coast of 12 kilometers between Aci Castello and Aci Trezza; the promenade is recommended for walks at sunset.

Built between 1574 and 1578, perhaps on a project by Galeazzo Alessi, today it is the seat of the Town Hall and preserves a mosaic floor of the third century; in 1685-1687 Taddeo Carlone built two fountains for the garden. It is connected by a balcony to the Pentagonal Tower.
Seen from the cliff.
The tower door.
The Piazza del Duomo.
The Cosmopolis of the Medici from above.

A hilly village about 350 metres away in the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, above the Calore river: medieval historic centre with the remains of Palazzo Carafa, the Museo della Civiltà Contadina in the old Town Hall and a long winemaking tradition.
Where the city took its name.
The seat of the medieval municipality since 1387, houses Roman and medieval finds, sarcophagi, frescoes of the fifteenth century and a prehistoric section from the caves of the Pennavaira valley.
The architecture of the reconstruction of Belice.
The Lombard jewel UNESCO heritage.
The hill church of the gifts of Maria Luigia.

In the municipality, set up in 2008 and rebuilt in 2023: panels, photographs and objects of epoch on fascism and resistance in Stura Valley, in four rooms (Italian army, German armies and ally, Resistance in Stura Valley, Resistance in Valloriate). Open Monday to Friday from 8 am to 1 pm; afternoons and weekends by reservation.
Two country churches built on Nuragic remains: Sant'Antioco rises on a nuraghe, Santu Miali, of the thirteenth century, on a tomb of giants whose large slab is the main altar.
The remains of the first cathedral and the memory of Irpina emigration.

The old town was built at the beginning of the fourteenth century with the castle; the castrum, quoted in 1148, was assigned to Fermo in 1214 by Aldobrandino d'Este. It is accessed by the well-preserved Porta Marina, with a pointed arch and ghibelline blackbirds.
Gothic cathedral that, with the Swabian-Ange fortress, testifies to the medieval past of the city.

Born from the project "Cento artisti per Ruffano" (1997-1999), it conserves over 300 works of contemporary art donated, including paintings, sculptures and graphics by artists such as Goliardo Padova, Luigi Veronesi, Ibrahim Kodra, Walter Lazzaro, Giovanni Conservo and Salvatore Fiume, catalogued by Carlo Franza; since 2008 it is in the former Convent of the Capuchins and hosts thematic exhibitions. Winter time: Mon, Mar, Thu 15.30-19; Wed and Fri 9-12.30 and 15.30-19; Saturday closed. Tel. 0833 1821254.
In Palazzo Pretorio the only public collection of graphics by the sculptor born in Barberino: 79 engravings from 1964-2006 and the polychrome plaster "Girl with wool dress" with an interactive table.
Itinerary in mountain bike signposted by Feel Florence up to the ancient mountain village of Lozzole, in the Apennines above Palazzuolo.

Restored in 1817 by Giuseppe Valadier, it has a portico of six Doric columns that holds a terrace with six Ionic columns and a tympanum carved by Thorvaldsen; near the Horti Torlonia and the Archaeological Park of Ibernesi, which preserves ruins of the Villa of Domitian.
The Duke of Rivoli who welcomes those who enter the Commune.
Founded in 2005 in the former thermal power station of Officine Lancia, a rationalist industrial building.
Twenty kilometers of sea from the Savoy stands.

In Vedronza (326 m) the torrent forms natural springs and pools; here stood the hydroelectric power plant of Arturo Malignani, built in 1906-1907, abandoned in 1968 and demolished after the earthquake of 1976.
Medieval village on three hills between Pisa and Florence, stop of the Via Francigena and capital of the white truffle.

Borgo della Val Gandino, in Valle Seriana, with the Basilica of Santa Maria Assunta, one of the most famous Baroque monuments of Bergamasca, the museum that preserves its treasures together with nativity scenes and fabrics, the Palazzo del Vicar portico and, at altitude, the paths of Monte Farno.

A route of about two kilometers follows the original path of the Appia with the Roman basolate, crossing the gorge of Sant'Andrea between Roman supporting walls in square and polygonal work and the remains of a Bourbon fortification, the Fort of Sant'Andrea.
Titian in Venice.

Castle in isolated position in the countryside of the village, square plan with concentric shorts and a high tower with loggia that had military function of sighting. Purchased in 1973 by the founders of the Oasis, it is still part of it: from the castle you can access the wildlife park.
The alpine postcard lake under the Mangart.

Necropolis of 22 domus de Janas excavated in a limestone bank not far from the town, in the Nurra, built by the recent Neolithic (3200-2800 BC) and used until the ancient Bronze Age (16th century BC), less than six kilometers from the altar of Monte d'Accoddi. Since 2025 it is one of the 17 Sardinian necropolis inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage.
The saint of lovers, in Barbagia.
Late-Gothic chapel built in 1513, with two sixteenth-century sundials on the outer wall.

Tomb excavated in the rock of the recent Neolithic (4th millennium BC), with four rooms decorated; a cell has a false door surmounted by Taurine horns.
The history of the first mountain guides in Piedmont.

Fountain of about 1850 at the entrance of the village, with three mouths and apotropaic masks representing Odio, Love and Oblio; an epigraph attributed to Mgr. Giovanni Andrea Serrao celebrates the water of Caprifico brought to the village at the expense of the citizens, another in Latin by Domenico Cordopatri invites the matrons to rejoice at the feasts of Caprifico.

In a mill of the community of the sixteenth century, remained in operation until the 1930s, on the outskirts of the village along the Via Francigena; the original water wheels, moved by the nearby stream Bagnone, are still in place. Founded in 1977 by the Cultural Association Manfredo Giuliani, it exhibits three millstones of different stones (a sandstone for chestnuts, blue stone for corn, basalt for wheat), objects of chestnut processing, breeding, cheese, fishing and handicrafts, amulets of fertility, the "Raganelle" of the Holy Week, cradles in beech including the famous cradle of Bratto, a rebuilt Lunigiana cuisine and a large frame.
The ceiling was decorated in 1684 by an unknown Spanish painter with over one hundred paintings.

Austera Mother Church of the village, dedicated to St. Peter the Apostle, in the historic center.

13th century castle with two towers at opposite angles: the Mastio, to protect the Fortress Savelli, and a watchtower on the Tiber valley. In its former stables and granaries is the Museum of the River.
€20 full (from 1 February 2026); €26 with Bargello in 48 hours; €38 for all 5 museums in the group in 72 hours
The Tasso prison.

The fifth century basilica where Dante's funeral took place in 1321; from the window under the altar you can see the crypt of the tenth century with the mosaic floor submerged by water, among the goldfishes.
The castle of the lords of Quart.

15th century castle, the only surviving part of the ancient defenses of the village, with square mast and angular cylindrical towers of the Aragonese era. It belongs to the Sanseverino and recently restored, it preserves the original structure with two watchtowers and the guard body; inside a museum with interactive classrooms, educational and multimedia and a conference room.
site not guarded; the municipal road of access is disconnected and passable with off-road

Trekking of medium difficulty (8 km, about 3.30 hours, 1,373 m of climb) that starts a little upstream of the village, where the private traffic ends (about 703 m): crosses the forest, passes just below Sant'Antonio di Alino and runs along the pastures up to the mountain hut Vaccaro, managed by the Parrese Hiking Group; from the refuge to the summit about one hour, with a challenging climb and a wide view. Recommended in spring and summer.
Rest of the medieval village built around the church and the castle away from the sea, with a slender arch over the stream.
The most iconic Baroque square.
Walk along the canal that leads to the sea.
The two bronze horses of Alessandro and Ranuccio Farnese, masterpieces of the baroque statue of the Tuscan sculptor Francesco Mochi (1580-1654).
The wildest valley in the Olympic mountains.
The romantic garden with peacocks, a stone's throw from the sea.
The city of salt: salt salt, salt stores, salt mines, pine forests and the beaches of Milano Marittima, Pinarella and Tagliata.

The eighteenth-century residence of the Vidua counts, probably on a medieval structure, in the highest point of the historic center overlooking the ancient piazza d'armi (today piazza Australia); purchased by the Municipality in 1996 and restored. The south façade is marked by loggias; the rooms preserve frescoes, in part by Antonio Ivaldi called the Muto, including the Chinese room with scenes from the East. It hosts the permanent journey of Carlo Vidua, Count of Conzano, traveler and collector, curated with the Academy of Sciences of Turin. Information to the Municipality (tel. 0142 925132).
Visit her during the liturgy in Gregorian chant.
The highest castle above Finalborgo, currently closed to the public.
Guided tours for a fee: rates on Bologna Welcome
Place of execution of the Martyrs of Belfiore (1851-1855), with the stone and the monument in their memory and the gardens designed by Giuseppe Roda.
The paths above the sea.
The Panaro on foot or by bike.
The oldest building in the village.

In a building of an ancient rural settlement in the upper part of Torriana, on the slopes of Monte Bracco, exhibits objects from the peasant and artisan world, with exhibitions on the cultivation of chestnut and vine and on the production of wine.
Three Caravaggios in a church.
The ancient barn became the church of the Arts, with the external niches and, on the upper floor, the original statues of Donatello, Ghiberti and Verrocchio.

In the Palazzo dei Provveditori Veneti designed by Andrea Palladio: Roman collections, early Christians, early medievals, Romanesques and Gothics, with lapidary, epigraphic and music sections and a collection of 56 Lombard gold coins.

Belvedere on the left of Palazzo Lanfranchi on the Civita and Sasso Caveoso, named after Giovanni Pascoli, who began teaching in Matera; there is the ... Goccia , bronze sculpture of Kengiro Azuma, more than three meters high.
The medieval fortress that gives its name to the village, reachable from the palace with a covered walkway; one of the most interesting examples of medieval Umbrian military architecture.

In the countryside west of Riese, it is the oldest church in the area, in the eighteenth-century form desired by the architect Ottavio Scotti; it preserves paintings from the sixteenth to the twentieth century, including a Sant'Eurosia by Noè Bordignon. The legend ties him to an apparition of the Virgin to a shepherd threatened by wolves; between church and bell tower remain fragments of the plaque of Lucio Vilonio, Quattuorviro of the Asolo municipality.
The villages of half coast overlooking the valley.
The starting point for the Tremiti.

Etruscan city along the Via Clodia, bloomed between the end of the IV and the middle of the II century BC: facade tombs dug in the cliff on two or three orders, such as the Tomb of the Three Heads, the Prostila, the Tombs Smurinas and the famous Tombs in Temple on the ditch of the Acqualta; on the plateau the medieval remains of the parish church of St. Peter, a castle and a tower, and the stretch of Via Clodia cut into the tuff at Cava Buia.

On Monte San Nicolao, above Velva, remain the ruins of a Roman hospital active throughout the Middle Ages, which welcomed pilgrims and travelers on the Romea road between Liguria, Emilia and Lunigiana until the fire of 1590. It is still readable the cross plan of the XII-XIII centuries, with three semicircular apses in the horizontal arm and a small church annexed; the site is the object of excavations and archaeological studies.

On the Riviera del Brenta, between Padua and Venice, Mira line up along the Naviglio dozens of Venetian villas: the Palladian Villa Foscari called La Malcontenta, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the eighteenth-century Villa Widmann Rezzonico Foscari with the park and carriages, Villa Contarini dei Leoni seat of the Town Hall, the boats of Villa Valmarana, the village of Mira Porte and the churches of Oriago and Gambarare.
Early Christian art under the city.
The residence of the Marquises of Barolo.
The Sardinian handicrafts in one collection.

In the reserve there are about one hundred waterfalls, up to 100 meters high: the Rupe, near rare prehistoric ferns, and the Salice are reached with a trail of 1.1 km (about 2 hours and a half, difficulty E); the Inferno Waterfall, whose name comes from the belief that the pool arrives to hell, is on a 600 meters route for experienced hikers, with 4 km of off-road access.

At 3.244 meters is the highest peak of the area of Cortina and the third of the Dolomites; the cable car Areccia nel Cielo climbs up to the top, to the panoramic terrace over the entire basin of Ampezzo, particularly beautiful at sunrise and sunset. The Tofane massif offers about 47 km of slopes in winter and hiking and mountain biking trails in summer.
The castle of bishops-accounts.

Romanesque church that recent studies date shortly after the year 1000, enlarged in the presbytery in the eighteenth century and recently restored to bring it back to the original style: today it is a building collected and simple. The eighteenth-century altarpiece depicts the Madonna del Carmine with two Carmelite saints and the Saints Cosma and Damiano; raised to the Sanctuary on September 26, 2006, each year it hosts a conference on health issues. Visits from Monday to Saturday by reservation, Mass on Sunday at 10:00.

On the granite plateau of Selene, almost 1,000 meters in a wood of holm oaks, chestnuts and oaks about 6 km from the village: remains the base of the nuraghe Gennacili, surrounded by about 200 huts and defensive walls, with two tombs of giants about 80 meters from each other and sacred sources. The smaller Tomb I has central stele and exedra with seat and chamber of about 7 meters of the fifteenth century BC; the Tomb II, about 12 by 5 meters, had a crowning pyramid trunk with three holes for the betiles (XIV-XII century BC). Picnic area; time indicated by MiC: summer 10-13 and 16-20, winter 10-13 and 15-sunset, closed on Mondays.
Blossoms and views to the sea.
A book illustrated in the open air, to be searched also at the top and in the andrones.
The walls and the view of the olive trees.

Educational farm and museum dedicated to the ocarines and whistles in terracotta, the result of a trade that the family has been carrying out for about a hundred years; it attracts hundreds of visitors every year, who with guided tour can follow the phases of clay processing and participate in the construction of an ocarina.

On Monte Calamita, in the Tuscan Archipelago National Park, the mining activity lasted over 3000 years and was suspended in 1981. The mines of the Ginevro and Vallone, the oldest, are the only underground of the island, with about 7 km of tunnels, and are indicated as the largest magnetite deposit in Europe. They are visited with guided tours.
The parish and the old tower.
Next to the house Maison Saluard, commissioned in the mid-Fifteenth century by the notary Saluard with a cycle of frescoes by Giacomino d'Ivrea recently restored.
Strozzi and Sacchi in the Franciscan monastery.
A historical library.
The two peaks that dominate the valley, the Perduca Stone (659 m) and the Parcellara Stone (836 m), formed by ophiolitic rocks called the "rocks of the devil."

The village is almost perched at the apex of the Upper Arroscia Valley, in the Regional Nature Park of the Ligurian Alps, linked to the shepherding and Ligurian capital of the white cuisine of transhumance; it offers the museum of the civilization of the pastures, the frescoed church of Santa Margherita, the sanctuary of the Madonna dei Colombi and the waterfalls of the Arroscia.
Milan yesterday.
The museum that explains why Spina was here.

The birthplace of Padre Pio, mentioned in the documents since 1133: the house where he was born in 1887, the convent of the Capuchins with the museum, the churches of St. Anne and St. Mary of the Angels and, little to the north, the place of the first stigmata; every year in December the nativity scene.

Many itineraries start from Bisegna: an easy route of about 1 km to Fonte Cerasa (about 30 minutes), a route of about 10 km to Macchia di Rose-Terraegna (about 4 hours) and a challenging one of about 20 km to Pescasseroli, in the heart of the Park, in over 5 and a half hours.

About 600 hectares towards Crispiano and Massafra, reached crossing south of Martina a landscape of red earth, with the richest evergreen formations of the Murge and numerous wild orchids; in the nearby district Specchia Tarantina the Cave of the Nine Housedde, 42 meters deep with limestone concretions, and Masseria Russoli a conservation center of the Donkey of Martina Franca.
A small ex-sixteenth-century vote at the entrance of the country.
15th century frescoes.

Sauze d'Oulx is part of the Milky Way, an eight-station area with 212 slopes and 69 lifts, suitable for skiers of all levels. In summer flowering meadows, itineraries on the ridges between Val di Susa and Val Chisone, bike park and summer ski lifts.
€5 (book of the Reserve), free up to 5 years

At the hamlet of Configno, owned by the Betturri family since 1610 and oasis open to the public since 2005: a trail of about 3 km with local guide crosses the Sacred Wood of chestnuts, beech and oaks, climbs 140 steps to the square of the Three Mothers and passes through the lake in the shape of a heart and the Source of the Ories, between 22 deers and 12 deer on 18 hectares.

The medieval Porta Torre is what remains of the castle of San Genesio; from here the streets branch out to checkerboard, a sign of the role of the village as a defensive outpost in the Gonzaghescan age. Beyond the door opens Piazza Matteotti with the neoclassical Town Hall designed by the architect G.B. Vergani.
The Mantua art of the early twentieth century in a sixteenth century villa.

In Piazza Mingori, the statue of a Russian soldier linked to the film The comrade Don Camillo and a replacement of Don Camillo's tank and Mr Peppone; the locomotive of the films is in the park dedicated to Guareschi.

From the village a path marked naturalistic, speleological and archaeological climbs towards the valleys Pennavaira and Ferraia, passing next to the ruins of the castle and reaching the caves ('arme') that have returned finds from prehistory to the Iron Age. The castle, on the hill of San Giacomo behind the village, is a bound asset that the Province attributes to the Marquises of Clavesana and indicates in bad state of conservation.
The cave bear and the Apennine nature.
Walk through stone portals and solar clocks.
The traces of the medieval castle in the heart of the village.
Built in 1442 in Gothic style in Laste and declared a national monument.
Sacred place about 3 km from the town, which over the centuries has attracted religious and noble. It is surrounded by a park suitable for relaxation and sport.

The heart is Piazza Fontana, among railing houses, Liberty buildings and gardens. Villa Frua, built in the mid-eighteenth century by the Tinelli family and then by the De Angeli Frua family, hosted Garibaldi in 1862 and is now home to the Municipality and the library; its park, known as a botanical park, is open to the public with a view of the lake and the islands.
