In front of the seventeenth-century Villa Tinelli with Italian garden and medieval towers; in the streets near Casa Terruggia and Casa Milanesi (XVIII century), the eighteenth-century church of the Immaculate and Sant'Ambrogio; in the Park of the Remembrances the monument to the fallen of Piero Portaluppi (1923).

One of the most impressive and best preserved defensive systems of Salento, built on an earlier angioin fortress designed by the architect Evangelista Menga, at the service of Charles V. Renaissance portal with decorations, Renaissance balconies, the chapel of San Marco frescoed by the Mannerist Gianserio Strafella and the chapel of Santa Maria Maddalena; Isabella di Chiaromonte was born there in the fifteenth century, then queen of Naples. It adheres to the "Cassio" project for accessibility, with tactile aids, subtitled videos and facilitated texts.
A fortified city of the Brettii in the spot.
To know the sources that gave the name to the country.
Medieval treasures and nativity scenes.
access on request (tel. 0942 744950)
A walk in the shade.

Church-Crypt of Greek rite rose around the thousand under the current Via Don Minzoni, abandoned in the fifteenth century, found by chance in 1929; three apsed aisles with stone iconostasis partly collapsed. The detached frescoes are in the museum, while since 1999 the crypt houses copies of fireproof polystyrene in the original positions. You go down with a metal staircase from the side of the Doge's Palace.
Mandatory for groups only (PinBoBooking app)
The Phoenician-Punic traces of Sulcis.
The symbol of Tesero.
Green area in the center of the village, close to the historic core, along the banks of the Acheron river, whose spring waters fed the mills and the local silk.
Norman tower and crypt in the Salento countryside.

Opened on May 9, 2009 in the house where Giorgione painted the Fregio delle Arti liberali e meccanici, the only fresco attributed to him, next to the Duomo that houses the Pala; it collects about 100 original pieces of the time, from the civic collection or from the antique market, and architectural reconstructions. Open Mar-Jo 10-13, Friday 10-18; closed Monday, Christmas, January 1st and Easter.
opening to be arranged by telephone according to the Metropolitan City
In the Renaissance Palazzo Cusani, with its porticoed courtyard and monument to Hercules and Anteo, a multimedia museum over four centuries of opera in music in Parma.
Caves, cave bears and a prehistoric technique.
Walk among the olive trees over the Greek city.

The town's flagship is defined by the municipality: park with rare plants and centuries-old trees, driveways among flowers, three water tanks with the swans' house and a children's playground; inside there is the ethno-anthropological museum.
Founded in 1543-44 by Luca Ghini, it is the first botanical garden in the world: three hectares with plants from all over the world, secular trees and a herbarium of over 300,000 specimens.

Ancient copper and silver mining centre at the foot of the Poggio di Montieri (1051 m), in the park of the Metallifere Hills, with a small well-preserved historical centre between walls, tower houses of the fourteenth century and the cassero. In the territory the church of San Giacomo, the archaeological site of the Canonica di San Niccolò, the Castle of Fosini, the Red Roses of Boccheggiano and the Garden of the Sounds of Paul Fuchs.
The central square of the city, surrounded by historical buildings including the Palazzo del Comune.

Country at the entrance of the Aurina Valley, in the Dolomiti Plan de Corones region, with the Romanesque church, the ruins of Kehlburg and the castle of Neuhaus linked to Ezra Pound; at Villa Ottone a museum with over 700 fire helmets from all over the world and above the village, from Montassilone, the panoramic ridge towards the Riesi Mountains.
One of the mother parishes of Carnia, with medieval frescoes.
The art of Serrastretta's stuffed chairs.
The village under the village.
Churches in the rock.

Porta Maggiore, part of the Palazzo Conti complex, is the monumental entrance to the historic centre, already access to the ancient Signia. The Scrabble Bridge is an arch of the mid-twentieth century in blocks of tuff, resting on two pillars, one anchored to the polygonal walls and the other incorporated into a house; the legend wants a young Carthaginian to give a scarab to a girl of Segni as a pledge of love.
in some stretches the road has no protection; bring a torch to the tunnels
The noble palaces of Piazza del Duomo with entirely frescoed facades, among the most beautiful examples of the painted palaces of Trento.
In the castle, the seventeenth-century paintings by Paolo Finoglio dedicated to the ...Jerusalem Liberata.
A rare Central European Pietà.

Born from the collaboration between Archeoclub d'Italia, Municipality and Ente Parco Nazionale del Gargano, it is located in the eighteenth-century Palazzo Paolicelli, public building of the historical center restored with funds of the Park and renamed "Palazzo della cultura" (Palace of Culture), opened in March 2010. It exhibits palaeontological and medieval finds; on the whole also the municipal library, the historical archive, a media library on Frederick II and a thematic museum on the Middle Ages and the Emperor.
The traces of the castle from which the village was born.
The most famous blue light in Italy.
Church of 1447 with octagonal plan, with frescoes by Simone de Magistris of 1576.
The works of Giuseppe Augusto Levis, a painter appreciated by Vittorio Emanuele III, and Carlo Sismonda; openings for events and groups.
From the tower of the Thousand to the dwelling of wine.

Easy path of 3 km (about an hour and a half) from Piazza Navarro: cross the Iannello stream, go down to the communal wash basins and follow the signs to the river Lao, crossed on a wooden bridge, with a view on a rocky spur. On the Lao you can raft between gorges and canyons.

Path that starts from the castle and goes down to the Dora; along the route you will find the Forra della Rocca, where the hydraulic works of reclamation of the canavesan marsh are supposed to have occurred.

Recent structure in the southern part of the country, established by the Municipality, the Park and the Community Montana Termino-Cervialto to protect the environment and study the animal and plant species of the Regional Park of the Picentini Mountains.
In the ancient palace of the city Senate, exhibition space dedicated to Don Luigi Sturzo, with a large tile panel on the victory of Iudica over the Arabs.
A wild gorge with a mill.
Tuscia Theatre.

Born as a defensive Longobard settlement on a rocky summit, the village develops in a pyramid along the hill: the entire historic center, well preserved, is an urban park of stone houses and portals decorated with family coats of arms along the alleys, animated by artisan workshops. At Christmas the torchlight illuminates the village with Roman torches like a living crib.

The first church was built in 1121, in Norman age, dedicated to Saint Mary Assunta and Saints Peter and Paul; restored several times, it has the chapel of the patron Saint Vitalian of 1309 with the relics, bronze doors and a bell tower of about 42 meters with the statue of the Assunta. Inside is a Madonna of the Angels of Messinese school and a Madonna with 16th century Child by Antonello Gagini.
within the military range: free beach accessible only from early July to September, from Foceverde (VisitLatium)

11th-XII century tower in large square blocks of local stone, which guarded access to the mineral deposits and to the passages at altitude. The 14th century castle Priacini remains the tower of the Lavanderio, perhaps even older.
The tradition of Umbrian embroidery in four hundred pieces.
The fossils of the Anthracotherium and the nature of the Bregonze.

Large 18th-century Baroque mountain residence above Mareta, without fortifications and still of the Sternbach family, built on the game of numbers: 365 windows, 52 doors, 12 fireplaces and 4 portals. Since 1996 it houses the hunting and fishing museum (part of the ethnographic museum of Teodone) with dioramas of fauna and fish, popular art and a collection of fly fishing; on the second floor the rooms preserved in their original appearance, with tapestries, show the noble life of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. A thematic path of about 1 km, accessible by strollers, climbs from the village to the castle.
One of the largest views of Piceno.
Oriented on the Ligurian southern side.
The villages of the Monferrato farmer.
The medieval castle around which the city was born, with walk on the walls.
The Macachi furnace.
Mantegna's masterpiece.

Opened in 2002 in the former sixteenth-century town hall, it exhibits the excavations of the Roman city of Pitinum Mergens, probably born with the assignments of the Lex Flaminia (232 BC) and the construction of the Flaminia and destroyed in the sixth century during the Gothic war; there are also exposed the remains of the Roman rustic villa of Colombara (II century BC) and a section of contemporary art.
The life of the lagoon fishermen.

First mentioned in 1520 but with elements suggesting the XII-XIII century, of Romanesque-Gothic inspiration with an elaborate rose window; inside capitals with medieval motifs, the triptych of the main altar and sculptures of St. George (1559).
The neighborhood of terraced white houses along narrow alleys, born from the caves of shepherds dug into the rock.
Mar-dom and holidays 9-19, Monday closed. Last entry 30 min before

Along the river Milo grows the Woodwardia radicans, a rare giant fern bulbifera of tertiary origin, a living foxyle with fronds up to 3 meters; in Calabria it was identified in 1985 by the biologist Libero Sibio and Polia there are about 900 specimens, the highest number in Italy.

Hill north of the centre with the oldest traces of human presence, of Picena age: there was found a necropolis of the IX-VII BC centuries, and around the X-XI century there stood the medieval castle of Castel Franco.

The centre of the Alta Murgia was built, according to the Municipality, near the Roman state Â Ad PinumÂ on the Via Appia: the former bauxite mines in the National Park, the nineteenth-century railway viaduct of the 21 arches, the Mother Church of San Pietro near the ruins of the castle and the fourteenth-century church of the Annunziata.
Reclamation plant inaugurated in 1934, known for its modernist and futuristic forms.
€5, both museums €7, families €10

Village on Lake Bracciano, on a cliff of leukic lava at the bottom of a small gulf, with the medieval center dominated by the ruins of the Rocca degli Orsini, the tree-lined lake promenade and the Etruscan-Roman civic museum with the furnishings of the tombs of the Olivetello; around the Regional Natural Park of Bracciano-Martignano.

Roman city excavated since 1952: you can visit the Forum, the altar of the goddess Feronia, the basilica, the Augusteum, the spas of Menandro, a late-republican domus, a small amphitheatre and the baths of the Via Capanate. Between the end of the 4th and the beginning of the 5th century A.D. the city was abandoned and used as a quarry of precious materials. Open Tuesday-Saturday from 8.30 to one hour before sunset; Sunday only the first and third of the month.

In Bardino Nuovo, probably the most recent of the parishes of the territory: erected between 1681 and 1708, parish since 19 November 1797 and completely renovated in 1924, has a richly frescoed interior and the highest bell tower of the valley, over 30 meters. From the front square opens a wide view of the valley and the Ligurian sea.

From the Maddalena a centuries-old paved mule track rises to Ramats, with a windmill, the chapel of Sant'Andrea, consort ovens, terraces and \'barme \', shelter under rock. In the square of the hamlet of Sant'Antonio, the parish church of the Immaculate Conception, mentioned since 1586, blessed in 1698 and with bell tower of 1888, which houses a sixteenth-century retablo of the Melezet carving school. From Ramats trails to the White Chapel, a panoramic point, and the Gran Pertus, hydraulic work of 1533.
View of the square from above.
The castle of Gardone Sopra remains traces, including a chapel dedicated to San Michele, archangel dear to the Longobards.
The French national church was completed in 1589 with the three paintings of Caravaggio on the life of St. Matthew (1599-1602).
The dolls of the first Italian factory and the Lombard painting of the nineteenth century.
A neolithic hut rebuilt in the heart of the UNESCO site.
The first church was built in 1587-1588 to better accommodate an image of the Virgin of Mercy painted on a newsstand that stood on the spot.

Inaugurated on July 28, 2023 next to the municipal park Giovanni Minozzi, in the Brignano Room, as the provisional seat of the civic museum: exhibits more than fifty works including paintings, sculptures, furnishings and sacred objects recovered and restored after the earthquake. In the connected area of Taste you can see the pipe organ of 1777 by Adriano Fedri Fedeli from the church of Santa Maria del Suffragio, a Renaissance wooden pulpit from the church of San Francesco and the canvas of the Eternal Benedict already at Cola Filotesio, restored with the Art Bonus for the Earthquake.
A Franciscan monastery with a mission museum.
€15 whole; €10 from 18 to 25 years; free under 18
The cloister of the convent of San Domenico in the district of Villanova, the subject of guided visits by the Ministry of Culture and the University of Cagliari.
A neo-Gothic-Moorish castle of the 1920s.

The complex was born after the demolition of the walls at the end of the eighteenth century, with Italian garden and a nineteenth-century park of botanical interest; next to the civic tower, the only surviving of the sects of 1526.
Medieval alleys and canvas by Francesco Vanni.

The village extends on a high hill above the sea; its streets, like the Viale delle Palme, are crowded with colorful shops selling plates, vases, heads of Moors, pine cones, majolica, jars and bùmmuli, with decorated lava stone inlays, decorated fountains and walls covered with majolica tiles. In artisan workshops you can still see the Matrangela, a figure born from the traditional Stefano ceramic and handmade with techniques handed down for centuries.
Inside the historical factory of 1936: the history Ducati and the bikes of the victories. Upon reservation you can add the factory tour.
The most famous of the villas of delight of Senago, linked to Borromeo.
As the Dolomites have become a holiday destination.
damaged by the earthquake 2016: technical insights in progress and provisional works installed (Region Marche, September 2025)

Next to the waterfall, surrounded by vegetation, on the right bank of Tagliamento there is a cave work of the Vallo Alpino del Littorio of the 1940s; the fort has been restored and you can visit with guided tours on weekends.

The oldest nucleus, probably of the 10th century, with the palaces of the main owners, the Archbishop's Farm that housed the town hall and looks at the sea and the hills, the church of Sant'Ilario, the parish with a wooden crucifix of the fourteenth century and a Madonna delle Grazie of the fifteenth century, well preserved towers and the cistern.
A unique Robbiano group in a country parish.
An easy walk along the water, from Kneipp to the mill.

The Roman port brought to light by the excavations of 1998-2001, with the Captain's House of the 13th century, the only medieval building survived the bombings of 1943, and sections of walls of the 2nd century B.C.
You enter a living dwelling, not a gallery.
The panoramic summit of the plateau.
The beach and the pier for the island.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione is 873 metres in the Mastallone valley, in the Parco dell'Alta Valsesia, home of the prick and Vincenzo Lancia.

Country of Chietino at the foot of Monte Pallano, overlooking the artificial lake created by barring the Sangro with a dam on earth; home of Silvio Spaventa, remembered by the bronze monument of the main square, houses the Sanctuary of San Mauro Abbot, a destination of pilgrims for centuries, and an ethnographic museum on rural life.
Transhumant pastors and painters of the Grand Tour in one museum.

Among the oldest churches in Valcamonica, dating back to the time of Charlemagne; in the sixteenth century it was used as a lazzaretto. It contains frescoes, including St. Martin on horseback that divides the mantle with the poor.
In front of the basilica, in the medieval square among olive trees, vegetable gardens and small houses.
€4 full, €3 reduced; single ticket with the Civic Museum €10

Market town at the crossroads of the Isarco, Ridanna and Vizze valleys, on the Brenner road, at its peak in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries: the Tower of the Twelve divides the Old City from the New Portico City, with the Gothic Town Hall, the parish church of Our Lady of the Swamp and the Multscher Museum in the Command of the Teutonic Order.

Set up in 1991 by the Alpine Group of Caoria, it exhibits Italian and Austro-Hungarian uniforms, weapons, equipment and personal objects of soldiers found on the field or donated by the inhabitants, with vintage photos on the life at the front and in the rear, and also tells the suffering of civilians. Open from 28 June to 13 September every day 15:30-18:30; admission included in the Trentino Guest Card.
The sources do not indicate whether the villa and the park can be visited
14th century frescoes along the road.
Neoclassical parish church with a single nave, erected in the 18th century on a project by architect Mattia Capponi.
Camaldolese church of the thirteenth century.

Maritime villa of the 1st century BC, remodeled by Tiberius that included the natural cave as a nymph; excavated at the end of the fifties, it also includes a fish pond and a spa and extended for over 300 meters along the east beach. The area closes in case of bad weather and is not accessible to people with reduced mobility.

Forra in the Raganello Gorges Nature Reserve, in the Pollino National Park, rich in biodiversity, with habitats for large raptors and rare plants; a naturalistic path follows them, with walls that recall the Dante's bolges.
The second bay of the city, linked to Hans Christian Andersen, who often stayed in Sestri Levante; in late spring there is the festival for children dedicated to him.
MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates the museum closed every day (tel. 0833 539391)

On the hill behind the historic centre, it is a pilgrimage destination and a sign of the link between Liguria and the Czech Republic. Born from the convent of the Scalzi Carmelites of Genoa: in 1888 Father Leopold of St. Joseph (Beccaro) chose Arenzano for a house of formation of young people dedicated to St. Teresa of Jesus.
The women's convent on the course.
The remains of the columns of the ancient church of Santa Maria del Buon Consiglio, among the monuments of interest in the historic center near the castle.
The church on Ceres temple.
At about 1400 meters, overlooking Mont Blanc and Grivola.

On the way to the Passo di Gavia, it is one of the oldest churches in the upper Camonica Valley: the foundation is assumed around the year 1000. In the apse frescoes of the fourteenth century with Christ blessed surrounded by the symbols of the evangelists.
Nature and sea in the Park of the Flegrei Camps.

Village of Sabina in the Tiber Valley, 66 km from Rome, with its medieval core surrounded by fourteenth-century walls: the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the Sabino Diocesan Museum, the thirteenth-century church of São Paulo and the chimney of the Glassworks Fajella.
Also in Villa Guerrazzi, it collects the tools of the peasant work of the northern Maremma.

The eighteenth-century villa was founded as a "Casino di Delizie" by the Marquis Accoretti and transformed in the following century by the Carradori, on the road from San Biagio to Filottrano: Italian gardens, a greenery of symmetrical cypresses, hunting forest with stakeout towers, greenhouses and groves.

Heart of the village with the Palazzocchio, home to an archive of the sixteenth century, and Palazzo Giannantonio, of late seventeenth century, now town hall; near, the Pomegranate Terrace is a small square on two levels with arches and murals of flowers and pomegranate fruits.

In the south-eastern sector of Sila, towards the Gulf of Squillace, the regional reserve has deep gorges and holes formed by the erosion of conglomerates and sandstones, which italia.it indicates as part of one of the largest canyons in Europe; the vegetation crosses the bands of Lauretum, Castanetum and Fagetum, and Monte Raga emerge pink granite banks. The trail of the river and the canyon is 1.3 km long (about 2 hours round trip, 190 m of altitude difference, tourist difficulty).

Built around 891-898 at the behest of Queen Ageltrude, wife of Emperor Guido of Spoleto; in 1443 it was sacked and set on fire by Ciarpellone, captain of Francesco Sforza, and the monastery was destroyed. There are still presbytery and crypt: the three sandstone apses retain the original characteristics, inside the frescoes of Sant'Amico that enshrine the wolf and the Madonna enthroned with the Child.
The fourteenth-century town hall in L with the coats of arms of the vicars, the prisons and a fresco of justice attributed to Antonio di Anghiari.

It collects the finds of the ancient Azetium peucezia from the Neolithic to the Early Middle Ages, with the collections donated Colamusi, Diogguardi, Didonna and Catamo: accessories of the necropolis of Azezius and Purgatory (over 400 tombs between VII century BC and XI AD), a dolmenic tomb of about 3500 BC and traces of the Byzantine and Longobard settlement of Sant'Apollinare.
The village of the castle and legend of Hannibal.

The historic centre was born around this ancient grassy transhumance road, which crosses the village and runs on foot or on horseback through hills, cultivated fields and woods, up to the area of Santa Maria dei Vignali.
On the hill of the medieval village, the working tools of the peasants, the domestic furnishings and the tools of the craftsmen: a frame, a lathe, a mantle, a machine for brooms.
From prehistory to modern times in a single palace.

Castle of medieval origin on a hill of red jasper, first residence of the Landi and in Bourbon era military garrison, several times renovated. You can visit the old manor with stone beaches, the walk of the ring with the angular towers, the square of arms, the salon, the underground glacier and the Bastion of the artillery wanted in the fifteenth century by Manfredo Landi the Magnificent, recently restored; inside also the Ferrarini-Nicoli collection, with about sixty paintings and sixteen sculptures of blind authors of the early twentieth century.
The Etruscan streets.

The place of memory is located on the watershed between Valli di Lanzo and Val di Susa, in the old cantoniere house of Colle del Lys: on the ground floor the reception, on the first floor the photographic exhibition on the partisans of the 17th Brigade Garibaldi .Felice Cima , which here had its base from 1943 to 1945; the exhibition revolves around the idea of resilience, human and natural. It is also a visitor centre of the Colle del Lys Natural Park and the starting point of the Tel. 011 9532286.
The complement to the visit of the Cathedral.
Engravings and medals.
The tower over the tuff.
A fifteenth-century castle that can be visited in every room.
A Young Palm in a hill parish.
The main square of the historic center, dedicated to the judge of Arborea.
The village born from the escape from Blanda, with views.

Country of Sannio at the foot of the Taburno-Camposauro, with a center of churches and palaces six-seventh-century linked to the Dukes Ceva Grimaldi: the Doge's Palace, the parish church of San Mauro, the food and wine museum in Palazzo Cutillo and, on the Monte delle Rose, the sanctuary of Maria SS. del Roseto.
The first meeting with the island.
Recognized quality museum by the Region: prepares for the visit of the salt.
The cloister next to the church of Santo Stefano, stop of the route in the historic center.
The Motor Valley before Ferrari and Maserati.
The story of who left.
Mountain trails full of history, just a step from the Val di Susa.
Church of the 11th century in the village; in the churches of the Aniene valley the faces of the women of Anticoli still appear, becoming models very requested by the painters.
The Renaissance square of the Sforza.

It is 18 meters high and dates back to the first half of the XV century, it is what remains of the medieval palace of the castle and is the symbol of the village; it houses three bells dated 1613, 1797 and 1811.
One of the great Romanesque masterpieces of Abruzzo.
Lambrette, Vespa and the daily life of the last century.

Established in 2008, it protects submerged archaeological finds and protected species such as the needlefish, the shellfish Tonna galea and two species of seahorses (Hippocampus hippocampus and Hippocampus guttulus), from which the name of "Baia dell'Hippocampo" is named; the horse is an indicator of environmental quality.
The cathedral of the historic center, between the stages of the tour of the Palladian city together with the Basilica and the Olympic Theatre.
Small, perfect, quiet.

Mother church of the diocese, a few steps from the Bollente, with the main portal carved at the end of the fifteenth century by Giovanni Antonio Pilacorte; inside the Triptych of the Madonna of Montserrat by Bartolomé Bermejo.

Villa purchased by the Municipality in 1998: sections from archaeology (from the sixth millennium BC) to the Middle Ages, with the bull of Frederick II with the gold seal and sandals of St. Francis, the Renaissance section with the works of Lorenzo Lotto, the nineteenth century Leopardian and modern art.
From the medieval gate to the Roman bridge.
MiC card indicates the closed tower every day, times to check

Natural monument formed by two pillars of dark volcanic rock in the south of the island, symbol of Carloforte: 16 meters high each, after the tides of November 2013 of one remains only the base. Around crags, caves and mouth of an inactive geyser.

Built by the Orsini between 1470 and 1490 on a nucleus with a tower of the 12th century of the Prefects of Vico, it passed to the Odescalchi in 1696 and is open to the public since 1952 by the will of Prince Livio IV Odescalchi. The rooms conserve fifteenth-century frescoes from the workshop of Antoniazzo Romano, the Papal Chamber with frescoes attributed to the Zuccari brothers, antique weapons, furnishings and a collection of Italian majolica especially of the sixteenth century, with the busts of the twelve Caesars and a rare hourglass of the sixteenth century; the walk along the cylindrical towers looks on the lake. Reduced €6 (6-12 years, disabled, law enforcement; over 65 only on Tuesdays); visits not bookable, ticket office closed one hour before.

Founded in 1896 after the chance discovery of the necropolis of Baldaria, on the initiative of the municipal secretary Cesare Gardellini, since 1991 it has been located in the late nineteenth century palace of the former Monte di Pietà. Three rooms tell the left Adige from the Neolithic to the Lombard age: the inhabitants of the Bronze Age of Santa Giustina di Baldaria and Sabbionara di Veronella, the necropolis of the Iron Age of Baldaria (IX-VI century BC), amphorae and Roman inscriptions and late antique funerary furnishings, including a mutilate statue of Emperor Magnenzio. Free admission, with Italian, English, German and French cards.
An octagonal church with works by Andrea de Magistris.
In the former convent the immersive route "Tempio del Brunello" dedicated to wine and the history of the territory.

Country of Val Rendena at the entrance of the Val Genova, in the Adamello Brenta Nature Park: on the cliff above the Sarca, the church of Santo Stefano with the Dance Macabra and the Charlemagne dei Baschenis, lower on the Antica Vetreria nineteenth century, and above the village the medieval hermitage of San Martino.
Two thousand years of maritime trade told by the finds of the backdrops.

Amphitheatre beach under the walls of Capo Bianco, a white limestone cliff about 75 meters high; the mud of the head offers to the bathers natural treatments outdoors. In the village under the archaeological area tourist facilities and a camping in the shade of a forest of eucalyptuses.
The panoramic road on the high coast of Cilento.
Unique river in Europe for the biodiversity of its branches; the pebble beaches become beaches to rest and points for the canoe, and in its waters you raise the trout, the queen of San Daniele.
The Marquis' theater.

It preserves the triptych signed in 1506 .Zuane Antonius de' Sacchis resident in Spilimbergo, rediscovered in 1909 by the parish priest Fr. Giuseppe Bertoni and considered the first sure work of the Pordenone: St. Michael who tramples Satan between the Saints Valeriano and Giovanni Battista. Damaged by the 1976 earthquake, it has been restored.
Medieval village of the Langhe del Barbaresco, among the most beautiful villages in Italy and Orange Flag, with houses with red roofs close around the Clock Tower.
Porticos and Gothic capitals.
The biodiversity of the Trentino woods, to measure of child.
Palace in front of the Duomo, seat of the Civic Library and the City Centre of Culture.
italia.it the inaccessible sign for the earthquake of 2009
In the locality Campicino, it has seven monumental baroque altars and paintings including a 17th century Deposition of the Roman Caravaggio school and a Madonna with Child of the 16th century.
The parish of the eighteenth century.
On foot or by bike along the Lanza to Switzerland.
The oldest Doric stone temple in Sicily.
The parish church of the pilgrims of Francigena.

The Carnic Alps are one of the hardest climbs in Europe and one of the most feared stages of the Giro d'Italia. In summer you can climb by bike or on foot, in winter there are 23 km of slopes served by 11 lifts up to 1,970 meters, snowshoeing and snowshoeing.

Ethnographic collection of Mocchie set up in a museum form, presented by the historian Luca Patria: it tells the material culture of the mountain community of the valley of Grave, with a special attention to dairy production and alpine life, but also to mining activities, weaving, mills and other protoindustrial structures. Not indicated hours: information to the Municipality (tel. 011 9643102).

Southeast Sicilian coastal resort known for its sandy beaches, clear sea and marina with connections to Malta and the Aeolian Islands; in the historic center the fifteenth-century Cabrera Tower, symbol of the city, and the sixteenth-century Villa Tedeschi, now a municipal library.
A castle still inhabited, with the vintage railway model.
The island of silence.
The place of the apparition under the oak.
The noble halls of the town hall.

The capital of the Langhe, the city of the hundred towers and the white truffle, the heart of the UNESCO wine landscape: the cathedral, the medieval towers, San Domenico, the Maddalena di Vittone and Alba underground.
The paths of smugglers.
The costume and traditions of Sardinia.
In winter it is a ski area of 50 km of slopes
The 14th-century castle that hosted Julius II.
The castle on the water that tells the Upper Garda.
A miniature castle with a view of the valley.
From prehistory to the city of the two seas.
The ticket can include some Etruscan tombs, upon reservation.
Walk on the Roman basolate to the woods.
The ruins on the cliff.

Sandy beach and pebbles, last stretch of coast free before the mining compendium, with clear seabeds and the Gemini islands reachable by swimming; it is served by the MareBus. The legend of the two lovers Lorenzo and Maria is remembered every July 14 with a historical reenactment.
Monastery with adjoining church built in 1616, with frescoed vaults and 17th century paintings.
The ancient Romanesque abbey a few kilometers from the castle, on the route of the Via Francigena, a traditional place for pilgrims to stop.
Ticket €10 whole, €5 from 18 to 25 years; free up to 18 years
The Swabian fortress of Catania.

A watchtower built around 1559 at the expense of the University of Scilla, part of the defensive system of the Strait, on the cliffs overhanging between Cannitello and Scilla; the name derives from the Latin Caput valleys. In the most recent era it served to spot the swordfish; it was several times in the census "The Places of the Heart" of the FAI. The Metropolitan City points to it as ruin.
A break in the green with a picnic at the lake.
Quote visits, to be booked through the Archaeological Museum of Sarteano

Monastery of the eighteenth century in a natural wood of oaks on Monte Cammarata, next to the cave where Santa Rosalia took refuge for twelve years after refusing the wedding in Palermo; it preserves an epigraph in Latin of the saint. It is the starting point of the Itinerarium Rosaliae, the path to the Sanctuary of Monte Pellegrino.

The University Museum of Earth Sciences, heir to the eighteenth-century collections of the Museum of Extense Natural History, with the name "Gemma 1786" since 2005; path without architectural barriers and captions in Braille.
Benedictine monastery of the 12th century just outside the village; the small Romanesque church has a medieval fresco on the façade.

Part of the Archaeological and Environmental Park of Orvieto, in a wooded area north-west of the village in the valley of Paglia: small chamber graves dug into the rock, preceded by a dromos, mostly the second half of the 6th century BC, dug in 1986. The intact tombs have returned orvieto painted ceramics, buccheri and metal objects, including an Etruscan bronze mirror engraved with mythological scenes. Info: tel. 0763 361010.
The crypt of the 36 columns.

One of the best examples of medieval architecture in the Val Trompia, in the area of the cemetery just before the village climbing the valley: hut church with slender stone bell tower, wooden portal of the fourteenth century and frescoed exterior walls, and inside paintings from the late Middle Ages to the full Renaissance, including rare fourteenth century frescoes. Outside, the chapel of San Rocco with portico and frescoes of saints; the oratory of San Domenico preserves a cycle of the half fifteenth century attributed to the Cremonese workshop of Bembo, called "Cappella Sistina della Valle Trompia."
Free walk; paid spa
Purchased by private individuals in 1869; the source does not indicate how to visit (Common 0975 865211)
16th century residence built around 1575 by Count Ottavio Trento, with Palladian-inspired façade; next to it is the Colombian tower, the only rest of a previous Benedictine rural complex.
The Farfense church of the miraculous Crucifix.

Valico at 2481 meters, one of the most challenging climbs faced by the Giro d'Italia, where stands the monument dedicated to the cyclist Marco Pantani; around the high valley pastures where Castelmagno DOP is produced.
A country church with ancient re-use columns.
Raised along the sea, with palaces that preserve the traces of the Jewish community, rare case in Puglia.
Industrial archaeology in motion.
Alleys and coats of arms above the Aniene valley.

Tobbiana is the highest center of the municipality and starting point for excursions to the surrounding peaks; the church of San Michele Arcangelo, of the eighteenth century, offers a beautiful view over the territory.

Quadrangular fortress with four bulwarks and 5 meters thick walls, built between 1501 and 1503 by Antonio da Sangallo at the behest of Cesare Borgia, to defend from the sea of Neptune, It was the Colonna until 1594, then the Apostolic Chamber and since 1831 the Borghese; in 1925 the convention between Italy and Yugoslavia on the Italians of Dalmatia was signed. Today it is municipal and hosts the Museum of Landing, the Antiquarium and exhibitions.

Built between 1629 and 1696 at the highest point in the historic centre, it is the most representative Baroque monument in the city, a minor basilica since 1946. It is so rich in paintings that it is considered a picture gallery: paintings by Giovanni Andrea Coppola (Martyrdom of Sant'Agata, Adoration of the Magi, Assunta) and Nicola Malinconico, choir and wooden pulpit by Giorgio Aver.
The Palace of the Rangoons with decorated atrium, courtyard, staircase and balcony, which in 1564 hosted Torquato Tasso; near, the permanent exhibition of sixteenth-century dresses Gold threads.
The medieval heart of the village, overlooking the valley.
The Ostuni Woman's cave among the olive trees.
The crucifix of the plague of 1656.

On the Kolovrat plateau, along the border with Slovenia, the positions of the third Italian defensive line of the First World War, linked to the defeat of Caporetto: trenches clearly visible at the Zagradan Pass (1042 m), positions on Mount Klabuk restored by the Poti miru v Posočju Foundation, remains of machine gun nests and military buildings on Mount Piatto. It starts from Passo Solarie, where at 50 meters stands the cyppo alpino Riccardo Di Giusto, the first Italian fallen of the Great War, following the path CAI 746; on the return you can turn to Clabuzzaro and San Volfango, with the large memorial on the site of a former military cemetery.
A five-thousand-year-old high-rise altar.

The medieval nucleus has a semicircle shape with its backs to the mountain, on the path of the ancient walls: via Lantieri with shops and architectural remains, via Scaletta that goes down to the lake, the alley Aie with the portico building that was a town hall until the eighteenth century and the civic tower of via Paris of the twelfth century.

From Barzio climbs the historic cable car to the Piani di Bobbio, renowned for winter sports; the name comes from the abbey of Bobbio (Piacenza), of which they were alpine pastures. In summer hiking rings between 1,800 and 2,000 meters around the Campelli and towards Artavaggio, easy (2h30-3h30) or challenging as the Path of the Roads with equipped stretches.

Born from the collection started by Aldo Cibaldi in the fifties and became civic at the end of the sixties, it conserves about 8,000 drawings of children and children from 3 to 14 years coming from 79 countries, exposed in rotation, with multimedia places to consult the works catalogued; it also welcomes digital works. It is located in the fifteenth-century church of the Disciplines, which preserves a fresco of the sixteenth century. Open Friday and Saturday 14-17, the other days by appointment; barrier-free.

The original church of 1601, surrounded by the cemetery and with the frescoed apse, was enlarged between 1629 and 1850 with a chapel of the Madonna; the current building with three naves with polygonal apse was designed by Mgr. Angelo Noacco was built between 1889 and 1921.
The artist's studio of the painted country.
A rock and its legend.

The pearl of Lario is on the tip of the promontory where Lake Como is divided into its branches: the historic centre with steps with the Romanesque San Giacomo, the parks of Villa Melzi and Villa Serbelloni and the hamlets overlooking the water like San Giovanni, with the Museum of instruments for navigation, and the ancient fishing village of Pescallo.

Birthplace of the Venerable Brother Theodoreto (baptized John Andrew, 1871-1954), of the Brothers of the Christian Schools, founder in 1913 of the Union of the Catechists of the SS. Crucifix and promoter of the House of Charity Arts and Crafts; transformed into a museum by Brother Carlo Torchio, it preserves furnishings and tools of an ancient country house. It is managed by the Association of SS Catechists. Crucifix; information to the church of San Marco, tel. 0141 950125.
The great prospect of water.
The miners' light.
The Cistercian monastery.
The citrus fruits of the lake.

Ruins about 950 meters in the thick of the forest, reachable from Pontenano following the channel of Capraia. Founded between 950 and 961 by the hermits Peter and Eriprando, it was the first Benedictine monastery of the Casentino; it had the greatest splendor between XI and XII century, passed to the Vallombrosani and at the end of the seventeenth century was in ruins. There remains the large semicircular apse with monophora and the sandstone fence that divided the classroom.
The sixteenth-century church of the low district.
The first Christian communities of Agro Veientano.
The picture gallery of the Gazzola Institute, among the places of culture listed by the Municipality.
The history of Italian oil in a former wash-house.
The thirteenth-century rose.

Castle on a sandstone hill at 520 m, perhaps of Norman origin, rebuilt in the fifteenth century with quadrangular belt and three cylindrical crenellated towers; the Catalan-Aragonese portal bears the coat of arms Carafa della Spina, Di Sangro and Monforte and a dragon with upside down lilies, symbol of the betrayal to the Angioini. You can visit the six-arched loggia, the courtyard with well and cistern, the noble rooms with painting decorations, stables and barn, towers and round paths; national monument since 1979, from 2023 houses a nucleus of contemporary art with works by William Congdon, Gino Marotta and Titina Maselli. Open from Tuesday to Sunday (closed on Mondays), tickets also through the official app.

Camaldolese hermits founded around 980 by a group of hermits on the slopes of Mount Catria, about 700 m above sea level, linked to the spirituality of St. Romualdo; St. Pier Damiani guided its development. Dante quotes him in the 21st canto of Paradise and perhaps stayed there after 1310. You can visit cloisters, Romanesque church, historical library, scriptorium and ancient cells of monks; it houses retreats, concerts and guided tours. Times indicated: every day 10-12 and 15-17:30.
A small staircase in the center of Busto.

Medieval village on a karst plateau at the foot of Monte Altuino, with arches of the ancient gates, double windows, bell tower and a watchtower. In the square of the church of Santa Maria Assunta are concentrated the medieval remains, with the tower that is believed to mark the oldest nucleus, today reduced to two sides. The village, called Ponza, was renamed Arcinazzo Romano in 1891 so as not to confuse it with the island.
It reconstructs the domestic life of the past, when each family weaves the hemp; in the exhibition you see the hand-crafted fabric.
View from Montecassino to the sea.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione della Valle Vigezzo, land of chimney sweeps, perfumers and painters, where the Cologne Water was born.
Ancient rock engravings along a mountain path.
Along the street of the village.
MiC card indicates the museum closed every day; times to check
An underground stop on the way back.
The myth of the 500 told by his fans.
Giò Pomodoro's tribute to Gramsci.
A wine villa buried by Vesuvius in the 5th century.
De Ferrari's fresco.
A 14th-century cloister in town hall.
The villa where Bellini composed his works.
A place of worship dug into the rock.
the MiC card (updated to January 2021) indicates closed every day; the Park warns that after the earthquake 2016 some areas are forbidden
Wooden roofs, murals and masks of the Fonnese carnival.
On the trail of the cardinal born in Roata Chiusani.

The origins date back to the beginning of the fourteenth century, coeve to Maso Curio; transformed into a noble palace by the Bertelli, it was for centuries the center of the political and social power of the country. It preserves the ancient façade, an austere androne, the monumental staircase, a stucco room, a room with wooden ceiling, the chapel of the accounts and the portal of Marcantonio.
The small Phoenix where Goldoni discovered the theatre.
The water village that flows through the houses.
The large mural painted in 1989 by Keith Haring with some students on the wall of the church of St. Anthony the Abbot: thirty figures dancing for peace.
Temporaryly closed for maintenance according to the Municipality (page updated in November 2023) and closed according to Let's Marche
Baroque in the square.

Wanted by Giulia Farnese to venerate the Immaculate Conception and built in 1522 (inscription on the portal) instead of a smaller chapel, of which Gothic mullioned windows remain. Façade with a bezel portal, rose window and a small asymmetrical bell tower; inside the single nave with a trussed roof, three Renaissance windows on the side and an apse with paintings dated 1581, attributed to students of the brothers Zuccari; the restoration started in 2006 brought to light frescoes waiting for restoration. Today it is the municipality and hosts exhibitions and conferences; the tradition wants the remains of Giulia Farnese to be hidden.

Built in 1835 by Giovanni Antonio de Manzoni, whose family had been enriched with the mines of Agordino, designed by Giuseppe Jappelli, the architect of Caffè Pedrocchi in Padua. Neoclassical and sober, with four giant parasts on the façade, it contains frescoes by Giovanni De Min (The fight of the Spartans) and Pietro Paoletti (Esop) and, in the tower, Egyptian views and a ceiling with the constellations of the zodiac; in 1870 Giuseppe Segusini added the neo-Gothic rustic wing. From the Province since 1977, it has been managed since 2014 by Pro Loco di Sedico for concerts, projections and exhibitions.
the MiC card (updated to 2020) indicates the museum closed daily; contact the Municipality
The village of Arbëreshë with a view of the sunsets.

Late medieval complex that guarded the Via del Passo Giovo: only the original mast, built in the middle of the thirteenth century by the lords of Passiria as a residential tower remains. The five-storey tower, restored and detached seat of the MuseumPasseier since 2003, houses small exhibitions on the castle, the Schildhöfe farms, the lords of Passiria and the counts Fuchs, Renaissance paintings of 1538 by Bartlme Dill Riemenschneider on the fourth floor and on top the view up to Merano; below, the late Dogotic church of Santa Croce with frescoes of about 1550. Open on Monday 10-13 from June to September; from the village bridge about 30 minutes walk.
The pope's house at Rerum Novarum.
The ancient Elbe on the shore of the port.
In October the chestnut festival.
A medieval village with artist mosaics in the walls.
The great church that gave the name to the village.
In the Medici Arsenals seven Roman ships from the third century BC to the VII AD, found since 1998 near San Rossore, with about 800 exhibits, visits and workshops for families.

Built at the end of the eighteenth century in a classical style on an older church, of which two chapels remain (in one was found a statue of St Elizabeth of Hungary); it houses a sumptuous altar in polychrome marble.
The peasant civilization of Monte Bracco.
Near the fortress, it has a portal of Roman origin and frescoes of the early sixteenth century.
Following the cardinal who ruled France.
The Oltradige style is a walk through vineyards and mansions.

Palazzo del Cinquecento with the statue of Sisto V del Sansovino above the entrance: it houses the Pinacoteca, with the Stories of Saint Lucia of Iacobello del Fiore and the Adoration of the Shepherds of Rubens (1608), and the archaeological section "From Villanoviani to Piceni."

Born on October 5, 1980 in the rooms of the castle, the Pro Loco group collects objects of use, tools, machines and tools of the traditional Piedmontese peasant and craftsmanship from the 17th to the 20th century, distributed in about twenty rebuilt workshops. Midweek visits and in the morning by reservation for groups of at least 15 people; Monday closed.
The nymph port.
You walk behind a 32-metre waterfall in 15 minutes.
The partisan memory of the valley in a small exhibition.
From the castle to the river on foot.
The Franciscan monastery of the accounts of Arc.
The Lodron fortress overlooking Lake Idro.
Agricultural equipment of the past.
Medieval irrigation channel from which you can see the village from above.
Butcheries where you choose meat (bumbette, sausages, gnummeredde, braciole) and they are roasted at the moment; Cisternino is considered the undisputed capital of the cookers of the Valle d'Itria.

Dogliani is in the heart of the Langhe, among the hills of sandy yellow soils cultivated with sweet, native vine attested already in the sixteenth century; here in 1897 the twenty-three-year-old Luigi Einaudi bought the farm San Giacomo with a vineyard. Seven routes of different lengths and difficulties cross the territory; the map of the trails costs € 4 at the information office, in the accommodation facilities and in the bars.
One of the gates of the walls.
Large lawn with a stone stele in the center reminiscent of the Synod of 1532, with which the Waldenses joined the European Protestant Reformation.

Impressive neo-Gothic church built between 1851 and 1862 on a project and under the direction of the Galliate architect Don Ercole Marietti, in place of the sixteenth-century parish. Three naves with dome on the central and eight side chapels; it preserves a canvas of Cuzzio with Saints Peter and Paul and a Saint Anthony of Padua by Bartolomeo Vandoni. Open every day from 8:00 to 6:00.

From Piazza Regina Margherita a walk follows the streets of the village and the old walks of the medieval walls; along the route the church of Sant'Anna preserves an artistic funerary stele of the prince of Salm Salm.
A walled village on the side of the Soratte.
The bell tower of 52 meters below the Mount of Ascension.
In the heart of the historic centre, it is worth visiting for its elegant interior structure richly decorated and for the season of shows.

Designed by Giordano Riccati, a contemporary and friend of Francesco Maria Preti, in the same period as Villa Spineda, has the facade dominated by a large pronao. The interior with a single nave is marked by semi-colons, among which are placed six large canvases of the Venetian school.
Beach and mining archaeology in a limestone fjord.

The Romanesque cathedral dedicated to the patron saint, built from 1212 at the behest of Bishop Federico Vanga, where the solemn sessions of the Council of Trento were held; it houses the tomb of St. Vigilio.
The civilization of oil.

On the hills north-east of Caserta, Castel Morrone preserves the ruins of the Norman castle on the top of the mountain, the polygonal belt of Monte Castellone-Gagliola and the seventeenth-century Sanctuary of Monte Castello, next to the monument to Pilade Bronzetti and the garibaldini fallen in October 1860.

At 1,280 m on the slopes of Mount Cimone, between pastures and firs, 748 crosses on several levels of fallen on the front of the Highlands, with many Hungarian and Bosnian names; next stood the military hospital of the Knights of Malta, and the chapel on the north side was rebuilt in 1954 and restored in 1992. From Bertoldi about 1.5 km, then 300 m walk.

On the edge of the walls of the historic center, the fortress of Pisa of the thirteenth century was demolished and rebuilt between 1487 and 1494 at the behest of Lorenzo the Magnificent (architects Giuliano da Sangallo, Francione and Luca del Caprina); it passed to the Banco di San Giorgio in 1496 and to the Republic of Genoa from 1562 to 1797, then it was barracks and prison until the seventies. Restored between 1985 and 2003, it hosts exhibitions, the Festival of Mind and the National Antique Exhibition; since 2016 the MUdeF, multimedia museum of the Lunigiana fortresses in 27 rooms. Guests can visit the piazza d'armi, towers, the walk of a roundabout, tunnels and underground galleries; Tuesday-Sunday 10-13 and 16-19, Monday closed.
The hill that tells the medieval issue of Calanna.
Parish of the fifteenth century with paintings by Anton Maria Panico and Orazio Gentileschi.
A 16th century watchman on the sea.

Ruins of the ancient municipal mill along the Coumbassa, near the Eiretto: on the next rock are engraved the dates of the millers, the oldest of 1770. It is located on the round of the Gardetta, which also touches easy climbing boulders.

Reserve of 2.939 hectares established in 1997, about 330 meters in the southern part of the plateau: it protects the most important relic of cork mixed with holm oak of central Sicily, which with the Bosco of Santo Pietro di Caltagirone is what remains of the largest cork grove of central-southern Sicily. Between corks, holm oaks, thorny oaks, cysts, heathers, myrtle and arbutus live wild cat and istrice, buzzard, ghetto, eschulapius columbra and leopardin columbra.

Hiking trails recovered by the Volunteers Group Hiking trails between rocky palm groves, aye and erotic boulders used as hermitage: Vignàle Peter and Paul of Agri, passing through the wash-house of Canale and the excavations of Scifi, the path Force of Agrico Taormina and the path towards Fondaco Prete, to the sea.
The widespread nativity scene of an alpine village.
A work by the sculptor of the monument of Castelfidardo.
The balcony above Cordevole.
The instruments and sounds of Piedmontese tradition.
A miniature Venetian living room.
The view of Etna from the churchyard.
A baroque 17th century building with 18th century paintings and a fresco of the Virgin attributed to Jerome of John; in front of it stands the birthplace of Filippo Marchetti.
The palace wanted by Prince Ippolito Bentivoglio and built by Aleotti together with the square, with the noble halls and the theatre.
The sun and moon portal.
The Byzantine and rural Salento.
The ship hull ceiling, unique in Calabria.

Inaugurated in June 2004, it documents the site of the Magdalene from the recent Neolithic period (end of the fifth millennium BC) to the second Iron Age (IV century BC), with the findings of the excavations; it also exhibits paintings of the landscape landscaper G.A. Levis (1873-1926), pupil of Delleani and mayor of the village at the beginning of the twentieth century. Guided visits and workshops with archaeologists upon reservation.
Prehistoric caves in a wild gorge.

Founded in 1987 by Bruno Caristo to enhance local and emerging artists, he collects painting, sculpture and photography by Calabrian authors, with modern and vintage reproductions in the photographic section; he has a photo library and a teaching room.

In a 19th-century rural building on two floors of the Barons Mazza complex, renovated as a museum, exhibits the excavations from prehistoric to Middle Ages: everyday objects, valuable artifacts, statues and monumental portraits. Unique ticket with the park.

Cittadina della Riviera di Levante in the eastern part of the Promontory of Portofino, in the heart of the Gulf of Tigullio, about 35 km from Genoa: a seaside village with marinas and fishing boats, the sixteenth-century castle on the promenade, Villa Durazzo with its seventeenth-century park, the abbey of Cervara overlooking the sea and the bay of Paraggi towards Portofino.
A thousand-year-old castle with a 19th-century park.

The seventeenth-century Town Hall was born as a Jesuit college: from the windows near the entrance there are Greek ruins of 400 BC and inside there is a life-size reproduction of the triptych. Next to it, the Jesuit church of San Girolamo has an octagonal tower with lantern, a Baroque stone portal and a plaque of 1872 with metric equivalences of the ancient local measures.

At the Duomo, of medieval foundation and already home to the Confraternity of the Battuti: above the door the dates 1300 (construction), 1446 and 1618 (restauri) and 1902; enlarged in 1693, it has eighteenth-century facade. Behind the tower of the dead is the old cemetery.
To understand how the Tuscan landscape was born.

Church enlarged by the Franciscans in the thirteenth century, with Gothic portal and bell tower obtained from a tower of defense; the interior frescoes are of Giotto school and include the Procession of the Whites painted by Cola di Pietro da Camerino in 1401, which depicts the procession of 1399. Nearby there is a large free parking.
A 17th century cloister.
An agricultural prison of the nineteenth century became a country.

River village about 5 km from the capital, in the golena of the Po, where the Po di Goro, the oldest branch, is detached, born from the Taglio di Porto Viro Venetian of the early sixteenth century: you can visit the church of Santa Maria del Traghetto and the oratory of Sant'Antonio. Around, the remains of the old village and abandoned farmsteads, trails along the ancient coastal dunes, reeds and river birds (colombacci, ducks, herons) and a river beach that changes shape with currents; recommended the bicycle, because few cars pass.

In the seaside village of Aspra, known for the limestone quarries and for the anchovies under salt and oil, the museum founded by Michelangelo Balistreri; opened from Monday to Saturday 9.30-12.30 according to the source.
A shrine frescoed inside the rock.

The ancient Hipponion, then Valentia and Monteleone: the Norman-Svevo Castle with the National Archaeological Museum ...Vito Capialbi , the sections of Greek walls discovered by Paolo Orsi, the Cathedral of Santa Maria Maggiore and San Leoluca and, on the sea, the port of Vibo Marina with the fish auction.
The marble village between the Apuan Islands.
The octagonal tower.

Museum dedicated to the Sicilian and Italian twentieth century, in the former Casa del Fascio: it collects artistic nativity scenes, paintings and sculptures of the Calabrian Salvatore Incorpora, whose work is linked to Guttuso, Migneco and Rijeka; it is also named after the sculptor Francesco Messina, baptized in the Mother Church in 1901.
The Gonzaghesque heart of the village in few steps.

Artificial invasion of the seventies of about 800 hectares, protected by the WWF since 1999 and indicated as the largest wetland in Campania, with riparian woods, pastures and steppe environments. It has visitor center, didactic workshop, nature trail and observation sheds.

Baroque with a single nave, built between 1660 and 1676 and enlarged in the eighteenth century: main altar in polychrome marble, choir, pulpit and carved doors, organ Agati di Pistoia; fresco of San Martino on horseback of Pietro Ivaldi known as "il Muto" and paintings by Antonio Monevi. Open during functions.

Wanted by Baron Bernardino de Ferrera and the bishop of Bosa Pietro de Sena and inaugurated in 1520, as evidenced by the inscription on the façade, it is considered one of the greatest examples of Gothic-Aragonese architecture in Sardinia: a single nave of five spans, portal gigliato, rosette and main chapel with keystone representing Santa Giulia on the cross. A crystal floor shows the oldest structures below, from the nuragic well to the early Christian church. The saint is celebrated on 22 May.

Marsica town overlooking the plain of the ancient lake of Fucino, dominated by the Piccolomini Castle which houses the Museum of Sacred Art of Marsica and the Torlonia Collection; home of Blessed Thomas of Celano, the first biographer of San Francesco. At the edge of the village are the Gorges of Celano, one of the most spectacular canyons of the Central Apennines.
The oldest church in the village, dating back to the 13th century, with Romanesque façade and terracotta frieze on the sides.
A path through the butterflies of Nero.

Romanesque church of the twelfth century in the cemetery of the village; at the end of the nineteenth century instead of the three naves were obtained chapels to support once a barrel that replaced the original trusses. Capitals have proto-Christian symbols.

In Val Brembana, the medieval village of Cornello dei Tasso, on a spur above the Brembo and reachable only on foot, was the first market after Bergamo on the Via Mercatorum and the cradle of the Tasso family, which organized the European postal service: today it preserves the portico street, the Romanesque church of Saints Cornelius and Cipriano and the Museum of Tasso and postal history.

Terraced shrine on the slopes of the Morrone, in use from the IV-III century BC to the middle of the II century AD: temple on high podium, sacellus with polychrome mosaic and a monumental staircase, overlooking the hair basin.

It tells the history of Gela through ceramics, bronzes and coins; the oldest core are the Navarra and Nocera collections. Among the findings presented by the Park are an archaic mask, a silent antefix, a horse head, a bronze corinzio helmet and a silver drama. It is the seat of the Archaeological Park of Gela; the ticket also includes the Walls Timoleontee and the acropolis of Molino a Vento.

Inaugurated in 1998, it is the main provincial centre dedicated to the lake environments, the water cycle and the ecosystem of Garda, with activities of environmental education and attention to sustainable tourism; it is open on request for educational activities.

Torcolato, sweet DOC wine made from grapes dried waspaiola for about four months, is produced only in the area of Breganze. In January, the Prima del Torcolato brings the first pressing with guided tours and tastings to the square; from May to September Open Wineries, to August the Wine Nights in Piazza Mazzini and in November the San Martino Fair with torresani on the spit.

Born from several donations of Paul VI, it collects about seven thousand works of the twentieth century (paintings, drawings, prints, medals and sculptures) belonging to Giovanni Battista Montini, with authors such as Matisse, Chagall, Picasso, Dalí, Magritte, Rouault, Severini, Morandi, Fontana, Manzù, Hartung and Guitton, testimony of the relationships between artists, the Pope and his secretary Pasquale Macchi. It has sections dedicated to graphics and medals and an educational center with guided tours and workshops. Open from Tuesday to Friday 9-12 and 15-17, Saturday 14-19; free entry for FAI members and with ticket of the Diocesan Museum of Brescia not more than three days before.

It preserves the Pala di Durante di Perugino, with the Madonna enthroned and saints, the Pietà and the predella with stories of the Virgin, returned to its altar in January 2026 after the restoration at the Opificio delle Pietre Dure; guided tours to the altars of Perugino and Giovanni Santi on Saturday and Sunday.
Built in the 11th century on a spur overlooking the town to control the valley, it became a symbol of the domination of the Challants; it can be visited freely within the walls.

Among the oldest factories in the city, documented since 1757: the four-storey cast iron building of 1866-1884, among the first in Italy with electricity in 1883; since 2000 it has been a public and cultural function and preserves the historical weaving machinery.
Two buildings just outside the village, the second near the cemetery, both with late medieval frescoes.

Collection started in the early 1990s by the Coplas cooperative, in the former restored slaughterhouse, managed by the Oreste Ventrice Association: tools and objects of agricultural traditions, artisans and pastorals of the arbëreshe community, a bedroom rebuilt with traditional fabrics and a working spinning and weaving corner. Booking not required.
The town center.
From the valley to the view of Lake Iseo.

The easternmost village of the Cinque Terre, from which starts the Via dell'Amore towards Manarola: the church of San Giovanni Battista, the remains of the castle and the sanctuaries of Montenero and of Health on the terraced highlands.
Understand how stone has become art in the portals of the valley.
The water of the Roman Narnia.
In the municipal seat, he collects works donated by the artists who have exhibited in the Romanesque church of San Lorenzo; it can be visited on working days in office hours.
The door to the ridge.
The life-size prehistoric elephant.
The Duomo of the city.

Parish church dedicated to a Roman martyr of the third century, with painting decorations of the XIV-XV centuries, a marble palace inlaid with a 17th century Neapolitan school at the main altar and paintings of the same period.

Explore for the first time in 1932 by speleologists led by Ermenegildo Zanchi, in 1939 they became one of the first tourist caves in Italy; the route of visit is about 70 meters. The most spectacular room is the ...Labyrinth (Büs de la Marta), with very high vaults and stalactites and stalagmites joined in columns; internal temperature of about 12 °C. Guided tours in groups of 25-30 people managed by the caves of Wonders caves; they serve slip-resistant shoes.
The Cathedral of Frederick II.
The Crivelli and the curious collections of weapons and hammers.
The liberation of Ancona in photographs.
The stuccoes at the foot of the country.
The Aragonese Gothic with millennia of history under his feet.
The liveliest fish market in the lagoon.
The cycle of hemp told on foot between the villages.
The famous natural mummy of Venzone.
Boat on the big river.
Inside a military area: visit only on the occasion of events organized by the Italian Army
The largest volcanic lake in Europe, ideal for sailing, fishing, diving, trekking, mountain biking and horseback riding.
In Stupinigi, in the countryside south of Turin, the hunting lodge of Filippo Juvarra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in its natural park.
A solar clock made of mountains.
The heart of the textile tradition that made the country famous.
Great stainless steel star by Pietro Consagra (1980) that welcomes those who arrive at the entrance of the new city, symbol of reconstruction.
The most important theatre in Venice, risen twice from the ashes, among the first destinations in the world for the opera.

In the village rebuilt after 1669 was opened the opening of the Quattro Canti, at the intersection between Via Giordano Bruno and Via Matteotti, on which the buildings of four important families overlook. The church of San Nicolò was the first of the new municipality: it resembles the ancient Mother Church and its bell tower copies the ancient one, but it is on the right of the facade instead of on the left.
Also in the Palazzo Agostiniano, it exhibits more than forty bicycles, all working, built or adapted in the early twentieth century for walking trades.

Borgo della valle Stura, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, capital of the filigree with the museum Pietro Carlo Bosio, dominated by the castle and crossed by the medieval bridge on the Stura.
Church of the 11th century rebuilt in the Baroque era, which preserves inside artifacts of various kinds.
FAI reports a highly endangered state of conservation; not indicated times

In the northern part of the territory, with the Valsoera valley, it is part of the Gran Paradiso National Park and is known for its protected flora and fauna, alpine lakes, glaciers and peaks suitable for trekking, mountaineering and climbing; there pass the Great Alpine Traverse and the High Via del Canavese with huts and bivouacs.
Three smaller churches between village and valley.

Square tower 23 m high on the 206 m hill, documented from 1022, passed in 1315 to Rinaldo Bonacolsi called Passerino and restored in 1611 and 1880. Inside a small museum with finds of the battlefield and the Hall of the Sovereigns with portraits of Vittorio Emanuele II and Napoleon III; a wooden ramp leads to the panoramic terrace on the Garda, the Tower of San Martino and the Apennines.
Seven thousand years of valley history.
Alexandria Cathedral.
On both sides of the building, panoramic walks on the coast.
The Red Palace of the Cybo-Malaspina, with columns, stairs and white marble loggias, now home to Province and Prefecture; the Hall of Mirrors and the Swiss Salon host exhibitions.
A Duccio in Maremma.
The historic building of the former liquor distillery Aurum, today ...Ideas Factory for exhibitions and events, the heart of the Dannunian Pinewood.
On the trail of the great painter born here.

The hilly village of Vercellese with a double-circle castle of walls in a dominant position, where in 1478 the Duchess Jolanda of Savoy died; around, the MoncriVillaTrails paths between vineyards of Erbaluce and Nebbiolo and the Garden of the Bees, living museum of beekeeping.
The green dome you can see from all over the city.
Walk where the reptiles of the Triassic have emerged.

Rebuilt in 1576 by the Orvieto architect Ippolito Scalza (replaced by Antonio Carrarino for the bell tower) on a first church of the twelfth century; it preserves a polyptych by Giovanni di Paolo of about 1440.
The oldest documented church in the center.

Late-Gothic church wanted by the lords of Duino, the Walsees, in the first half of the fifteenth century and rebuilt after the wars: a single nave, polygonal apse and the pavement mosaics of the early Christian basilica below, next to the Risorgives of Timavo.

Hypogeal tombs along the ancient road that connected the municipality of Misenum to Cuma: the excavated section includes at least seven quadrangular funerary buildings and barrel-shaped vaults, aligned in a single fifth, with a pediment kiosk on the back wall and niches on the walls, plus a multi-storey underground mausoleum behind. The oldest monument is late Republican, the others of the first century A.D.; the Municipality recalls the doumbars of officers of the Imperial fleet of Miseno, with portraits and birds frescoed and an inscription citing a military of the ship Virtus.

In the Palazzetto dei Vicari, 16th century building, the museum opened in October 1993 by the Municipality with Professor Dino Cheese, which donated the collection: about 200 paintings and sculpture from the end of the 19th century to today, including works by Medardo Rosso, Aligi Sassu and Tito Gasparini. Open Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 16-19, without reservation.
Palazzo overlooking Piazza Dellepiane, known for the decorations of the facade, including two sundials; it is one of the stages of the historical center of the municipality.
Roman Lupiae in the center.
The MiC card (updated to September 2021) is closed every day; tel. 0983 356494, mon-sab 8-11
At the balustrade of the belvedere a stone indicates the seventy-two visible countries, distributed in six provinces and four regions (Latium, Campania, Abruzzo and Molise).
The frescoed cloister of San Francesco.

On the morainic hills south-east of Garda, along the ancient road between the lake and Verona, the hamlet of Palazzolo preserves the Romanesque Pieve di Santa Giustina, built around the Mille and reopened after a long restoration, and the fifteenth-century church of Santi Quirico and Giulitta with the Crucifixion attributed to the school of Liberale da Verona.
The mother church of Romanesque origin.
The sulphur mines of Sicily.

A place of worship of the "federal" and a pilgrimage destination of the nuragic populations, known since the mid-nineteenth century: they remain part of the town and a sacred well. The numerous votive bronzes, from the IX-VIII century BC, are today at the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari and the Museum of Teti.

Sughere forest (Quercus suber), an evergreen typical of the Mediterranean coasts here usually overwhelmed by holm oak; open to the public, is managed since 2016 by the Regional Park of the Roman Castles.

On the monolith in the center of the village, on the right bank of the river: of the medieval complex are perhaps only the walls of the belt; renovated by the Bourbons around 1845, it was prison until 1968 and today houses a hermitage of the Friars Minor Renovated. In the Middle Ages it was joined to the Castle Soprano by a city wall.

The lively centre between the San Bernardino and San Giovanni streams, with medieval traces in via San Vittore, piazza Castello and piazza San Rocco; the church of San Vittore preserves paintings from the XV and XVI century. From the port the boats depart for the Italian and Swiss destinations of the lake.

The city rebuilt at the foot of Montecassino, the abbey founded by Saint Benedict in 529 and destroyed in 1944: below, the archaeological area of Casinum with theatre, amphitheatre and mausoleum, and the Fortress Janula on the Gustav Line.
In the eighteenth century Palazzo Ancajani di Tenaglie, houses the findings of the Umbrian-Etruscan necropolis of Fosso San Lorenzo, dating from the sixth to the fourth century BC.

The territory occupies the eastern side of the Limbara massif, with forests of holm oak, conifers and Mediterranean maquis; in the Limbara park, in the valley of the Santu Paulu river, walking and cycling paths with views. Near the village also the park of Stazzana with secular holm oaks.
Fortified structure that with the Fortress formed the defensive system of the city.
The gate of the battle of 1263.

Relief of 557 meters on the Belice Sinistro, inaccessible on three sides for three large rocky bastions, inhabited by the end of the Eneolithic in 1246: it was one of the three helimes cities with Erice and Segesta, occupied in 404 BC by the mercenaries of Campania and in the thirteenth century the last stronghold of the Islamic resistance against Frederick II. The excavations of the Scuola Normale di Pisa with the Superintendence have brought to light Hellenistic fortifications with towers and bastions, a public barn of the fourth century BC, the necropolis and, on Pizzo della Regina, a medieval fortification with cistern, as well as a castle and a fortified palace with hammam.
The white octagon next to the Rock.
A rock balcony on the high Scrivia valley.
The medieval tower at the top of the village.
Common memory of the fallen of the two fronts.

Opened in 2001 in the historic center, it is under construction in a renovated municipal building in Borgo Vaccareccia-Mezzana: two rooms with ancient crafts and crafts, relics of the two world wars and twenty years and the reconstruction of family homes of the early twentieth century with furnishings and utensils.
Latin sundials and mottos.
The torch's D.A. ruins.
The eighteenth papal on the pier.
From the castle tower you can see the whole valley.
The sixteenth century of Santa Croce in the heart of the village.
The ascent of pilgrims to the sanctuary.
The richest forest in the Murge, a few kilometers from the Baroque.
In the parish church and sacristy, works by Guido Cagnacci and Centino and sacred furnishings.

About 4 km from the village, it dates back to the 14th century with remains of the IX of probable Lombard origin; it is among the castles of the Marches remained intact, with a 35 meters high tower crowned by Ghibelline blackbirds, with archers and plumbings.

The symbol beach of the city, loved by the Olbians, about 8 km from the center on the road to Golfo Aranci: long crescent of fine and clear sand between the promontories of Muriscinu and Filiu, bottom suitable for families, bars and restaurants overlooking Tavolara. Accessible services, large parking, equipment rental, pedal boats and boats.
last 3 km on narrow road with bottom in bad condition; at the top no parking spaces nor refreshment points

Trexenta Centre, in 1614 elevated by Philip III to Duchy, unique in Sardinia created by a Spanish king, and stop of the Green Train told by D. H. Lawrence in 1921: the Gothic-Catalan parish church of St. James, the ethnographic museum Is Lollas de is Aiaiusu, the museum of sacred art Peregrinatio Fidei, the convent of St. Anthony on the Roman road and the nuraghe Su Angiu.
The nineteenth-century palace is owned by the municipality, already home to diplomat Nicolò Massa, who on the noble floor houses a collection of contemporary art started in the eighties.
Renaissance frescoes and a Roman mosaic inside the town hall.
Mantegna in the Verona Romanesque.

Country of the Ciociaria overlooking the plain of Cassino and crossed by the Via Francigena del Sud, rebuilt after the destruction of the Second World War; it preserves its goldsmith tradition in the Museum of Goldsmith Art and, at the foot of Mount Aquilone, the fifteenth-century sanctuary of Santa Maria de' Piternis.
An Etruscan road inside the city.
The Man of the 16th-century pains on the square of the village.

Hill country with views of the morainic hills and the plain, dominated by the remains of the castle with the small church of San Michele Arcangelo; you can visit the museum of peasant life Cjase Cocèl and the Oasis of the Quadris, where white storks have been reintroduced.
A silent Renaissance cloister under the castle.

The ski resort shared with Aprica from the village of San Pietro, about 15 km from Edolo, with slopes of different difficulty; the Superpanoramica del Baradello is indicated as the longest illuminated track in Europe. In San Pietro there are also the Baradello Wild Park and, in summer, the Saturday market in Piazza Funivia.

Medieval village at 751 meters above the summit of the mountain, above Trapani: the Castle of Venus on the sanctuary of Venus Ericina, the Garden of Balio, the Mother church of 1314 and the Cyclopean walls, with a look up to the Egadi.
The legend of Flaminio's grave.
The big ficus of the historic garden.
Aironi and kayak under the Circeo.
The convent that according to tradition the nobles dedicated to Saint Francis, guest of the nearby Badia di Santa Gonda.

The castle was built after 1217, when Spoleto allowed the men of Vallo to fortify the hill: the pedestrian village, closed by walls and towers, you enter the Portella and Portaranne gates, among which stands the main tower of the fifteenth century; narrow streets and light stone houses connected by passages and arches converge on the square of San Giovanni Battista.
A panorama of the Alps from the heart of the country.

Main church of the city, in Piazza Cavour near the lake, with Baroque appearance due to the eighteenth-century reconstruction: a single nave with side chapels, a large painting of the Assumption on the main altar and the Sorrows of Craffonara, a local artist.

Hardwood of almost 39,000 m2 on the right bank of the Dora Riparia, upstream of the village, on moraine deposits of the glacier of the Valley of Susa: lindens, elms, poplars, tremoli, farnie, ash and birch. Walk along dirt road and path along the river.
The monumental heart of the city, with rows of orange trees and the marble obelisk with four fountain lions erected in 1853, enlarged under Elisa Baciocchi.
A hilly village rebuilt in the eighteenth century.
The civic museum of the city in the eighteenth century Palazzo Fulcis on Piazza Vittorio Emanuele.

The seat of the Magnificent Community, built between 1444 and 1492 next to the church of Santa Maria Nascente. In the Council room, the Dedication of the Cadore in Venice by Cesare Vecellio and a Madonna by Marco Vecellio, a pine ceiling with the coat of arms of the Cadore and one by Valentino Paciera Besarel from 1862-64, and a frieze with 34 niches dedicated to illustrious cadorini. Opening to the public on Monday-Saturday 11-12.

Ruins a few meters high of a square tower of about 4,50 m of side, with square stones at the corners and pebbles arranged with fish spine, masonry dating back to the XII-XIII century: it is the only material testimony of a fortification in Roasio San Maurizio. It is located on a hill at the edge of the village, a few hundred meters north of the parish of San Maurizio.
Source celebrated by Ippolito Nievo and rediscovered by Pier Paolo Pasolini, whose original landscape has been restored with native tree species.
Contemporary art among granite houses.
The tradition of the tombolo pescolano.
The treasures of the Norman Miletus.

Area of the Roman settlement of the first century BC on the Via Iulia Augusta, where according to the source under Augustus (13/12 BC) a mansio arose.
