The fulcrum is the deconsecrated church of Saints Nazarius and Celsus, a single nave with semicircular apse, built on Roman structures; the excavations of the International Institute of Ligurian Studies, since 2005, have brought to light about eighty burials. Few remains are visible because the modern city rises above the site; the finds are at the Museum MARM.
The life of the shepherds of the Marghine.

Wanted by the brothers Daniele and Marcantonio Barbaro, commissioned between 1554 and 1560 and designed by Andrea Palladio, who inspired himself to the Roman temples for the facade; the central body is decorated by the fresco cycle of Paolo Veronese (1559-1561), while the stuccoes are attributed to Alessandro Vittoria. Behind the building there is the water lilies wanted by Marcantonio Barbaro; the side boats, intended for agricultural activities, end with two dovecotes decorated with sundials. The visit to the frescoes includes the six rooms painted by Veronese; the villa has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.
One of the great Gothic crucifixes of Italy.
She asked them under the floor.
Borgo del Chianti with Etruscan remains, the 14th century fortress and the covered walk of Via delle Volte.

Along the Viale delle Terme, the commercial heart of the city, the square houses one of the largest sundials in Europe in polychrome marble, 3,000 m2 on a project by Salvador Condè, completed at the end of 1996.
The life of a time in Valsesia.
The most beautiful glance on the village and lake.
Exit the village on foot, by bike or on horseback.
The treasures of Strong Ice.

Town of wool at the foot of the Alps, a UNESCO creative city, on three levels: the Piano with Duomo and Romanesque baptistery, the medieval village of Piazzo, since 2025 among the most beautiful villages in Italy, and the Sanctuary of Oropa on the Sacred Mount UNESCO heritage.
The urban beach along the Gulf of Angels.
Useful before a birdwatching exit.

Borgo dell'Alta Irpinia of the 13th century, known as the "Positano dell'Irpinia" (Positano dell'Irpinia) for its triangular plant and medieval structure with alleys and views; it was the epicenter of the earthquake of 1910 and is known for its bread and ceramics, told in the museum of Borgo Castello. Since 2013 it hosts every summer the Sponz Fest designed by Vinicio Capossela.
A Camaldolese abbey of the year 1000.
Carlone and the school of Margliano in Scrivia valley.

Giant fuchsia bench between the green and large trees, with 360° views of the hills and the village with the Fortress; you can reach following the signs "rainbow" in the area of Macchiosi - Grasceta dei Cavallari, destination of hikers and picnics.
The Peccioli symbol.
the Park warns that the earthquakes of 2016 have damaged many historical buildings and some areas are closed
Locality at 1029 meters above sea level, very frequented by bikers.
The altarpiece of the Cossali in a votive church.
In Via Rati the house linked to Christopher Columbus, which Cogoleto claims as his son; Italia.it indicates it as a stage to see from the outside.
On the ground floor of the Palazzo dei Musei, an emotional and interactive journey of 40 minutes in the history of the city and the palace.
Walking from Monterotondo to Rome.
The ancient parish church of Santi Vito e Modesto, just below the village, with its millennial cylindrical bell tower.
An easy climb to a panoramic tower between the sea and Slovenia.
Also known as the Basilica of the Tomb, there is buried the illustrious Roman Quintus of Sertoriano.
The center turns everything on foot.

Embedded in the Filonardi complex, it is probably where the Spanish hermit Pietro Ispano lived (X-XI centuries): the crypt of the tenth century is on the cave of the saint. In the Chapel Simoncelli there is the Angel of Giotto, a mosaic fragment of the ancient basilica of St. Peter and the only surviving mosaic of the artist, a marble bas-relief of the Madonna attributed to the Sansovino, a silver bust attributed to Benvenuto Cellini with the relics of the saint, the porphyry cross of the first Jubilee (1300) and a paleochristian sarcophagus (330-350 A.D.), found in 1941, with a Nativity bas-relief considered the oldest carved.

It is located in Palazzo Cumano, built by the Cumano brothers in 1763. It exhibits traditional gala costumes, half gala and newspapers from different arbëreshe communities (Vaccarizzo, Frascineto, Farneta, San Demetrio Corone, Piana degli Albanesi, Santa Sofia d'Epiro, Spezzano Albanese); on the upper floor there is the collection of gold and reproductions of ancient local jewels, with an exhibition of photographs and lithographies of Albanian costumes. Booking not required; MiC card does not report up-to-date times.
Giorgione's only fresco in his house.

Parish church of the diocese of Treviso from ancient origins: the census of the churches of the CEI records pre-existences around 1000 and the completion between 1043 and 1074, a portion of cloister of 1184, war destruction between 1192 and 1356 with reconstructions in 1234 and 1311, frescoes of 1344 and consecration in 1570. The bell tower was rebuilt in 1682, the main façade dates back to 1906 and in 1938 the chapel of San Benedetto was frescoed; inside also the chapels of Santa Francesca Romana and of the Addolorata and a baptismal font of 1860. The building was restored in 1991.
A shrine of peace made with the stones of war.
The ruins on the hill above the city.

The main port of the island was originally a lake, Lake of the Baths, open to the sea at the beach of Ferdinand II in 1854; today it is the most lively center, with restaurants, clubs and shops. In the third week of September, the Port Festival recalls the arrival of Frederick II and his dolphin.

In the Park of Murgia there are rock churches of the X-XI century; the abbey had rock churches in the Murgia of Sant'Andrea and near the village there is the crypt of Cozzo Sant'Angelo (XI-XII century).

The festival of bruschetta celebrates bread with extra virgin olive oil Sabina DOP; the fettuccine alla trebulana have their feast in the first week of August; other specialties are pancakes and aniseed doughnuts.

It was mentioned in 1220 and 1249, burned in 1499 after the battle of Calva and rebuilt in Gothic forms in 1570-1580; the excavations found an earlier church of the VI-VIII century and fragments of Romanesque frescoes of excellent quality. You can reach it on foot to the Sölesweg; guided tours in German only on request.
The ruins that dominate the village.
The story of Troy from its origins to today.
MiC card (updated 2021) indicates closed every day, times to be verified
The Last Supper of Tiepolo.
To eat fish on an ancient fishing machine on the sea.

A small village in the Val d'Isarco between Bolzano and Chiusa, dominated by Castel Trostburg, one of the largest fortified complexes in South Tyrol, a residence for over six centuries of Wolkenstein and now home to the Museum of South Tyrol castles.
The two high peaks of the municipality (3142 and 3559 meters); the Mont Emilius can be reached also by a via ferrata.
Free of charge, both the porch and the sanctuary
The memories of Donizetti in one place.
An Italian theatre of the nineteenth century in miniature.
Stone villages of the Master Comacini.
In the Cistercian Abbey of Valserena, the museum-archive of the University with millions of drawings, photographs, design projects, architecture and fashion of the twentieth century.

The 63-metre-high bell tower is the highest of the Eastern Polesine: the original nineteenth-century, struck by lightning in 1922, was rebuilt in 1927 in a form that recalls that of San Marco in Venice.
The medieval church of the village.
In Piazza Missori the surviving crypt of the church, important early Christian witness.
The patron's church on the main square.

Comune del Monferrato casalese with two castles and their historical parks: that of Ponzano, mentioned already in 1014, with nineteenth-century gardens and a panoramic tower, and that of Salabue of the Cozio counts, as well as an infernot excavated in the Pietra da Cantoni.
Nature of the Lunigiana and view from the hanging garden.
Baroque plasters and frescoes next to the memory of Garibaldi.
Medieval village in the hills, about 4 km from the coast, partly surrounded by the walls of the castle; Annibal Caro was born there.

The summit and the alpine lake of the valley.
Granite island of the Tuscan Archipelago with three centers, Giglio Porto, Giglio Castello and Campese, clear sea and vineyards of Ansonica.

The fortifications of one of the oldest castles of the Casentino, dating back to the 11th century, destroyed by Bishop Tarlati in 1322: the small round tower with octagonal base survives, recently restored, together with the ruins of the 14th century military camp. The palazzo podestarile, now canonical, has an elegant loggia of the first fifteenth century and stone coats of arms on the façade; near the center the eighteenth-century church of San Giovanni Evangelista and the historic oven of the village.
Nature and sport on the former quarry's water mirrors.
The excavations that emerged during the reconstruction of the theatre, which show the city from the fourth century BC to the nineteenth century.
Ring path of more than 10 km that climbs from the village to the Sanctuary of the Chapels along the Iannello stream and returns to Laino Borgo.
One of the first stable theatres of the modern age.

Immersed in greenery, with a barchess and a 17th century church; a canvas by Alessandro Maganza with a guitar player, today at the Academy of Venice, gave the name to the locality "Guitarra" . Visits only by appointment.

A tower of about 30 meters with a quadrangular plan on a hill just above the village, with views of Perugia and Trasimeno; built between XII and XIII century by the Knights Hospitallers, controlled supplies for Perugia, especially the fish of the north shore of the lake. Restored by the Municipality in the eighties, it hosts exhibitions on four floors and has a panoramic terrace; around a park with life path. Hours: July-August Mar-dom 10-13 and 16-19.30 (sab-dom also 21.30-23.30); April-June and September-Jo-dom 10-13 and 15-18; October-March by reservation. Info: tel. 075 8473078.
In the sacristy of the Collegiate Church: sacred art and vestments from the sixteenth century, including a marble tabernacle of 1545 and eighteenth-century vestments.
The door to the castle with its original key.
Among the best preserved walls of the Marche.
Late medieval frescoes in a Romanesque church.
The most beautiful view of the Itria Valley.

Built in 1919 for Ottorino Pomini in a late eclectic style: three floors and a panoramic tower, exposed brick facades and plaster with two-lighted windows, arches, loggias and graffiti, a stone plinth of Moltrasio and a long portico with red brick arches. In 1982 Luciano Pomini offered it to the municipality as a cultural centre: today it houses exhibitions, courses and the library donated by the family, in a park of about 5,300 m2.
In the town hall the evolution of communication: microphones, gramophones, telephones, telegraphs, a reproduction of the Titanic radio cabin and a donation Rai.
One of the oldest churches in Lucca, with the thirteenth-century golden mosaic on the façade, the chapel of Santa Zita and the chapel frescoed by Amico Aspertini in 1508-1509.
Dunes, wetlands and olive groves on the Adriatic shore.
Each holm oak in the park is reminiscent of a temple that fell in World War I.
The walled village born of the survivors of Kaulon.
A place reminiscent of the massacre of World War II in which 244 people were killed, along with a tombstone and a monument.
The palm garden.

Founded in 1942 by the University of Padua at 1045 meters above sea level, it houses the Galileo telescope, a reflector with a primary mirror of 122 cm, the largest in Europe when it was inaugurated and still used for research and didactics. Guided tours, by reservation, include the Galileo dome and a multimedia room connected to the telescope; a few kilometers away, in Cima Ekar, there is the 182 cm Copernicus telescope.
The X century tower.
Historical trains on the last section of the Rome-Fiuggi.

Villa Liberty built in 1880 for the financier of Antwerp Edouard Cahen, made marquis by Vittorio Emanuele II, on a large estate between two ridges of the Paglia; it is surrounded by a largely Italian garden with rare plants, a Japanese garden restored, greenhouses and lemon trees, in the protected area of Allerona-Meana.

In the Dolomiti Bellunesi National Park, between Sospirolo and Sedico, wide meadows still mowed surrounded by woods and along the Cordevole: a place suitable for observing deer and chamois, as well as deer, green woodpecker, sliced salamander and amphibians. Easy access from San Gottardo, with parking near the church; recommended spring period.
The most beautiful square in Como.
The rocks carved in the middle of the woods.
Nobile rooms and walk of patrol over the Volturno plain.
Palace of 1542 with the Museum of War and the Gothic Line and the Chestnut Museum.
Six centuries of sacred art from the high Val Trebbia.

Section of the Museum Ladin, the provincial museum of South Tyrol, opened in 2011 on three floors: at the top the formation of the Dolomites through the fossils typical of the surroundings of San Cassiano, at the center the discovery and excavations of the Conturines cave with the remains of the Ursus Ladinicus, the cave bear lived over 50,000 years ago, and on the ground floor the reconstruction of the cave with the bear hibernating and the puppy. Fully wheelchair accessible; open 10-18 hours from 26.12.2026 to 15.03.2027 and from 02.05.2027 to 05.11.2027.
A large baroque sanctuary overlooking the plain.

Alleys and rustic houses between the lake and the Centa: in Via Roma the houses were built together in a few years and they carry engraved dates on the arch keys, the most recent in 1836 at number 23; in Piazza Vecchia the fountain and the tourist office, in front of the Town Hall a panel on the Tower of the Sicconi and on Federico IV "Tascavuota" in Via Graziadei one on the bachiculture.

In the building in front of the town hall, it illustrates with panels and reproductions the diseases and parasites of chestnut and its fruit, with numerous original tools for the working of the wood and its products. Open only by reservation.
A Ghibelline castle in the woods.
Built at the end of the fourteenth century to defend the historic center.

A thematic route of about 2.3 km (about 1 hour, tourist difficulty) made in 1992 by the Community Montana del Giovo and now managed by the Park of Beigua, a ring on the square of the Hermitage; crosses the remains of the walls of the ancient monastic complex between holm oaks, oaks, black pine trees and beech trees, touches the Source of Sant'Elia with the rare fern and counts about 50 panels on the species.

A church of the tenth century in the heart of the village, with a bell tower of 25 meters and four bells in Gothic style, enlarged in the first half of the nineteenth century under the guidance of Valadier; it houses the Madonna of the Heart of Sebastiano Conca, who arrived in Gerano in 1729 at the center of the devotion of the infiorata.
A whale in the hills of Valdelsa.
Ovens and mills.
The viewpoint on Lake Maggiore.
Naturalistic area of about 5 hectares preserved in an almost natural state.
A village painted above the valley.
The defensive profile of the city.

Village of medieval plant along an elongated axis with transversal alleys and arches that strengthen the houses-walls, protected to the west by a cliff and facing south; of the ancient belt remain Porta da Capo (called the Ribellino) and Porta da Piedi.

Remains of a Roman sanctuary about 2 km from the village, built from the middle of the II century BC and abandoned in the first century A.D.; the first stone blocks emerged in 1950 during agricultural works. The complex includes a temple dedicated to Jupiter, a worship building behind and a large porch that encloses the sacred area.

In the 19th century country villa of the counts Avogadro degli Azzoni, with rustic outbuildings, more than 4 hectares of meadows, woods and fields, an ancient rose garden and a didactic apiary, at the foot of the Park. It collects objects from Bellunese from the eighteenth century to today on crafts, home, religion, clothing and emigration, with sections on the baliatic and emigration to Brazil of the late nineteenth century; thousands of recordings of stories, songs and prayers, photographic and film archives and the collection of mountain art by Giuseppe Mazzotti. Open Mar-Fri 9-13, Sat and Sun 15-18.30; closed Monday.
An industrial architecture of the 1930s symbol of reclamation.
A medieval hospice for pilgrims on top of the mountain.

Medieval village with concentric circles around Piazza Alta, at the foot of the Sibillini Mountains: Santa Maria Assunta, the Pinacoteca with works by Vittore Crivelli and Simone De Magistris, the thermal baths of oligomineral waters and the Via delle cascatelle lost.
Rural architecture in raw earth, rare to see.
The towers of the castle that dominates the village.
A rare Carolingian building on Garda.
The hamlet Bandiera Arancione di Roncofreddo, among the most interesting historical villages 15 km from Cesena.

The birthplace of the writer Vincenzo Cuoco, owned by the Municipality; according to Italia.it has been restored as a space for events and reception, while Visit Molise indicates it in renovation to become a Museum of Contemporary Art.
The hills of Monteferrato that close to the north the plain of Prato.

Franciscan monastery of 1481 on a rock spur 35 meters high: cloister porticoed with lunettes painted in 1661 with stories of Saint Anthony of Padua, church with choir and door of 1481, refectory of 1748 with a Last Supper of the first sixteenth century.
The medieval bridge with the goldsmiths' shops, surmounted by the Vasarian Corridor.

About 3,500 square meters dedicated to the flora of Monte Baldo, which counts 1,655 varieties of plants and flowers: geometric flowerbeds, the Garden of the simple and an area of spontaneous species. Guided tours also include the halls of the palace and the fossil museum.
The Seat Square.

Castagno called dark bottle, estimated between 4 and 5 centuries, with hollow trunk and blackened about 12,85 meters of circumference and crown of about 15,5 meters; for the tradition it was born from a chestnut thrown to the ground by San Francesco di Paola. The municipality has asked for its recognition as a monumental plant. It rises 1,160 metres in a clearing about 150 metres from Lake Cecita, which can be reached by car, by bike, on foot or by the Parks Cyclovia.

The municipality offers a walk or bike ride through the farmhouses of the territory. Among the stages: the Cascina San Biagio, with the perhaps oldest oratory of Cameri (walling of the second half of the 11th century, fresco of the Virgin enthroned between St. John the Baptist and St. Biagio); the Cascina Argine, where from 1347 the Lateran Canons settled, with the oratory of the Blessed Virgin of the Snow frescoed in the eighteenth century; the Cascina Bornago, a fortified farmhouse already in 912, overlooking the valley of the Ticino; the Cascina Galdina with the oratory of San Galdino. The farmhouses are private property: they are observed from the outside.

Founded in 1978 and managed since 1995 by the association of volunteers       ÂAL Palèsi Â, it has a paleontological path and a geomineral path, plus a short path of paleoanthropology. Among the finds mollusk and pliocenic crabs of Vignola and Marano, a rare jaw of tapir, remnants of cetacean, shark teeth, parts of ichthyosaur and Cretae ammonites of the Apennines, the Crespellani collection, rocks and minerals between Reno and Secchia with septari and ... Open on Sunday 10:30-12:30; on weekdays by telephone reservation, guided tours also to the fossiliferous outing.
The tower of the abbot of Farfa.
The fractions and a hidden frescoed crypt.
The millennial parish church above the lake.

Road bridge in steel tower on the Po, shortly after the confluence with the Ticino, 1040 meters long in 13 bays. The debate on the new bridge began in 1893 and was chosen Mezzanino because there already existed since 1865 a bridge of boats; it was built in 1912 by the Society Nathan Uboldi of Milan on a project by engineer Jules Röthlisberger of the Società Nazionale di Savigliano, and an inscription on the access arch recalls that it was born for the concordi energies of Municipalities and Provinces. Restored in the fifties after the damage of the war, it was the subject of interventions after the flood of 2011.
The ancient history of the territory.
It preserves the Madonna del Ponte, the fresco above the altar to which miraculous apparitions have been attributed over the centuries.

The capital of Abruzzo at the foot of the Gran Sasso, reborn after the earthquake of 2009: the Basilica of Collemaggio with the Holy Door of Forgiveness, the 99 Cannelle Fountain, the Spanish Fort and the MuNDA, up to the Roman remains of Amiternum.

The three circles of fortifications of the Five, Six and Nineteenth Century, with curtains, bastions, ditches and revells; the third line, the Lunetta, was added by the French of Napoleon in 1805. Route on the walls of about 360,000 square meters.

Artificial basin created by barring the Tiber near Corbara, with about 207 million m3 of water and 51 m of maximum depth, in the Tiber River Park established in 1995: it opens from the Forello Gorges, with travertine walls and caves; habitats of herons, deer and mouflons, fishing destination for carp, canoe and trekking.

The tower of Regina della Scala on the Lambro.
The great Nilotic mosaic of Roman spas.
A medieval village still intact.
A castle of the Roeros among frescoes and prisons.

At Palazzo Ruffo (1875): agricultural tools, cauliflowers and iron objects, a stone mill from the early twentieth century with a large hydraulic Pelton wheel still working, furniture of the eighteenth-nineteenth century, clothes and terracotta; a room exhibits over two hundred pipes of Mastro Rocco De Giglio, many shaped animals and human figures.

The remains of Julia Concordia: two Roman sepulchral enclosures and the ruins of two early Christian buildings of the fourth century, the Trichora Martyrum and the Basilica Apostolorum, built on an older house; it also opens with guided visits and extraordinary openings of the Ministry.
Templar church with frescoes of Giotto style.
In the Visitor Centre of the park, in the territory of San Romano, the Natural Museum is located together with the Museum of raptors (or predator); next to the garden of mountain flowers.

Built between 1265 and 1286, with bell tower of a century later and white stone portal with the Assumption in the bezel. He preserves works by Lorenzo d'Alessandro (1483), Niccolò Alunno, Paolo Bontulli (1530) and the Madonna of Mercy by Pietro Alemanno, who also frescoed the crypt in 1494.

Overlooking the square, built around 1680, it retains a Crucifixion of 1570 by Nicolò Circignani called the Pomarancio, a Madonna with Child (XVI-XVII century) attributed to Giovanni della Robbia and a bell dated 1269.
A small nineteenth-century theatre in gold and damask.
In the villa where Guglielmo Marconi did the first experiments, a three-storey museum with functional apparatuses; next to the Mausoleum of 1941.

Designed by Renzo Piano and inaugurated on 1 July 2004 after about ten years of work, wanted by the Capuchin Friars Minor and financed almost entirely by the offerings of pilgrims. The spiral plant, inspired by the spiral of Archimedes, places the altar in the middle; walls in stone of Apricena, oxidised copper cover and a window with scenes of the Apocalypse. In the lower church the crypt where St. Pius' body has been resting since 2010.

Inaugurated in 2004 in the baronial castle, it exhibits the excavations of 1928-29, which brought to light 65 burials between the VIII-VII and the IV-III century B.C., of the culture of "Oliveto-Cairano." The feminine ornaments rich in ornaments (pendants, earrings, pendants, heart-shaped bracelets) are outstanding with the reconstruction of a costume, black paint vases and red figures and bronze belts of the Sannitico costume. The Touring indicates opening on Tuesday-Saturday 9-13 and 14-15, Sunday 9-13.
The last trench of Waldensian history, in the place where it happened.

Mountain of the house above Lana, about 1,800 meters, reached by a modern cable car from Lana di Sopra up to 1,486 meters; the cable car of Monte San Vigilio is indicated as the second oldest in Europe. The church of San Vigilio, probably fourteenth-century, is located on an ancient place of worship at 1,790 metres, the Gampl mountain pasture and the Bärenbad alpine pasture; in winter a small ski area.
Where the idea of the Red Cross was born.
A Neapolitan Atlantis.
A sorority church with seven centuries of history.
The house of Roncole where Verdi was born on October 10, 1813 with a multimedia path told by the voice of the Child Master; near, the church where the organ played.
Sican tomb kits.
Relax in altitude after skiing or hiking.
The catacombs under the church of the saint.
Latin cross church of 1278, originally Romanesque, remodelled in Baroque style in the eighteenth century; in the twentieth century the exterior was restored to Romanesque forms.
Stone houses and memories of the Shroud.
The memory of the Battle of Cornuda in 1848.
Green basin at the foot of the Colle del Piccolo San Bernardo, between the Rutor Falls, the Roman remains and the cromlech of the pass and the ancient coal mines.
Born from the donation of Mario Foresi's collection in 1914, in the historic De Laugier barracks.

The largest glacier in the Stelvio National Park, in the Ortles-Cevedale group, is reached from Rifugio Forni: the glaciological path passes through the remains of fortresses of the First World War and, in the high path, crosses two Tibetan bridges to the mouths from which flows the melting water.
The Wolkenstein castle and all the castles of South Tyrol in miniature.
Adventure park in the forest of Montepiano with trails suspended between walkways, pulleys and lianas, suitable for families.
Authentic Middle Ages among the chestnut groves.

Erected in 1567 on a design by Lelio Orsi, enlarged in the eighteenth century, with 1616 bell tower and stucco by Giuseppe Mazza (1704). Inside the Martyrdom of St. Lawrence (1570) and the Ascension of Pier Maria Bagnadore (1580); in the sacristy two historian plates signed by Nicolò da Urbino and Orazio Fontana (1538).
A Basilian hermitage in the valley.
visits only for groups of at least 5 people by reservation (Visit Rovereto)
Styrone's fossil whales.

It is part of the Casentino's ecomuseums and tells of the production and trade of gunpowder, which marked Chitignano in the nineteenth century, both in the authorized powder kegs and in the "pilli" hidden in the woods, together with the tobacco smuggling favored by the privileged tax regime granted by the Grand Duchy.

Less than 700 hectares with over a thousand plant species: beech, linden and maple in the valleys to the north, oaks and oaks on the southern slopes, prairies, karst springs and limestone walls; it is a stopover point for many species of migratory birds. Paths from very easy to challenging go up to the summit and medieval remains, with views of the Brianza and the lakes of Como, Annon and Garlate. At the Hermitage a 48 seat park hostel.
Palace built in 1770-1773 by Baron Francesco Maria Pantaleo at the western end of the Old City, with majolica floors and paintings by Domenico Carella.
Closed as Dürer saw it.
The perfect medieval square, the city's greatest artistic pride: the Town Hall in the Broletto, the Torrazzo, the octagonal plan Baptistery and the Duomo.
Walk on the trail of the first inhabitants of Beigua.
The spot where a canal passes under a stream.
Thirty underground rooms built in Roman times to collect and purify the city's water, among the best examples of this kind in Italy; the Museum Polo offers a tour itinerary.
The square overlooking the Town Hall and Palazzo Sersanti, a node of a center from the Roman plant.
A Madonna of Raphael school a few steps from the caves.
The monastery of the village.
A wet area of great importance for birdlife and biodiversity, overlooking a bay where small boats can be moored.
The palace of the Grand Dukes.
The reborn village.

The highest hamlet and one of the oldest in Villadossola, mentioned in documents as "Scogno": the position on a fertile shelf protected by overhangs suggests an ancient castle, where in times of danger the inhabitants of the valley bottom brought families, cattle and goods. There are the oratory of St. John the Evangelist and the Museum of peasant civilization. You reach it by mule tracks and steps.
Interactive workshop with models, multimedia, games and a sensory space on scents and sounds of the forest.
The porticoed heart of the city of ceramics.
Pebble beaches at the foot of the village, within walking distance or by shuttle.
Thirty nuraghi in a valley.
A lighthouse on the hill watching the Murge.
visit only by reservation (tel. 347 8436982)
The ancient church with white and green bands today civil building and the Tower of Catilina, which complete the complex of the square.

The town of Valdarno, above the foothills of the Chianti Mountains, marked by the extraction of lignite that emptied the village of Castelnuovo dei Sabbioni, now home to the MINE museum; also worth seeing is the Botanical Roset "Carla Fineschi," the parish church of San Giovanni Battista with its museum and the castles of Montegonzi and Montaio.
Two centuries of Sardinian costumes and jewelry in a palace of kings and writers.
Villa built in the middle of the sixteenth century by Cardinal Bartolomeo Gallio, then by the Borghese, with almost three hectares of wood and a clearing.
The utopia of a sculptor.
The canal district, in the evening full of bars, restaurants and clubs; Corso di Porta Ticinese is one of the most beautiful streets in Europe to walk.
A neoclassical temple full of symbols.
the city card indicates only extraordinary openings

Borgo della Majella on the high Aventine, dominated by the 11th century ducal castle that houses the Geopaleontological Museum; in the former convent of Sant'Antonio the Museum of the Marsican bear with the fauna area, and under Mount Porrara the hermitage of the Madonna dell'Altare.

World War II shelters: one, from 1941, could accommodate from 61 to 82 people; the one in Via Roma, from 1943-44, had a capacity of 344 people and a fireplace of 17 meters. The tour, guided only and with sound effects, is held in Italian, English, French and German for groups up to 25 people, by reservation at Discoverminiera; the refuges of Via Roma are fully accessible by wheelchair.
The temple where the Waldenses chose to resist in 1686.
Contemporary art inside the old cells.
The decrees and treasures of Entella.
The heart of the city, a place of ceremonies, markets and concerts, between nineteenth-century buildings and the town hall.
A green break after the climbs.
Matteotti's memory.
Museum that tells the secrets of the beekeeper's trade.

Inaugurated in October 2006 by the Foundation chaired by Fiorenzo Magni, at 754 m altitude, it preserves over 2,000 objects of great champions: the largest collection of pink shirts, made with the Gazzetta dello Sport, yellow tops of the Tour, the bicycles of Bartali, Coppi and Magni, the bikes of the records of the hour of Baldini, Rominger and Moser, military bikes of the early twentieth century including a Bersaglieri folding Whites, sections on cyclocross, MTB, paracycling and female cycling and a wall dedicated to the cyclists who died in the race. From the viewpoint next to the museum you can see Lake Como from above; open from Tuesday to Sunday.
Wet areas and birdwatching along the Secchia.

It recalls February 28, 1522, when an image of Our Lady and Child painted at the end of the fifteenth century on a wall of the Monastery of St. Augustine shook tears and the French general Odet de Foix (Lautrec) spared the city from looting; on February 28 it has since been a town festival. After the authentication desired by San Carlo Borromeo, the first stone was laid on March 25, 1594 and the building was completed in 1619, when the image was taken to the main altar. It preserves the sword and helmet of Lautrec, works of different eras including Bernardino Butinone and contemporary mosaics of Trento Longaretti; it is a stop of the Via di Sant'Agostino. Open every day 7.30-18.30.
The only remnant of the walls, one of the three gates of the medieval village, in the oldest part of the village; the church of St. John the Baptist next to the castle destroyed in 1693.
18th century façade; inside paintings of the eighteenth century of the mountains, an intense crucifix of Guercino school and the 17th century chapel of the saint, entirely covered with stuccoes.
The water that unites the Roman and Middle Ages.
The ancient heart of the valley, with its sundial-motto.
Veio and his centuries in a noble palace.
Versi by Virgilio graffiti on the walls.

Opened in 1992 in the former church of San Nicola, along the ascent to the sanctuary of the Fortress, it is part of the Valsabbia Museum System. Along the aisle, for thematic areas, hundreds of objects of breeding, handicrafts, domestic life and weaving: carpenter's shops, blacksmith, beekeeper, shoemaker, host and tanner, an old kitchen, a bedroom and an ancient frame still working for wool carpets; each object has the name in Italian and dialect. Timetable and rates: tel. 0365 85119.
The museum of the sea of Genoa.
Gothic frescoes and a painting of the 17th century Vimercate.
Alleys, towers and pink stone.
A unique aeronautical collection in Europe, in the castle of the flight on Vienna.

At 350 metres above sea level, next to the oak-tree site that the legend linked to the Holy Land (which collapsed on 18 June 2010); the nucleus is medieval, with additions of the late seventeenth century, and is entrusted to the Missionary Sisters of the Immaculate. The parishes of Cornuda, Coste, Covolo, Maser, Nogarè and Onigo go on pilgrimage every year.
A rare fourteenth-century cycle of school in Brianza.
Prints, ceramics and views of the bridge.

Built between 1213 and 1282, as two internal inscriptions recall, it was the bishop's seat of the diocese of Sulci until 1503, when it passed to Iglesias. Late-Romanesque with Gothic omens, in sedimentary and volcanic stone, has three naves on pillars, covered with trusses, rosette on the façade, hanging arches, capitals of influence of Pisa to the southern portal and two lions on the architrave of the north portal; in the left nave a retablo of 1596.

About 180 hectares established in 2004 between Port of Ascoli and the mouth of the Tronto: sandy cordons, humid backdunal areas and brackish prairies, two ponds for birdwatching, the Tower on the Port of 1543 and cyclopedonal paths.
Sanctuary on Monte delle Rose, 608 meters above sea level in the Taburno-Camposauro Regional Park, in the diocese of Telese.

Convent in the hamlet of Alvignanello, built between the middle of the XVI and the middle of the XVIII century by local workers and still used as a convent, owned by the Bishop's Curia Alifana-Caiatina. The ICCD card describes it as a rectangular plan, in tuff masonry, with barrel vaults and roof in tiles, in good state of preservation; it is protected as a cultural asset.
Verbicaro's wine in the former prison.
The parish church of the village.
A garden like a play.
Collection of musical instruments in a former railway building of the pine forest Zerbi, renovated by the cultural association for the protection of the musical instrument.

Built between 1836 and 1839 on a project by Giuseppe Talucchi, with neoclassical facade with six columns and frescoes by Luigi Hartmann; inside, with three naves, the frescoes on the life of Sant'Agata (1858-1862) by Paolo Emilio Morgari, Luigi Hartman and Carlo Costa, the nineteenth-century organ of the Serassi, the polyptych of Gerolamo Giovenone of 1531 and the chapel of Sant'Ignazio da Santhià, canonized cappuccino in 2002. The 12th century Romanesque bell tower, about 35 metres high, lost its summit in 1555 under the cannons; with the crypt it is a national monument. Open every day 7.30-12 and 17-18.30.

Born in 1997 from the expansion of the Antiquarium, in a wing of the eighteenth century municipal palace called "Stalloni dei Borboni": male and female honorary statues of the forum, mostly between the 1st century BC and I AD, with Gaius Caesar nephew of Augustus, and the sculptures returned from the National Archaeological Museum of Naples; also architectural elements, funerary objects and mythological subjects from the maritime villas.

One of the best examples of a barrage fortress of the early nineteenth century, almost intact; one climbs up with panoramic lifts. It houses the Museum of the Alps, the Prisons and the Museum of Fortifications and Frontiers.
The peasant's mint pancake.
Crypt on Roman capitals and frescoes of the Pisanello school.
The Ligurian Alps.

In the territory there are about ten nuraghi: Sa Tanchitta and Corona Alta in red trachyte, Su Crapione and Buffulinu in white stone. There are also domus de janas, called coroddos: four attributed to ziu Juanne and the domu de su Crapione, dug into the tuff.
Dam lakes.
Here Galileo was baptized.
The Roman Pusteria told from its finds.

The trapezoidal acropolis of about two hectares is surrounded by ciclopic walls of the second century BC on a more ancient fortification; the urban belt of about 2 km, work of the Ernics between IV and II century BC, has five doors. The Porta Maggiore has a monolithic architrave of over five meters, estimated in about 30 tons; from the gardens of the Civita the view extends over the Ciociaria and the Ernici Mountains. Every June 21st we go up to the acropolis to see the first light on the eastern wall.
The church on the hill overlooking the stream.
Five thousand years of ethnic history inside a medieval donjon.
The bridge over the throat.

The capital of the Salento Baroque: the Basilica of Santa Croce, the scenic Piazza del Duomo, the Roman amphitheatre in Piazza Sant'Oronzo, the Roman theatre, Porta Napoli and the Castle of Carlo V; outside the city the archaeological park of Rudiae and the Abbey of Cerrate.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates the museum being set up and closed every day
The panoramic walk above the Lario.
Documented from 1185 and already surrounded by solid walls in 1258, several times damaged, it preserves the medieval walls, a door, perimeter towers and two medieval wells.
The baroque symbol of the center.
A green break between the Sanctuary and the excavations.
Industrial archaeology next to the waterfall.
The traces of the abbey.
The highest castle in the Apennines, suspended on Baronia.

Medieval village called the "balcony of the ternan basin" for its views, with polygonal walls; on Mount Torre Maggiore the remains of a temple of the sixth century BC and, in the surroundings, the Aeolian Cave.

More than two thousand objects reconstruct the past of Roseto, his people and his crafts: agricultural tools and domestic tools, ancient toys, a school hall of epoch, carpenter shops, blacksmith, shoemaker and barber, weaving frames; a photographic section with portraits of rosetans, photo library, classroom and library.

Dedicated to Saint Bernardino da Siena, it includes the church of San Bernardino and the convent of Santa Maria degli Angeli. The church has a unique nave with three small polygonal chapels on the left: in the first, dedicated to the Madonna, frescoes attributed to the Treviso Bernardo Zenale and Bernardino Butinone; on the tramezzo the cycle of the Passion of Fermo Stella, recently restored. Open Monday to Friday 9-17; guided tours by reservation.
Baroque frescoes and a perfume museum.

Borgo of Etruscan origin on a cliff of tuff about 132 meters high above the Tiber: under the houses runs Orte underground, a hydraulic system of tunnels, wells and cisterns of 2,500 years; on the surface Renaissance buildings, the basilica of the Assumption, the sacred art museum in the Romanesque church of San Silvestro and, in the plain, the Roman river port of Seripola.

Comune dell'alto Lago di Como, on the western shore, which rises from the lake between woods and pastures to the peaks, with long beaches loved by windsurfers and kiters; here Don Guanella started his work with the first house of mercy for the elderly. The Museum of the Barca Lariana, in a nineteenth-century spinning mill, is worth a visit.

Ancient entrance door of the village, dating back to about 1500, which owes its name to the bloody massacre of the Waldenses of June 1561. The Waldensian community, which arrived from the valleys of Piedmont between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, was repressed by the Inquisition after joining the Reformation, with severe penalties for the survivors and the prohibition of speaking the Occitan.
A little forgotten Romanesque.
Collection dedicated to wine and corkscrew, in the same villa.
Lake near the village with view and walk around; the fog of the lake often surrounds the village.
To be checked on the Pinacoteca website
Church built before 1128 with the altarpiece of the Madonna del Rosario by Bernardo Strozzi; the bell tower is a defensive tower of the IX century.
A path of about 10 km, part of the Via Francigena, which is done in about two hours, almost everything in the shade and with views of the lakes.

Borgo about 3 km from the sea, municipal seat until the 1920s: stone buildings, carugi, squares, houses towers and doors painted with the imaginary shops, the houses, turned outwards, were walls. At the entrance the high Sarcena tower, of sighting, of the late fifteenth century; in the village the sanctuary of Our Lady of Graces, where St Bernard of Chiaravalle preached, the Oratory of the Assumption and the deconsecrated church of Santa Crescenza.
Water and granite in the heart of Gallura.

In the fifteenth century Palazzo Bruni-Ciocchi sculptures and paintings from the thirteenth to the sixteenth century (Margaritone, Spinello Aretino, Signorelli, Vasari), with majolica, glass, coins, avori and weapons.

A fortified area that occupies the entire plateau at the top of the fortress, with walls still visible: after the first entrance a space housed the houses of artisans and soldiers, a second fortified entrance leads to the courtyard from which you access the Donjon. The entrance door is at the entrance of the Palazzo De Antonellis-Villani.

In front of the seventeenth-century Palazzo Spinola, a nymph with niche, semi-dome and white marble mask pours water into a large stone basin; on the same square a covered washbasin and, along the main street, the fountain for the mules with copper drips, in front of the former palazzo pratorio. The fountains are fed by an ancient water system that carried the waters of Borbera through a roar, still largely in use.
The largest gorge in Italy, seen from above and from the bottom.
The history of the Anconetan Jewish community.
The church near Termini Station, the first architectural work by Gian Lorenzo Bernini.

Small church among the orchards of the valley floor, at the eastern entrance of Naturno, probably built at the end of the eighth century in honor of San Procolo, bishop of Verona. Inside a cycle of frescoes discovered in 1923, with angels, saints, the famous figure ... on the swing and a herd of oxen, among the oldest examples of pre-Romanesque mural painting of the Alpine arch; author and meaning of some images remain unknown and scholars propose dates between the 8th and 10th centuries, with the decorations of the triumphal arch more ancient than those of the nave.
Frazione can be reached only on foot by steps, with the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie in panoramic position on the sea and Villa Guariglia with its terraced park.

Museum spread in the historical center of Velva, with its headquarters in the ancient Oratorio dei Bianchi (used to worship until the early twentieth century) and in cellars, funds and domestic environments where the objects remain in their context. The sections illustrate agricultural and domestic activities, handicrafts, transport and commercial: workshops of the carpenter-boatmaker, the carter-mulker and shoemaker, beating of chestnuts, threshing, mills and mills. From April to the end of October open on Saturday 14-18. Tel. 0185 408016.
Among the most beautiful churches in the center.
Different summer and winter hours: check the website of the University Museum System

Large karst cave in which the river Lete flows under the ground, explored by the cavers from the twenties of the twentieth century, with stalactites and stalagmites; on the opposite side overlooks the valley. The waters cross Mount Favaracchi and fall into the waterfall in the Rava di Prata before joining the Volturno.

Among the typical dishes are the acquacotta, the frascarelli with ricotta cheese, the gnocchi with beans and the breadcrumbs, pasta with chickpeas, rosemary and tomato served on breadcrumbs; the giant cake is enjoyed at the feast of the patron Saint'Edisto, in October, with historical procession. On the last Sunday of May the Madonna of May brings the torchlight with bundles of reeds lit on the side of the mountain.
The Roman ship re-emerged from the sea.
A Gaginesque Madonna and a 12th century candlestick.

The emporium of the ancient Gela on the south-eastern slopes of the hill, systematically explored in recent times: there are two medieval furnaces, the site of a military camp and the remains of a large residential quarter of the fourth century BC. The Museum of Greek Relics is located there.
From Carthaginians to early Christians.
Two centuries of observations of the sky and climate.

Church built in stone in 1290 by the Camaldolese monks of the abbey of Santa Maria di Sitria and extensively renovated between 1442 and 1480: the lower part is Romanesque in stone, the upper Gothic in brick. He preserves works of the Marche school including a Madonna and Child in heaven between St Andrew and St Michael the Archangel (1581), a Madonna of Mercy between St Nicholas and a holy bishop (16th century) and a Sedes Sapientiae (1442). Open by day, free entrance.
The parish church of the valley, already existing before 1228.
The town cathedral, built in 1938, houses a work by Guercino.
The bridge wanted by Cosimo I in 1555 on the Sieve and the municipal palace with the frescoes of the Room of the Heroines.
The museum church in Gothic style, with frescoes, among the sights of the village.

Today, in the area of expansion of the city, until the 1950s, it stood among large olive groves. It contains well-readable frescoes, including a deep apse of great expressive power, and an almost intact iconostasis. It is part of the guided tour of the rock churches.
Beat iron and country memory.

Gagini's triptych.
The rock mushroom symbol of Aritzo.
The four oratories of the village: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Saint Martha, Our Lady of the Visitation and Saint Andrew.
Thermal establishment in the park along the Sillaro.
A walk between walls, loggia and the door of Vignola.
The ferruginous water.
The village above the sea.

Garden of medicinal and aromatic herbs with hundreds of varieties (culinary, aromatic, perfume, medicinal, ornamental perennials), present since 1986 in the agricultural estate next to the abbey and recently expanded.
Sea and pinewood with the delta behind it.
The iron age tombs on the hill.

Borgo del Vallo di Diano dominated by the Certosa di San Lorenzo, the largest monastic complex in southern Italy and UNESCO heritage since 1998; in the village the birthplace of Joe Petrosino and, at the Fonti, one of the oldest early Christian baptisteries in the West.
Silvers, artist jewelry, design and fashion inside a Visconti castle.
The village that gives its name to the winery "Bandiera Arancione," in the UNESCO wine landscape of the Langhe, collected around the castle of Falletti.

Its seat is in Palazzo Tafuri, also known as Villa Picciotti, an eighteenth-century residence with an almost octagonal shape, once the residence of a noble Gallipoli family. It preserves one of the most important archaeological collections on the Messapians, with funeral sets, balsamaries, trozzelle and divinities in terracotta; in front of the museum there is the archaeological park.
The Romanesque granite of the Gallura Giudicale.

A watchtower among the largest in the territory, erected against Saracen raids: square base and large access staircase on three arches, the last recently added because originally the staircase ended with a drawbridge.

In the complex of San Benedetto, from the prehistory of the caves of Polla, Pertosa and Palinuro to the Greek settlers; the strong piece is the bronze head of Apollo fished in the gulf in 1930, on the upper floor the finds of the necropolis of Fratte.
The sanctuary of the patron, between Gaggini and between Umile from Petralia.
The oldest square in the city, with the cathedral, the portico De Catiniano, the loggia of Palazzo Balsamo and the Archaeological Museum.

Renovated on the project of Gae Aulenti: on the first floor the brothers Dino, Mirko and Afro Basaldella with a cycle of frescoes by Afro, on the second the Astaldi Collection with Morandi, Martini, Mafai, Guttuso, De Chirico and Savinio, and the Friam Collection with De Kooning, Lichtenstein and Frank Stella; temporary exhibitions on the ground floor.

The recent Neolithic "sepulturas de zigantes" (3500-2700 B.C.). Ladas, the most imposing of the four dolmens of Luras, is a tunnel about 6 meters long and over 2 meters high, covered by two large slabs and closed by an apse; the back cover plate measures about 15 m2. Next to it is Ciuledda, smaller and semicircular, on a granite bench overlooking the Limbara; from both come ceramics of the third millennium BC. Ladas can be reached with a walk of about 15 minutes from the village.
A church saved from the water, stone for stone.

Next to the parish church, in the most panoramic point of the village, rises on the foundations of the castle with local stone masonry; next to barn and stable the municipality has created a multifunctional space that also enhances the typical products. Opposite, on the other side of the street, the noble Quarone Palace.
The plain of Ravenna as it was before the Bonifice.
Liberty Ceramics in town.
The fortress of the thirteenth century on a spur of limestone, of the Salimbeni in the Three and fifteenth centuries, where St. Catherine also stayed: he controlled the south of the Sienese State.
The abbey of 726.
The theater of figure, good with children.
The stone staircase, the scenic heart of the village.

Born as watchtower at the end of the thirteenth century, castle Orsini (stone of 1373) and noble residence in the present form since 1464, with porticoed courtyard with octagonal columns of pepper; from 1661 of the Chigi, with cardinal Flavio who created a museum of curiosity. Re-opened in 2011 after 25 years of restoration, it hosts the MAV (established in 1992), which tells the territory from the necropolis of the Iron Age to the Etruscan age, to the Roman conquest of Veio in 396 BC and to the feuds Orsini and Chigi; the rebuilt steel tower Corten by Andrea Bruno has a staircase with multimedia settings and views of the Agro Veientano.
The ancient coins.
A show inside a quarry.

Expanded by the oratory in which Francis dressed Blessed Lucio Modestini; facade of the late sixteenth century with memorial plaque and wooden statue of the Black Madonna of Loreto, which replaces the original stolen by Napoleonic troops at the end of the eighteenth century.
The Romanesque of Monferrato.

In the basement floors of the palace, now the headquarters of the Municipal Archives, there are still cell doors, numbers and graffiti of prison use until 1965; they can be visited seasonally, with evening visits to small groups; not accessible to disabled people.
The most celebrated beach on the coast.
The tomb of the "Swan of Catania."
The life of the valley.
A mountain sanctuary accessible only on foot.
House-museum with over 4200 books, furniture, handicrafts, paintings, sculptures and drawings.

Byzantine castrum of the IV-V century with phases up to the XII, border castle between judged, perhaps the castrum Asonis cited in 1189 and restored by Eleonora of Arborea in 1389; the name There are still sections of walls, a cistern and two towers, surrounded by vegetation, on a cliff halfway between Samugheo and Asuni. Asphalt road up to about 500 meters, then on foot or off-road in the woods.
The history and traditions of Val Canale.
Fireflies in June.
Farmer's job with a view of the lake.
House where the composer was born in 1774, declared a national monument in 1924; it retains the essential aspect of the dwelling of his childhood.
A missing Roman city, rediscovered.
