Perhaps the oldest church in the town, of medieval origin, was a mother church for about four centuries; here the feudal lords swore, from the Crisafi in 1392 to Orazio Bonanno in 1504. At the Latin cross, it has a Gothic portal on the transept and over 450 metres of frescoes rediscovered under the plaster; on the altar the sixteenth-century wooden statue of the patron, carried in procession every 1st September.
Aemilia Ars funerary art.
The church on the cliff.
The castle of the hanging gardens.

The seaside town of the Gulf of the same name was born as a steel pole: the former Ilva area with the MAGMA museum and the Library of Ghisa, the church of San Leopoldo with the cast iron pronao and the Etruscan site of the ovens of Rondelli; sandy beaches and the pine forest of Boschetto.
Navene is the last village before the old Italian-Austrian border; from here starts the path to Bocca Navene, a panoramic terrace overlooking the lake.

Traditional farmhouse of the Parco delle Capanne di Marcarolo with exhibitions and multimedia facilities on the local life and economy; the roof is made of chestnut wood, around centuries-old chestnut trees, fruit trees and a new orchard of ancient local varieties of apples, pears and plums. It has a theater in nature that in summer hosts shows and meetings.
The sanctuary on the gorges.
A single nave church open to worship in 1710, already home to the brotherhood of the tailors, whose statutes date back to 1344.
A panorama that goes from the Apuan to the Gran Sasso.
The cathedral on Piazza IV Novembre, with the Capitolare Museum that houses, among other works, the fourteenth-century triptych of Meo di Guido da Siena.
The view on the Vallesina.

Karst cavities in the Cambrian limestone of Mount Meana, about 6 km from the village on SP 70 towards Teulada: discovered in the sixties, when they were marble quarry, and explored in the seventies for 1,650 meters, are open to the public since 1985 with a path of about half a kilometer and a visit of about an hour, at 16 degrees constant. Cross the Theatre Hall, the Room of the eccentric with the vault covered with aragonites that grow in every direction and the Sala dell'organ, where a crib is set up at Christmas; at the entrance there are traces of the Sardinian Prolagus, an extinct rodent.
A whole country painted on the walls.

The village of Ciociaro on the slopes of Mount Cairo, founded in 996, overlooking the Liri Valley: in the plain it preserves the archaeological area of ancient Aquinum, home of Giovenale, with the Museum of the city of Aquino and Lake Capo d'Acqua; on Mount Asprano, the remains of the castle of Castrum Coeli and the church of Santa Maria Assunta in Cielo.
The treasure of a queen of Spain.
The industrial history of sulphur.
A piece of Florence on the square of the village.
The small national park, for children.
The round village with sharp roofs.
Small theatre on the north-western walls, built in the mid-eighteenth century on the remains of a fifteenth-century church and recently restored.
Walk on the dam, in front of the landslide of the Knock.
A miniature 19th century theatre.
A bathroom in Lake Iseo.
A large villa of brianzola delight with gardens on several levels, to be taken at the FAI openings.

Borgo della Bassa Atesina sulla Strada del Vino, with Roman origins and a portico center of about 500 meters built between the fourteenth and seventeenth century along Via Andreas Hofer; among the main places the Museum of popular culture, the church of San Nicolò and, above the village, the hamlet of Mazzon with the vineyards of Pinot Noir.
Michelangelo and Leonardo in the same castle.

Wet zone in a circle of morainic hills, born in the Quaternary from an ice lake then become swamp and filled by vegetation transformed into peat; at the edges typhus, reeds and horseback rides. On its banks stood a Neolithic village of stilts, whose traces were discovered in the nineteenth century. Managed with the Montana Community of Valcuvia, it has protected observation points and educational panels.
Panoramic terrace of the Castello district, reachable on foot, ideal for photos and sunsets with views up to the district of Stampace.
Sorso's most heartfelt devotion.
The highest point of the village, overlooking the Valdarno.

Small rural village of Marmilla, mentioned in 1346 as "Silli" at the foot of the Siddi Jar: among the main places the tomb of Giganti Sa Dom'e s'Orku, the park of Sa Fogaia with its nuraghe, the Romanesque church of San Michele, Casa Steri and the Ornithological Museum of Sardinia.
At the beginning of the road to the valley of Cervo, the vast secular park of the Sella family.

Built on a project by Pietro Del Fabbro between 1933 and 1939, in Romanesque style with three aisles, he replaced the ancient archpriest's bell tower in 1955, of which remains the bell tower in Piazza della Vittoria. It preserves a Madonna with Child on a table dated 1505 by Francesco Vecellio (maybe four-handed with Tiziano), paintings by Pietro Marescalchi and Antonio Lazzarini and a wooden case by Andrea Brustolon.
Ruins in the pines.
Just outside the historic centre, symbol of the power of the Marchesate, it houses a masterpiece by the Flemish painter Hans Clemer.
Rural life and memories of war in a noble palace.
Walk in the Majella Park.

Small church of the sixteenth century on the main square of the village, at over 600 meters above sea level, where on August 12, 1944 the Nazis killed hundreds of people, especially children, women and elderly, and burned the bodies with the benches of the church.
It shows how the flour processing cycle used to take place; it is open at fairs and by reservation.

At the highest point of Toffia, built in the seventeenth century on the site of the Palace-Castle of the Columns: the bell tower reuses the male of the castle and the apse one of its towers. Originally a single nave, then divided into three naves; it preserves a Virgin with the Child of Carlo Maratta school and a round with the Virgin and Child of the Florentine school of the fifteenth century.
Daunia's painted graves.
A thousand-year-old abbey among the Sibillini.

Example of late Baroque architecture, built in 1838 on the ruins of the ancient convent. The canvas of San Domenico is venerated there, with the book on the right and the lily on the left: according to legend, it was handed over to Fr. Lorenzo da Grotteria Maria Maddalena and St. Catherine of Alexandria, between 14 and 15 September 1530. Free access, with platform for those who have difficulty walking.

Sanctuary of pilgrimages near Tagliacozzo, existing already in the sixteenth century, with the thirteenth-century icon of the Madonna dell'Oriente, according to the tradition brought by Ravenna; the Eastern Museum holds ex-vote, Byzantine icons, sacred furnishings and Middle Eastern coins.
The wheat salon.
A painted audience with its imaginary audience.
Remains of the amphitheater built in the 1st-II century A.D.
The green gold of Reggio.

Around 1270 there were already a small castle and two farms, then incorporated into the castle of Moos; Moos and Schulthaus had different lords and were renewed in the Three and fifteenth centuries, until the estate passed to the von Schulthaus for marriage. In 1958 he bought it and restored the Bolzan merchant Walther Amonn, whose Foundation (1982) owns it; museum since 1983. Buildings of the 16th and 17th centuries with unpainted walls, a tower on the northeast corner, wall paintings, a Gothic-style stube, vintage tools, an exhibition room and the 14th century chapel, of which since 1988 a room has returned to its original use. Open from Tuesday to Sunday, guided tours by reservation, usually between 11 and 16 (info@moos-schulthaus.it, 0471 053906).

Artificial basin created in 1954 for the electricity of the neighbouring countries, with a Roman archaeological area on the south bank; above the lake the castle of Pievefavera, of the thirteenth century.
It preserves a large canvas with Saint George coming down from horse between Saint Anthony Abbot and Saint Anthony from Padua.
The main church of Grimaldi, dedicated to the saints patrons Peter and Paul; it houses sacred works of art, ancient frescoes and decorated altars.
The two majolica bell towers.
An 18th-century ducal oratory in the center.
The fourteenth-century cathedral of the village.
An architecture of Bramante outside Rome.
In the fourteenth century Palazzo Neri Orselli Etruscan and Roman finds, paintings of Sienese school, Filippo Lippi and Sodoma and Robbian terracotta.
Just outside the centre, it is dedicated to the flora and fauna of the Apennines Dauno and organizes educational excursions (tel. 329 0826352).
From the prehistory of the gravina to the ceramic laertine.
The queen of the Orobies.

It is located in the sixteenth-century monastery of San Benedetto and exhibits architectural elements and statues of the ancient marble furnishings of the cathedral, partly rebuilt, bronzes, paintings of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and sculptural groups from various town churches. Guided tours available.
The memory of the water and the washbasins.
The Black Madonna and the view of the gulf.

In the former convent of San Francesco, remodelled several times, it houses a specialized library on southern Italy and a photographic archive with works by Henri Cartier-Bresson, Arturo Zavattini, Mario Carbone, Mario Cresci and Antonio Pagnotta.

Built in 1284 with the support of Paganello II, Bishop of Lucca, in the Tuscan Romanesque style (the brick arch in the façade remains), it was rebuilt and enlarged in 1719 with baroque stuccoes; on the side a sandstone panther recalls the Lucca domination. Inside the fifteenth century baptismal font, a marble Saint Peter and the two polychrome wooden statues of the Annunciation of the Pisan school of the thirteenth century (attributed by Visit Tuscany to Nino Pisano), a crucifix of the fifteenth century very venerated, the Resurrection of Tabita by Cosimo Gamberucci and St. Peter in prison by Alessandro Allori.
Two steps through the districts after the museums.

The village of Alto Vastese is over 1,000 meters away, with its medieval historic centre, the Mother Church of San Michele and, in the territory, the Madonna del Monte complex on the ancient fiefdom of Lupara and the WWF oasis of Abetina di Selva Grande.
paid
The reliquaries of the Holy Spina.

Medieval village at 430 meters in the Fiastra valley, with spiral streets, staircases and stone houses connected by small overhangs: the Leonina Tower of the sixteenth century, the church of San Michele Arcangelo and a vocation of  "city of contemporary art" with a gallery of more than three hundred works and sculptures scattered in the village.
Ancient Longobard settlement near the Castellano stream.
A walk along the river.
Medieval village walled above the valley of Crevole, between Val di Merse and Val d'Arbia, in a land of Etruscan sites.
A medieval castle intact in the countryside.
The walk on the ramparts with a wonderful view of the Langhe and the Alps.

Borgo dell'Alto Molise at about 1,200 meters, overlooking the whole valley of Sangro and known as the village of the stone for its historical maestros chiara chiara chiara Marinelli, told by the Museum of the Stone; around woods of white fir, red fir, beech and cerro, with the rock hermitage of San Luca.

During the golden age of the marquisate of Saluzzo, the painter Pietro da Saluzzo, called Maestro del Villar, painted the apse of the church of San Giovanni and the ancient pylon in front of it (frescoes of the pylon of the XV century) and also worked in the chapel of Sant'Anna. The chapel of San Rocco conserves frescoes from 1534; the chapel of Santa Brigida, with Romanesque apse, was frescoed in Saluzzo by unknown artists.
Museo civico, also accessible with the ticket together with the Chapel of San Severo and the complex of San Bevignate.

Probably born in the fifteenth century with the union of the parishes of Industria and Monteacuto, it was set on fire by the Spanish troops in 1625 and rebuilt between 1631 and 1636 with the stones of an ancient house, whose ruins with a stone coat of arms of Monteu are still visible. Baroque with three naves, has the main altar in seven types of polychrome marbles, a fresco of the Nativity in the choir and a baptistery in carved wood.
The portal with the choir of angels.

The municipality of Val Passiria and a member of the Alpine Pearls, with the hamlets of Corvara, Plata, Stulles and Plan: in a bunker of the Second World War the Bunker Mooseum tells the valley, the Nature Park Tessa Group and Monteneve mine, while around the village the waterfalls of Stieber and Stulles fall.
The only rest of the castle built under Ruggero II, of the 12th century, in limestone; restored with the green light of the Superintendence of Trapani, it returned to use in January 2024.
Aironi and the river along the Po.

Municipality of the province of Isernia in the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, made up of 12 villages distributed over three valleys from the basin of Filignano to the first buttresses of Monte Marrone, with paths between dry walls, votive newsstands in majolica and ancient stone straw; in Cerasuolo the church of San Pasquale Baylon, rebuilt after the Second World War.
The view of the countryside stops.

From 1440 to 1826 a strip of land born from a border error between the Papal State and Tuscany was an independent republic, where tobacco was cultivated from 1575; the Scroller Path crosses it remembering the times of smuggling.
Medieval tower-house, already seat of the bishop's jurisdiction, with next to the seventeenth-century chapel of the apparition of St. Michael.

The main cultural centre of the country, in 1944 was the seat of the government of the Free Zone of Carnia and Upper Friuli, the territory that was liberated for a short time from the Nazi-fascist occupation; today it houses a photographic-documentary exhibition on the Resistance.

Small village about 1,050 meters in the upper Valle del Gizio, on the historic Via della Lana between Sulmona and the Piano delle Cinquemiglia, crossed by the Tratturo Celano-Foggia; it preserves the medieval structure with loggias and 'viginali', the ruins of the castle above the Castelluccio, the Palazzo Fidei, the parish church of Santa Maria Maggiore and, outside the village, the rural church of the Madonna del Casale.

In addition to the Duomo, the center preserves the Gothic church of St. James (13th century), restored with the former convent of the Augustinians; St. Francis, with oval portal of the fourteenth century; Santa Maria Assunta, the church of the Kings Magi and Saint Andrew, with Baroque interiors; and the eighteenth-century church of the Tintes, with Greek cross with octagonal dome.
The last door of the village.

Dedicated to Saints Peter and Stephen, it is the oldest church in Cistercian Gothic of Marittima and Country, built between 1150 and 1170 after a presence of Basilian monks; tradition binds it to the Templars and wants the architraves to crack in 1314 at the stake of Jacques de Molay. Façade with 12 columns rosette, XII century capitular hall and square cloister with the palindrome
Clear alpine lakes for trained hikers.
The pots dug by the glaciers.
Walking in a city designed by artists.
The history of a city of Magna Grecia.
Frescoes of the fourteenth century in a country sanctuary.

The ancient Fanum Fortunae, where the Via Flaminia arrives to the Adriatic: the Augustus Arch of 2 AD and the Roman walls, the basilica designed by Vitruvio re-emerged in piazza Andrea Costa, the Palazzo Malatestiano with museum and gallery, the Pala di Perugino in Santa Maria Nuova and the beaches of Lido and Saxony.

The wall erected in 1630 by Urban VIII north of the Fort, to separate the port from the city, rests on buildings of the Roman port and preserves the fisheries in opus reticulatum. The travertine fountain of Luigi Vanvitelli, commissioned in 1740 by Benedict XIV and completed in 1743, depicts the head of an old faun in a canopy with curved tympanum; the complex has been recently restored.

Canyon of about 300 meters excavated by the Pollina River in rocks of the upper Triassic (about 200 million years ago), site recognized by the network of UNESCO Geoparks; a 400 steps path descends to the river bed and nearby there is an equipped area. Visit Sicily offers boat excursions in the gorges.

The centre preserves elegant palaces, squares, medieval fortifications, the ancient city walls and alleys that descend to the river, between Castle and Tower of the People. From the station start in summer the panoramic carriages of the historic Sebino Railway towards Paratico-Sarnico.
Permanent exhibition of relics of the Second World War dedicated to the Battle of Filottrano in 1944; open every Saturday from 10 to 12.30, free entrance (curator Giovanni Santarelli, 071 7222576).
The Romanino in a Lombard Gothic cathedral.
The Palaeontological Museum of Asti, in the Palazzo del Michelerio.
A macabre curiosity of the village.

It opens on the top of the hill of Sant'Angelo, in the district Serra degli Angeli, about 3 km north-west of the village along the SP 110. Digged into the white-blue limestone, it penetrates for about 50 meters; at the bottom have been found bone remains in advanced state of fossilization and fragments of ceramics of various eras, and the traces of numerous early Christian frescoes testify to its use as an ancient place of worship.
To be seen together with the GeoMuseum, in the same complex.

Built in 1854 at 1257 meters, where stood a fortress or watchtower of Roman times (there were found vases, bones and flints); a hut façade with large ogival window, in limestone of Lessinia and red marble of Verona. You can reach it on foot from the cemetery; enter only in summer or on the occasion of some celebrations, with Mass on the first Sunday of August.

Built at the end of the 11th century in the agricultural district of San Vincenzo, it is considered by the municipality the real jewel of the area; it was used as a lazaret during the epidemics, the last of cholera in 1884. Inside frescoes in part of the 15th and 16th centuries with the three Kings Magi; it preserves burials and is the object of archaeological excavations with guided tours. In 2026 the extraordinary free openings were held on the first Sunday of the month from April to October.

Center of the Piné Plateau, a few kilometers from Trento at the foot of the Lagorai, with the lake of Serraia and the nearby lake of the Piazze (Blue Flag), the biotopes of the Laghestel and the Sternigo Paludi, the parish church of the Assunta and in Montagnaga the Sanctuary of the Madonna di Piné, the most visited Marian destination of Trentino; in Miola the Ice Rink Piné, an ice stadium with a 400 meters ring.

It arose around the 10th century against the incursions of Saracens and Ungari, was expanded several times and settled definitively by Maurizio di Savoia; in 1794 the French troops dismantled it and today remains the ruins.
Mills, bridges and dry docks of a secluded valley.

On the edge of Rupingrande, a typical rural house of the Karst, perhaps two to three hundred years old, with the current appearance of 1831 and restored in 1968: roof in stone slabs, kitchen and cellar on the ground floor, bedroom and barn on the first floor, furnishings, tools and costumes of the nineteenth century donated by the inhabitants. In the summer barn are held contemporary art exhibitions and events; every two years, at the end of August of the odd years, it hosts the karst weddings, re-enactment of a Slovenian wedding rite of the late nineteenth century. From April to November open Sunday and holidays 11-12.30 and 15-17. It is also an information point of the reserve of Monte Orsario.
The castle of accounts.
Typical structures of the Garganic coast once used for fishing, today transformed into small restaurants suspended on the Adriatic.
The treasure of the Collegiate and the history of the country.
The sorority dairy.

The fourteenth-century church above San Leonardo with the only cycle of frescoes in the valley: scenes from the life of St. Ippolito of 1380 of a Giotto influence, attributed to the school of Bolzano and perhaps commissioned by Hiltprant von Passeier, arrived only in part; on the south façade a Saint Christopher and the coat of arms of the lords of Passiria. Cocci found near the church suggest a place of votive fires of the late Bronze Age. It can be visited only from the outside, with ample view of the valley.
The venerated fresco and organ of 1780.
A path equipped inside the canyon excavated by the stream, which goes up to the castle passing over cliffs with views of the valley.
The civic and diocesan museum in the former monastery of Santa Chiara.

Alleys, cordonades and squares with views of the valley of Sacco and Rome; there you enter from two open Urbian gates in the walls. The village was set in 1953 to "Pane," love and fantasy" by Luigi Comencini, with Vittorio De Sica and Gina Lollobrigida.

Città sul Metauro heir of the Roman Forum Sempronii, with the Corte Alta built by Federico da Montefeltro which houses the Museum and Pinacoteca civica, the Quadreria Cesarini Museum House, the Logge of Corso Garibaldi, the Ponte della Concordia and, just outside, the Marmitte dei Giganti.
The daily life of a cloistered monastery told by the objects.
The main shopping street, which starts from Piazza Bra towards Via Cappello and Casa di Giulietta.
Public washbasin fed by the resurgences of the area, recently restored and still used by the women of the country to wash the clothes by hand.

In Piazza Garibaldi, facade with black bands and large sculpted rosette; the bell tower was a sighting tower, in the bezel an eighteenth-century fresco of the Baptism of Jesus and inside, renovated in the Baroque age, the baptismal font.

Borgo 60 km from Rome founded in 1560 by Giorgio Santacroce according to a planned plant, collected around Palazzo Altieri, manorist palace-villa with the gallery of portraits of all the Popes; around the Sabatini Mountains, the Faggeta of Monte Raschio, UNESCO heritage since 2017, and the Natural Monument La Mola on the Mignone.
The baroque that dominates the city.
The end of the tragedy.
The feast of St. Anthony riding.

On a promontory overlooking the sea to the west of Capo Carbonara, about 3 km south of the village: to the first polygonal nucleus, probably Aragonese, the Spanish added a complex with four towers, three of which pointed, with walls with two entrances and internal courtyard, in defence of the barbaric incursions of the port of Capo Carbonara and the mouth of the river; restored at the end of the eighteenth century, was abandoned in 1847. Outside, the permanent exhibition "Enemigos de la fe," pirates and coastal defenders, on the assaults on the Sardinian coast between the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries; from the wounds you can see the towers of Capo Boi and Porto Giunco and the lighthouse of Capo Carbonara.
Ancient castle on the Via Francigena on the border between Val d'Orcia UNESCO and woods of the Amiata, with the Fortress of Tentennano and the thermal baths of Bagni San Filippo.
Stone houses gathered around the parish on a hill between vineyards and olive groves, with a wide view; the village is a frame for re-enactments like the traditional Festa delle Fae.
The starting point of the boat tours on the canals and rivers of the city.

The precious village of stone: palaces of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, narrow alleys with small arches, balconies-barn, workshops dug in the rock and ancient fountains, among newsstands, icons and ancient Spanish inscriptions. In Palazzo Dionisi the visitor center of the National Park.

A circular village on a hill in the Valle d'Itria, with white houses with sharp roofs in \cummerse Â Â, a panoramic balcony overlooking the trulli countryside, the Mother Church of San Giorgio and the church of Santa Maria la Greca.

Gorge of the river Rocciamelone close to the village Foresto, starting point for excursions to the Rocciamelone, with rock gyms, a via ferrata and the Ginepri Path (about an hour). At the entrance of the Orrido, leaning on the right wall, the Lazaretto: stone construction that according to tradition in the seventeenth century housed the sick with plague. Open all year round; you leave the car downstream and walk about 500 m along Via Gran Borgata.

Impressive castle about six kilometers from the center, going up the valley of Carpina north-east, restored and restored to the ancient splendor; according to a tradition, perhaps invented by Braccio, was founded in the early Middle Ages.
Tourist land among the largest in Calabria, with a two-armed overflow pier that contains a dock with floating docks.
The masterpiece of the Gothic Angevin in Calabria.
The cromlech pass.
Well preserved medieval village, a few hairpin bends from Elici, overlooking the sea. The fairytale village in August hosts the Fairy Festival.
At about 1,250 meters, isolated under Mount Infornace, where according to tradition he retired Colomba, Countess of Pagliara.
Borgo della Valle dell'Esaro gathered around the medieval castle on the hill of Motta, with the Parish Museum of Archaeology and Sacred Art "Don Fiore Borrelli" in the Mother Church.
The church dedicated to the Benedictine nun patron of motorists, canonized in 1608, built in a cell of the Temple of Venus and Rome.

Founded in 1980 by the Paleontophilo Fidentino Group: in three fossil rooms of the Stirone stream, shells of molluscs, sea stars, remains of whales and plants, which tell the geological history of Parmense. Times to check with the museum.
The valley that grinds.

In Piumazzo, the sanctuary was born from a terracotta image of the Virgin on an elm to a crucifix: the oratory of 1817 was replaced by the current sanctuary in 1927. The Oratory of San Colombano, considered the oldest place in the village (VII century), was rebuilt by the Boccadiferro in 1559 and preserves a fresco of the Crucifixion recently rediscovered.
A crucifix signed in 1396.
A city under the city, between barrels and shelters of war.

A fourteenth-century villa overlooking the homonymous square, with a chapel dedicated to Blessed Emilia di Vercelli (1238-1314), Dominican nun of the Bicchieri family who founded a small convent in the surroundings.

The matrix church, born in the eighteenth century as a chapel of the Rosary and remodelled several times: altar of Our Lady of the Rosary, processional statues and bronze portals with saints, scenes of the life of Christ and Marian scenes.

Walled village built after the Mille, 180 meters with 360 degree panorama: clock tower with ancient mechanisms, Gothic parish church of Santo Stefano and church of Santa Lucia (1485); at the end of the year it hosts "Candles in Candelara."
The miniature village inside a liberty palace.

Romanesque church, the most important church of the feud of Vernio, documented since 998 and in the current forms probably of the XII century, with medieval facade and porch on columns of the XVI-XVII century. In the single aisle baroque altars in sandstone, a Deposition of 1579 by Giovanni Bizzelli with the coat of arms of Cardinal Girolamo de' Bardi and a Madonna of the seventeenth-century Rosary; in canonical a Adoration of the Shepherds of Girolamo Ristori.

Terrace at 212 meters on the slopes of Monte Poro, overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, the Aeolian Islands and the Strait: the castle Ruffo, the Cathedral, the ancient Giudecca and the marina with shallow and clear waters.
With the frescoes of the Canavesio.

Hill east of the village with a village of the Copper Age, excavated by the brothers Cafici (1879), which gave its name to the culture of San Cono-Piano Notaro; the hill was frequented until the Byzantine era and preserves a Christian-Byzantine necropolis, of which today there are few tombs.
Walk through a Roman tunnel still in use.
Built in 1876 in the ancient ghetto, after the demolition of the previous in 1860; open to the public on Memory Day.
Three hundred headwear in uniform.

Convent and adjacent church erected between 1625 and 1635 at the behest of the Marquis Francesco Castromediano and his wife Beatrice Acquaviva, who then donated them to the friars. Today it houses the school of excellence ISUFI of the University of Salento and the direction of the Museo Diffuso.
The large Franciscan basilica of the San Polo district, among the unmissable stops of the city.
View of the plain.
Autumn colors on the pass of the Park.
Antonio Zanchi's paintings.

Romanesque-Gothic church of the 12th century (Italy.it indicates the fourteenth century); the façade was restored in 1999 for the 9th centenary of the deposition of the Holy Nail in Torno. It has a fifteenth-century marble portal and paintings from various eras on the walls.
An author's waiting room.
A century of mountaineering and tourism in Solda.
Church in Via Bottai with the altarpiece of Martin Knoller, between the historical stages of the center along with Via Argentieri and Piazza del Grano.

Nusco rises on a narrow ridge between the valleys of Ofanto and Calore, from which the name of the "balcony of Irpinia" is named; from Porta Molino and via Coste you can enjoy wide views of the surrounding mountains.
The view from the "balcony of Romagna."
You can disassemble and reassemble a knife.
The largest Italian public collection of contemporary photography.

In the seventeenth century Collegio dei Jesuiti, with works from the Renaissance sculpture to Mannerist and Baroque painting: the section of sacred art exhibits works saved from the churches damaged by the earthquake of Belice of 1968, including pieces attributed to Domenico Gagini and Francesco Laurana; the archaeological section finds from the excavations of the territory. A wing reconstructs the Holy House of Loreto with frescoed vaults.

The narrow streets paved with Roman stones, small squares, arches and wooden passages and the Urbian gate; in the medieval walls mosaic benches are set with flowers, birds, ducks and cats, the work of Rosina Wachtmeister and grandson Giovanni Battista Rea. On the main square the sculpture "Il Momento" (9 meters) by the Hungarian Ervin Lorianth Hervé, a man leaning on a building that looks at the landscape.
€20, reduced €15 (3-12 years, over 65 in weekdays, groups over 20 people)
The 19th century theatre destroyed in war and rebuilt as it was, reopened in 2018.
The fossil sea of Monte Baldo.
The oldest church in the country and its medieval festival.
Sea for families with pinewood behind them.
Opened after eleven years of closure for the 2012 earthquake: 120 works, 46 drawings and 20 frescoes by Guercino, with Scarsellino, Guido Reni and Ludovico Carracci.
Country between apple orchards and vineyards at 731 meters with two castles: the fairy-tale with four turrets and the Sarriod de la Tour with the "sala delle teste" (sala of heads).

Inaugurated in 2010 on the noble floor of Palazzo Mannacio, it has three sections: historical documents, especially of the municipal administrative activity; sacred art linked to local devotion, including a viatic piss in copper and silver from 1598; rural and social life with agricultural and craft tools, instruments of the ancient town band, domestic objects and trunks of emigrants. The route is accompanied by vintage photographs of the twentieth century and images of the territory, such as the medieval ruins of Pendino. Open Monday and Friday 9-13, Wednesday and Thursday 15.30-18.30.
The popular museum of the people of Lucca.
To the north, beaches between white cliffs and sea bottoms suitable for snorkeling.

Wooded hill of 452 m between Lake Bertignano and Peverano, known for its prehistoric finds: the ruins of a stone fence, the Castelliere, suggest a use in the Iron or Celtic Age, perhaps later adapted by the Longobards as a viewing place. At the top an erratic rock with a smaller stone at the base, to which some historians attribute a ritual use. You will pass the Grand Crossing of Biellese.
Nature along the river.
The church of Valadier in the village.
Privately owned and used as a summer home, it is not normally open to visitors: for visits to municipal offices (open in the past during the open castles)
Villa and romantic park fed by thermal waters.
The State Museum of Etruscan and Faliscan Civilizations, with finds especially from southern Etruria.
The village is located inside the park, with numerous paths and outdoor activities in all seasons.
The diocesan museum and the garden of the Bishop's Palace, venue for concerts in the summer season.
Walk on the bottom of the gorges dug by glaciers.

Narrow and winding streets with ups and downs and passages with a tunnel, between palaces and palazzotti of the Seven-nineteenth century with granite portals, coats of arms and decorations of the families Massara, Amoroso-Aceti, Basile and La Grotteria.

Park Visitor Center at 1005 meters dedicated to the Marsican brown bear, symbol of the Park: museum with panels, bulletin boards, dioramas and temporary exhibitions, projection room with naturalistic films, 3D station on fauna, space for children and picnic areas. Along the Nature Path you can see a bear in semi-freedom in a large fenced area.
The Franciscan church of the village, to be reviewed at the reopening.
The museum dedicated to the Florentine champion, along the Via Chiantigiana in the district of Gavinana and Galluzzo.

Opened in 1979 in the former farmer's house behind Villa Stampa and reopened on May 25, 2024 after the restoration, he exhibits relics and documents lent by Casa Manzoni and by the Rosminian Fathers of Stresa on Manzoni, Teresa Borri, Stefano Stampa and Rosmini, the legacy of Giulio Carcano (poet, translator of Shakespeare and among the first biographers of Manzoni) with the reconstruction of his study and bulletin boards on the fortune of the Promises married. Open from May to September on Friday 16.30-18.30, Saturday and Sunday 10-12 and 16.30-18.30 (closed on 15 August); in other periods on request at 345 1577649.

Borgo dell'interra anconetano surrounded by walls with medieval gates and towers, with nine castles scattered throughout the territory. In the centre the Collegiate Church of San Medardo houses the only altar of Giovanni Della Robbia in the Marche region, and the complex of San Francesco houses the State Archaeological Museum.

Small village perched on a cliff above the lake, birthplace of writer Francesco Jovine, born in the Lombard period around a Roman tower; the historical walled center runs along the ridge to the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, with its bas-reliefs, the crypt discovered in 1975 and the Holy Door linked to the indulgence granted, according to tradition, by Leo IX in 1053.

In the plain about six kilometers south of Lodi, two kilometers from the South Adda Park, Mairago preserves the Cascina Grazzanello, typical closed court of Lodi documented already in the cadastral map of 1723, today didactic and eco-friendly farm with the old mill, and the Provincial Astronomical Observatory inaugurated in 1999 in the former kindergarten.
17th century frescoes in the heart of the village.

The Retrone is located in the hills west of Vicenza: it houses a megalithic complex of the Copper Age, churches with works by Orazio Marinali and Francesco Maffei, Venetian villas from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century and the natural tunnels of the Spurghe di Sant'Urbano.
A 16th-century church in the square.

Country of the woods in Val di Sole, on the road of Passo del Tonale, where from June 1915 to October 1918 the White War was fought: the Museum was born from the collection of Emilio Serra, together with the Fort Strino and the other Austro-Hungarian forts of the Tonale system.
The villa of the emperors in the cemetery.

Chapel authorized in 1625 and built in the manner of the Loreto house, flanked in 1720 by a building for spiritual exercises and then by a porch. Since 1896 it was the mother house of the Sisters of Santa Maria di Loreto, who bought it back in 1988-1989, restored and transformed into a center of spirituality. Inside a wooden statue of the Virgin in a glass niche.

Built by the Orsini in the 13th century as a fortress to control the territory between Salaria and Nomentana, it was purchased in 1626 by Barberini who, at the impulse of Pope Urban VIII, transformed it into a ducal residence; then passed to the Grillo and Boncompagni-Ludovisi and today it is the seat of the Municipality. The rooms of the noble floor, decorated at the behest of Cardinal Franciotto Orsini, have the myth of Adone attributed to Girolamo Siciolante da Sermoneta (about 1553), the Stories of Joseph the Jew, frescoes by Giacinto Calandrucci and a view of the city painted by Paul Brill in 1581. The tower was rebuilt after the earthquake of Avezzano in 1915; in the courtyard a marble cistern of the sixteenth century, the Swan Garden and the Cippo-Ossario garibaldino.

The Arch of the Earth, the ancient main door of the village in front of the staircase of the Mother Church, has on the outer wall a stone head that could portray a feudalist; next to the church the Palazzo Marchesale, also wanted by Bartholomew III. From Piazza Vecchia start the "stréttole" alleys built with Lombard technique, with portals, columns and bas-reliefs of the mastri chiselellini.
Partially accessible
A poor material that decorated the ceilings of Monferrato, in a panoramic castle.

Deep and wild gorge at the entrance of Val d'Ultimo, with walls of porphyry quartz, gneiss and granite, where the Valsura flows; fresh in summer, with lush vegetation. The walk of the Gaul starts from the bridge over the Valsura in Lana di Sopra on wooden bridges to the meadow under Castel Braunsberg and a waterfall (about 20 minutes). Always accessible; in winter ice rink in the throat. Do not go down into the riverbed: the level can rise quickly.
Civic museum dedicated to the history of the city, which can be visited together with the Pinacoteca civica.

Sequence of large squares connected by long arcades (1987-90), designed by Franco Purini and Laura Thermes around Piazza del Comune, whose portico is by Vittorio Gregotti and Giuseppe Samonà; symbol of the city is the civic tower of the clock of Alessandro Mendini. Through the streets of the village murals and works of Schifano, Cascella, Pomodoro, Paladino, Angels, Accardi and Rotella.
A shrine porticoed in the countryside.

Small chapel of the 13th century built on a large granite mass, where according to tradition in 1227 two Franciscan friars found the bodies of the hermits Nicola and Trano. The cave in which the saints lived is embedded in the wall and acts as a natural apse above the altar, made from a single block of granite; a single nave, granite floor and a roof with exposed beams. On clear days you can see the mouths of Bonifacio and Corsica; at the beginning of June the saints are celebrated with an evening procession.
The most famous image of the city.
The symbol of the city on the hill.

The regional park, established in 1989, covers about 18,000 hectares between the valleys of Tiber and Aniene; the main peaks are the Pellcchia (1,368 m) and the Gennaro (1,271 m). From Palombara Sabina starts the classic ascent to Monte Gennaro: difficulty excursion E, about 900 m of difference in altitude and 6 hours, between holm oaks, storace and Judas tree to the beech forest; from the summit the 360 degree panorama embraces Soratte, Rome, Roman Castles, Circeo and the nearest Pontine islands.
The Naples that is reborn.
To understand May, the most famous ritual of Acceptura.

In the ancient bishop's palace, born as a fortress and residence of the bishops from the second half of the thirteenth century, restored in 2018: sacred art from the early Middle Ages to the contemporary of the dioceses of Feltre and Belluno, about 250 works including the cup of the deacon Bear (VI century), considered the oldest Eucharistic chalice of the West, a post-Byzantine cross of 1542, a Madonna in alabaster of the fifteenth century, the reliquary bust of San Silvestro by the Florentine goldsmith Antonio di Salvi and works of Tintoretto, Sebastiano Ricci, Luca Giordano, Andrea Brustolon, Gaspare Diziani and Domenico Corvi. Open from Friday to Sunday (June-September 9.30-13 and 14.30-19; October-May also holidays, 9-13 and 14-18).
The sacred art of Asola, with the Moretto.
The church founded in the ninth century where it was believed to have been crucified St. Peter and, in the cloister, the circular temple of Bramante (1502-1509) with 16 granite columns.
Vesuvius at sunset with black sand.
The heart of the walled village.
A medieval village dug into the rock.
A small nineteenth-century theatre still in operation.
Since 2013 in the medieval palace in front of the Duomo, enlarged in the sixteenth century and decorated at the beginning of the twentieth century.
The flea market.
A bench to look at the valley.
12th century church that preserves frescoes of the school of Paolo da Visso.

In Piazza Lauretana, in front of the church of Our Lady of Loreto, a stone of Roman times slightly oval (about 110-135 cm of diameter, 20 thick) used as a bank to conclude business: coins were beaten there, judged good by sound.
Roman baths overlooking the lake and the sea.
The shop house overlooking Erbe Square.
The cellars of Rosso Conero a stone's throw from the sea.

In the Renaissance monastery of Sant'Agostino (1439-66), the Cremasco recounts from prehistoric times to today with archaeological finds and documents, the reconstruction of rural life of the late nineteenth century and the industrial past; it has a painting gallery from the seventeenth century to today, a large collection of works by the architect and stage designer Luigi Manini and one of the most important Italian collections of pirogues, found in Adda, Oglio and Po. In the ancient refectory, frescoes of the Crucifixion and the Last Supper by Giovan Pietro da Cemmo.
The baroque church of the Trivulzio, cradle of the Missionaries.
Malaria, the enemy of the pontoon marsh.
The peasant house in which the friar poet was born.

Church of the 14th century restored between 1513 and 1529 by Nicolò Bonafede (1464-1534), bishop of Chiusi, as a family mausoleum. On the high altar the Crucifixion of Lorenzo Lotto (1531), on three levels, with the client in prayer on the left; also late-fiveth century frescoes of Durante Nobili, pupil of Lotto, a stone Pietà of the fifteenth century and a Madonna of Trapani attributed to Nino Pisano. Hours: every day 9-12 and 16-19.
From the village to over 3,000 meters by cable car.
7th century church with 14th century frescoes, among the best preserved Romanesques of Ravennate.

The capital of the plateau on the Trentino side of Monte Baldo, in the Natural Park, called by the botanists ...Giardino d'Italia...: Palazzo Eccheli Baisi with the Fossil Museum and the Botanical Garden, the church of Saints Peter and Paul with the Romanesque crypt, the Zeni Mulino alle Sorne and paths through flowery meadows and trenches of the Great War.

City of the largest salt pans in Europe, which run for about 20 km parallel to the Adriatic and are a natural reserve since 1977; in the center of the sixteenth-century torrione, the Historical Museum of Salina and the thermal baths that use the mother waters and the sludge of the salt pans.

Lyrics on the Ionian Sea at the foot of the hill of Roccani, called "Costa dei Lili" (Costa dei Lili) for the rare marine lilies growing on the dunes: almost white sand, crystal clear green sea, eucalyptus behind. Monument to the battle of 24 June 1859: the 64-metre-high tower, with statues of the protagonists of the Risorgimento, frescoed ramp by Vittorio Emanuele Bressanin and panoramic terrace on the lower Garda, the morainic hills and the plain; behind, the museum with weapons, relics, documents and objects of the soldiers; along the avenue the Ossario Church with 1,274 skulls in the apse and the remains of 2,619 fallen in the crypt. Centre of Baronia on the gulf that bears its name, with a historic center of seventeen consecrated churches, the tower of Sant'Antonio with the church frescoed in the fourteenth century, the district of Palatzos Betzos with the Museum Don Nanni Guiso of miniature theater and a coast of beaches that goes from Marina di Orosei to Cala Liberotto to the oasis of Bidderosa.

Borgata di Olbia on the granite massif of Cugnana, near the Costa Smeralda, born in the late nineteenth century around a small country church and called "the village of the artists": houses in Gallura style in pink granite, square with atelier and artisan workshops. Villarosa, at 523 meters of altitude, was founded in 1762 by Placido Notarbartolo-Zati as San Giacomo di Villarosa, with a regular plant centre along the Garibaldi course and Corso Regina Margherita; its economy was linked to agriculture and then, between the end of the nineteenth and mid twentieth centuries, to the sulfur mines. The main monument is the Mother Church of St. James Major, 1763.

The town square is dominated by historic buildings: the Palazzo della Meridiana, the old eighteenth-century hospital, Palazzo Fieschi and the church of San Pietro. The village, with traces of settlement from the fourth century BC, passed in 1242 to Genoa, which infeudated it to Spinola, and at the end of the thirteenth century to the counts Fieschi of Lavagna; from the mid nineteenth century became a holiday destination of the Genoese families.

It was built on a large rock, probably in the eighteenth century: the hammer moved by the water of the river Nembo produced the tools of the village. Salt town since 798 and then the salty waters: the Berzieri Thermal Baths and the former Grand Hôtel des Thermes decorated by Galileo Chini, the fossil museum of the ancient sea in the Stirone Park and the Pallavicino castles on the hills.

A site stratified with helimal, Hellenistic-Roman remains of Muslim, Norman-Svevian and medieval era: Segesta, the main city of the Elimi and rival of Selinunte, was destroyed by Agatocle of Syracuse in 307 BC and rebuilt as a Roman city. Outside the walls stands the Doric temple of the fifth century BC, with 36 columns and remarkably intact; on the top of Mount Barbaro the Hellenistic theater (mid III century BC), with the cavea partly dug into the rock, which in summer hosts classical shows, music and poetry, even at dawn. You can also visit the two acropolis, the Vanella Cave linked to the shrine of Contrada Mango, the quarries of the temples and the remains of a Hellenistic necropolis. Here Matteo Maria Boiardo, author of the Orlando in love, was born, and Spallanzani experimented in the underground; the frescoes of Nicolò dell'Abate with stories of the Aeneid were detached at the end of the eighteenth century and are today at the Galleria Estense in Modena. An ancient church porched on the road to Niella Belbo, once a stop for travellers and lazzaretto during the epidemics. The fortress that dominates the historic center dates back to the Longobard domination. The Torre dell'Orologio, the ancient tower-gate of the castle, has a Gothic coat of arms of 1324 and exterior decorations of Lorenzo Luzzo (1518) and houses the "Window of Time" multimedia installation on the evolution of the square since 1510; the Torre del Campanon, about 34 meters high, has the first stages of late-Doromanic construction. Parish Church of the diocese of Benevento, built between 1656 and 1688. It has an isolated bell tower: on its south side is walled a marble plaque at the fallen of the two world wars, with a bronze disc depicting Victory as an armed woman in a laurel crown; the upper part recalls the 27 fallen of the Great War, the lower gravestones of the 25 of the Second World War, gathered in 1976.

Originally a convent church dedicated to Santa Maria la Nova, with an imposing façade in stone cones and bell tower with Arabic-style dome. The main work is the great wooden crucifix attributed to Fr. Umile da Petralia: according to tradition on 1 October 1656 the face of Christ turned and the country was freed from the plague. It preserves a Madonna and Child by Antonio Stabile (dated 1580 from the regional portal) and an Immaculate with a 18th century monk attributed to Domenico Guarino.

Basin in the heart of the National Park with centuries-old trees, pastures, streams and waterfalls that in winter become ice sculptures, crossed by the Path Italy and the Parks Way. Borgo about 915 meters between the Ionian Sea and the Aspromonte, capital of Bovesia, the Greek area of Calabria where the Greek of Calabria is still spoken; under the ruins of the Norman castle it houses the cathedral with the Madonna of Rinaldo Bonanno, the church of San Leo, the museum of Paleontology of Aspromonte, the museum of the Greek-calabra language "Gerhard Rohlfs" and a steam locomotive in the square.

Built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries against the rocky wall and remodeled in the seventeenth century, it has a spectacular fifth with columns and volute pediment from which a waterfall descends for about three meters in a semicircular tub. It probably rises on the source Bandusia celebrated by Orazio; a more ancient tank in front of the basin could be Roman. You can reach it with a short walk in the woods from the Villa di Orazio.

Original nucleus of the seventeenth century on a previous structure, Baroque facade, central nave with golden wood vault and side naves with domes; in the crypt, ancient burial place, some frescoes have recently emerged. It preserves the polyptych of Simone da Firenze (1520) with the statue of the Madonna del Polittico in the center, coming from the destroyed convent of Sant'Antonio, a statue of the Assumption of a Venetian school donated in 1522, a painting of Sant'Anna with the Madonna of an anonymous Neapolitan master of the early fifteenth century and the wooden choir of the nineteenth century wanted by the archpriest Correale.

Born on the initiative of Maestro Francesco Scerbo, collector of ancient objects: at the entrance numerous tools including a press for olives, then tools and objects of common use, small handicraft machines, masonry tools, blacksmith and carpenter, and rare photographic and literary documents.

Outdoor museum along the river in the valley (Thal): the water-powered forge with a long canal, the Schiassermühle that produced marbles, the Matznellermühle, the Thal-Mühle on the side of the hill and the old saw of Stampfer. An easy 3.5 km ring (about one hour, suitable for strollers) starts from the fire station, touches the biotope Möserwiesen and the Maria Schnee chapel; on Saturday in summer the Museum Association guides the visit and runs the mills.

Built from the 13th century and never finished, slightly raised on Piazza San Marco, with brick facade and fifteenth-century bell tower; inside the Pordenone altarpiece, the frescoes of the Montereale Mantica chapel of Calderari and Amalteo and sculptures of Giovanni Antonio Pilacorte.

Born as the Po Museum, for the finds and fossils returned from the river, it documents today the natural environment of the whole Oltrepò Pavese: geology with minerals, rocks and traces of gold of the Po, a small anthropological section with human and fossil remains of the Paleolithic and Neolithic, a large paleontological section with mammals of the Pleistocene found in the Po, plant and animal species of the territory, collections of butterflies and snails, an area on bees and silk bugs and reconstructions of environments and climates. An easy ring of 2 km (about 40 minutes, 141 m of difference in altitude) that starts from the central parking lot of Varna under the parish church of San Giorgio and goes up the river Scaleres along the right bank, with wooden walkways, an ancient chestnut and the first original Kneipp tanks of South Tyrol, with water path, playground and lawn; we return to Salern along paths 6 and 20.

Light sand and low seabed for tens of meters, suitable for children; the sea is calm because sheltered by Capo Falcone, the Piana Island and the Asinara rocks. Next, the Pelosetta, closed by the islet with the tower. It's better to be here soon.

Built in the second half of the 15th century by Ferdinand I of Aragon on the western side of the village: quadrangular plan with two cylindrical towers, the major (Maestra Tower) of Angevin age (1380). Here Gioacchino Murat, landed at the Navy on October 8, 1815 to regain the Kingdom of Naples, was imprisoned and shot on October 13 ('Mirate to the chest, not to the face'). Inside the Museo Murattiano reconstructs the environment of those days; managed by the Municipality in the Civic Museums of Pizzo.

Last great work of D'Annunzio, who lived there since 1921 and donated it to the State in 1930; built with architect G. C. Maroni between 1921 and 1938, includes the Priory (the house, which can be visited only with a guide in about 35 minutes, with a library of 33,000 volumes), museums, park, auditorium, the open air theatre with 1,500 places with summer events, the ship Puglia and on top the mausoleum where the poet is buried.

Stone bridge started in 1442 on a natural boulder in Natisone's bed: 22,5 meters high and 48 meters long, with two arches of 22 and 19 meters; destroyed in 1917 during the retreat of Caporetto, it was rebuilt in the same form in 1918. The legend wants it built with the help of the devil.

Fortified enclosure of the end of the 12th century, enlarged in the 16th and the second half of the 17th century: the main tower, about 19 meters high and now bell tower, was restored between 1990 and 1995; two original doors and three towers transformed into houses remain. Baroque church of the historic center. It preserves the Robbiano altar commissioned in 1510 by two Sienese hermits for the hermitage of St. Jerome and completed in 1513 in the Florentine workshop of Giovanni Della Robbia, its only altar in the Marches, transferred here in 1870; also two painted statues of St. Catherine and of the Magdalena (rare terracotta robbian not glazed), a glazed Crucifix of Mattia Della Robbia and perhaps a nativity scene of the workshop of Hercules Ramazzani.

Città della ceramica del Canavese, where the processing of the red earth developed at the end of the eighteenth century with the first stoves "Franklin": the Unfinished Round by Alessandro Antonelli, the neo-Gothic parish, the ceramic museum of Palazzo Botton, the Stove of Ugo Nespolo and the remains of the castle on the hill.

In the early Middle Ages, the abbot of Montecassino built the defensive castle of Castrum Cerbari on Mount Trocchio, next to the castle of Torrocolo (VisitLatium indicates 1057); together they controlled the Cassino plain. According to tradition, the name of the village derives from a herd of deer, or from a white deer, which grazed on the height of the 'pesculum', now home to the castle.

The only permanent exhibition of this kind in Lazio and among the few in Italy: over forty costumes made by Beatrice Minori, costume designer RAI born in Serrone in 1923 and assistant to Eduardo De Filippo, who donated them to the birthplace; many were worn by Eduardo, Gassman and Beppe Barra. The itinerary "Il costume," the actor, the character" is divided into two rooms, from the Renaissance to the eighteenth century and from the nineteenth to the twentieth century, with captions on work, author, interpreter, character and year. Open Saturday 16-19 and Sunday 10-19.

In the square built on the site of the ancient castle, it has a fourteenth-century terracotta portal surmounted by the coat of arms of the confraternity and frescoes of the sixteenth century, including a Madonna and Child of the Pagani.

Of a first building of the XII-XIV centuries there are few traces left; the castle was created in the XV-XVI century, was unified by Guido Aldobrandino, who completed the works in 1726 eliminating the central tower and giving the east a façade with three avant-corps crowned with tympanians and balconies. The castle was almost completely demolished at the beginning of the 19th century and replaced by an English garden, where a glories of the early 18th century remains. Privately owned, it is the venue of events: visits by reservation (contact@castellosangiorgio.it).

In the hamlet of Coloti, about 8 km from the center, in a village today uninhabited: opened since 2000, it has a telescope under a dome of 7 meters, twelve rooms, the former church of the village used as meeting room and the Sala Sirio for events.

The castle, of Longobard character with last great reconstruction at the end of the fifteenth century attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini, houses in six rooms the history of the Caudina Valley and the furnishings of the necropolis of Caudium (mid VIII-III century BC), with attic and italian vases and materials of Saticula and Telesia; the most famous piece is the crater of Assteas with the rat of Europe. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 9-19 (last entry 18.30).

Probable military garrison already in the Lombard age, passed to the Castelbarco and in 1441 to the Venetians; since 1977 it is of the FAI, that has restored it. You go up among the vineyards on the slopes of Mount Vignola to the tower "Picadora" where the condemned hanged themselves; the frescoes of the Verona school include the "Parata dei combatti" in the House of Guards and the courteous "Room of love" in the mast. In 2026 open from 14 February to 4 October at 10-18 (last entrance 17), then reduced hours until December; free entry with Trentino Guest Card and Museum Pass.

Residenza dei Trinci, lords of Foligno from 1305 to 1439, then of the papal governors: the loggia and rooms of the liberal arts and planets frescoed by Gentile da Fabriano in 1411, the chapel painted by Ottaviano Nelli in 1424 and the Sala dei Giganti; it houses the art gallery, the archaeological museum and the multimedia museum of the rides with the original wooden statue of Quintana.
Opened in 1988, the first museum in Italy built for avant-garde art, with over 1,000 works by 300 artists; expanded by Maurice Nio with a futuristic form.

On the acropolis of ancient Lagaria, linked by Strabone to the legend of Epeo, stood a sanctuary of Athena with construction phases around 700 BC and in the middle of the VII century BC; the cult of Athena was joined by that of Pan and the Nymphs, then the sanctuary was probably destroyed by the Brettii and in the tenth century there was built a Byzantine chapel. The site is still under investigation and has no defined visit routes.

The castrum Plage already appears in a bull of Pope Anastasio IV of 1154; the fief passed from Riva to Roero, who held it until the end of the eighteenth century, then to the Faussone of Clavesana (1829), to the Genoese Raffaele Bombrini (1880) and finally to the Cross of Doiola. The present, huge 18th-century castle dominates the village and is surrounded by a park with a geometric garden; there are regularly held antique bars. Visits by reservation, also guided in Italian, English and French; from March to May it opens for the event "Narciso Incantato" .
Brixellum, the Roman Brescello on the Po.

Walled village with walls and towers and a geometric road system between Porta Parma and Porta Romana, along Via Bertoloni and Via Mazzini on the ancient route of Via Francigena. Sarzana is one of the capitals of the antiques; here on October 6, 1306 Dante Alighieri appeared before the Sarzano notary for peace between the Malaspina and the bishop-count of Luni.

Built by the community since 1750, in devotion to the Immaculate Church, where the monastery of San Pietro in Monte was built, and consecrated in 1839; the ceiling was decorated in 1928-1929 by the Brescians Vittorio and Giuseppe Trainini. On the high altar the Blessed Virgin with Child by Pietro Ricchi, known as the Lucchese, on the Nativity and Visitation sides of Francesco Maffei (1647), behind the altar the ciborium of Andrea Solarius; in the room next to a museum of parish works and sacred objects, with a canvas signed "Camillus" perhaps by Camillo Procaccini.

Classical stone façade, a single nave with four chapels on each side, a table of the Madonna with saints attributed to Genesio Galtieri, two wooden organs and in sacristy furnishings of the XVI-XVII century. Not far away is the Old Fountain, fountain and washbasin of 1816 with a surviving marble mask, next to the old Town Hall.

At the entrance to the historic centre, the Renaissance oratory with frescoes painted in 1535 by Saccino Saccaccini da Carpi.

Country residence of the sixteenth century transformed in the eighteenth century into a noble villa of delight, with U-shaped structure around the courtyard of honour, Rococo and Baroque decorations, trompe-l'oeil and frescoed vaults; in the salon and gallery of the noble piano paintings of the Milanese Salvione and Bosso. The Italian garden rises on four terraces connected by stairs with balustrades, statues and fountains, up to the lawn of the theater closed by an eighteenth-century fish pond; in the park also the Filanda. Late medieval bell tower of the 15th century, born with civic and defensive functions and linked to the first town hall, later became bell tower of the nearby parish church of San Cassiano; in the 18th century hosted a telegraph. Visitable only on occasion of events.

Built by Enrico II to defend the village, it formed with Cengio, Cosseria and Roccavignale a defensive quadrilateral on the road between Piedmont and Liguria; stone tower and eastern walls are the oldest parts.

Square brick tower about 47 meters high, with walls 1.75 meters thick, only surviving part of the medieval defenses of the village; according to tradition it was spared when Frederick Barbarossa destroyed the castle in 1186. On the promontory overlooking the Costa dei Trabocchi, it was founded in 1015 by the will of Trasmondo II, Count of Teate, buried in the crypt, on a small monastic cell documented between the VIII and the X century; the name would recall a Roman temple of Venus of which only the place name remains. The present aspect is due to the work of Abbot Odorisio II (1165-1204) and Abbot Rainaldo (1225-1230): the portal of the Moon, with the bezel of Christ enthroned between the Baptist and St. Benedict and the stories of St. John the Baptist, is crossed by the sun at the sunset of the summer solstice, while at the winter solstice the light enters from the apses (Porta del Sole). Inside three aisles, raised presbytery and crypt with frescoes from the middle of the thirteenth century close to the workshop of Jacopo Torriti; the 13th century cloister, partly rebuilt in 1932-1935, retains the inscription of Odorisio II. Today the Passionist Fathers live there; open every day according to the MiC card (April-October until 20, November-March until 19), guided tours by reservation.

Municipality of the lower Foglia valley born from the union of Sant'Angelo in Lizzola and Colbordolo: the hamlet of Montefabbri, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the walls and parish church of San Gaudenzio; the castle of Colbordolo, home of the painter Giovanni Santi; the sixteenth-century Mulino di Pontevecchio with the Museo della Mezzadria and the remains of the bridge on the Foglia.

In 1610, in 1692 it became a female convent by initiative of Chiara Foscarini Duolo and the parish priest Francesco Lantieri de Paratico, with the church of Santa Maria degli Angeli consecrated two years later and reopened in 1835 with the arrival of the Orsolines. Designed in 1985 by the director Maurizio Corgnati for his native country, he initially invited twelve frescoes: today he has 115 works, mostly frescoes on the exterior walls of the houses, as well as abstract paintings and sculptural forms, by many artists including Piero Gilardi, Eugenio Comencini, Mauro Chessa, Bert Van Zelm and Klaus Munch. You can visit freely, without timetables or tickets; in 2025 you can visit Sundays from July to October (10-12, 15-18).

It preserves a fresco of the Last Judgment dating from the 14th to the 15th century, restored with a contribution from the Lazio Region and presented to the community on September 30, 2026, the first major intervention on the work after more than thirty years.

Campestre church in Biddanoa, zone of mineral springs and thermal baths: the Byzantine circular central body of the VI-VII century, about 7 m high and 10 m wide, covered with dome, rises on a Roman thermal building and preserves traces of the water system; the oldest parts are in opus listatum of bricks and black basalt. In the 11th century it passed to the Benedictines of Montecassino, who added the apse and a compartment to the north. Feast on Monday of the Angel; a trail of almost 6 km leads to Monte Santo.
