In 1935 Count Vittorio Cini restored him and furnished him with Gothic and Renaissance furniture and a rich armory; since 1981 he has been from the Veneto Region. In the Library are the Antiquarium Longobardo and the Museum of Rareness Carlo Scarpa. Open every day except Tuesday, with guided tours.
A wild valley of Grappa between paths and paraglidings.
To be seen especially during the Christmas period.
The sky from an observatory that studies the planets.
To be combined with Sa Domu 'e s'Olia in the land of oil.
The wandering church at the end of the valley.
Green giants a stone's throw from the walls.

Pieve documented since 1184, built between 1165 and 1183 and assumed its current appearance in 1588, probably on a project by Pellegrino Tibaldi; in 1621 it had the title of distinguished collegiate. It has five aisles with the central one on ten large granite columns and facade never completed; the portal of 1183, signed by the Magister Albertus, has in the bezel Samson that rifts the jaws of the lion and David that saves the flock, with capitals to grifi and scenes of the seasons. Inside paintings by Pietro Grassi, Tirsi Capitini and Francesco Mensi, the Last Supper by Alessandro Berri and, in counterface, the Madonna of Mercy of the fifteenth century attributed to Quirico Boxilio da Tortona.
An hermitage with ancient rules.
Between San Patrizio and Conselice, it recreates the original environment of the valleys with wetlands and woods.
One of the most famous legends in Tuscany.
Piazza con il bronzo di Ovidio by the sculptor Ettore Ferrari, of the early twentieth century.
The nineteenth-century paintings by Giulio Musso and a altarpiece of the Moncalvo school.
The scenic square of the village.

The villas in the center were built by the noble families of Milan as holiday residences, with the façade facing the village and the park towards the countryside; the owners called artists and architects known for monumental staircases with balustrades and painted or stucco ceilings. Among the other Villa Frisiani Olivares Ferrario, Villa Borri Manzoli, Villa Massari, Villa Mereghetti and Villa Pagani della Torre. On the first Sunday of May the Pro Loco organizes the walk among the villas, when gardens, historic buildings and churches open to the public with guides.
The smallest island of the archipelago, part of the UNESCO site, with remains of ancient monastic settlements.
Walk in a Roman aqueduct dug into the rock.
Seaside town with fishing port, beaches and promenade and, 4 km inland, Civitanova Alta, medieval village within the walls of a castle, home of Annibal Caro.
An underground world in the Sambughetto quarry.
The beach of the house, a few steps from the center.
The historical elevator loved by the poet Giorgio Caproni rises from Strada Nuova to the esplanade, overlooking the rooftops of the historic centre.

In front of the parish, the only waterfall of Sardinia in a town: fed by the Funtana Manna resurgence, it jumps for about seven meters and disappears in sa Bucca manna, a cavity that can be visited with a stone path, to emerge about 150 meters below.

Isolotto of the municipality in front of San Pietro, historical seat of the trap: granted to Don Francesco Pes at the end of the seventeenth century and renewed in 1898, the fishing ceased in 1964 and the village of the tunarotti is now a residence. No cars, motorcycles and bicycles: it is a reserve where they nest the queen's hawk, royal seagull and friar.

Founded in 1702 in the place where the Augustinian nuns lived since 1517; in the works of 1755 the façade was designed by Francesco Valeriano Dellala of Beinasco and the main altar by Gioachino Felice Buttrini. Inside stuccoes and ten stories of the life of Mary frescoed by Carrera. Owned by the municipality since 1978.

Built from 1606 by the will of the Duke Charles Emanuele I of Savoy after the destruction of the Angevin castle, it preserves frescoes and wooden ceilings of the eighteenth-eighteenth-century; King Charles Albert lived several times its noble floors in the first half of the nineteenth century. A gallery dedicated to Carlo Alberto, built by Count Borelli in the second half of the nineteenth century, connects him to the nineteenth-century park with four terraces with fountains, caves and greenhouse. It houses the Documentation Centre Lalla Romano, the Porcelain Museum and the Civic Library; guided tours on pre-established dates, by reservation (tel. This appropriation is intended to cover expenditure on the implementation of the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF).

It exhibits minerals and rocks from the mining area of eastern Liguria and northern Apennines, sorted by extract element and type of mine, with samples from the mines of the provinces of Parma, Modena, Piacenza, Genoa and La Spezia. An ancient miners' trail (about 2.5 km) connects it to Gambatesa. Tel. 0185 338876.
The Florentine fashion in the square.
The large protected forest of Alta Irpinia.
Ammonites, dinosaur footprints and the cave bear.
The crenellated loggia and the stone ramp.

Pleasant square with the 18th-century parish church, which behind the main altar preserves a large nineteenth-century mache group of the Saints Martyrs, and the Baronial Palace of the sixteenth century built on previous structures, with next to a more ancient tower.
A medieval hermitage in the valley of Sant'Angelo.
It overlooks a deep gorge almost at the border with Issime, reachable from the regional road.
The medieval cathedral and the Feast of the Assumption.
A sanctuary born of a snowfall in August.
In the former monastery of Santa Chiara, the finds of the Roman city of Vercellae.

Built by the Knights of Malta in honor of their patron, with a small hospital annexed to it today disappeared; according to legend it was commissioned together with the church of the Madonna del Verde.
Church on a panoramic hill, reached by a staircase; next to the oratory with sports field.
Visits to verify.
The village of the Eucharistic miracle on the Via Francigena, overlooking the largest volcanic lake in Europe.
In Sant'Alberto, the naturalistic museum of the Delta and starting point for guided tours of pine forests and oasis.
The two churches of the village, built in the 12th century and then remodelled. The visits are organized by booking by phone through the municipality.
A former vote of the Risorgimento.
Church just outside the village with a cycle of frescoes in the apse attributed to Antoniazzo Romano; in May the feast of Sant'Antimo is held.

Municipality of Costa Verde famous for the dunes of Piscinas, up to 60 meters tall, and for the knives \'arresojas Â Â: in the territory the abandoned mining village of Ingurtosu, the complex of Montevecchio shared with Guspini, Mount Arcuentu and the Museum of Sardinian knife.
In the north-west suburbs, houses, squares, temple and necropolis of a colony first Phoenician then Carthaginian, preserved in an intact way as in few other places.
To be checked (for a fee, cumulative with other sites)

Inaugurated in 1996 by the then Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, it collects works of the churches damaged by the earthquake of 1980: the main seat in Santa Maria del Carmine exhibits sacred art, reliquaries, manuscripts and an Annunciation of Giaquinto; the section in the Bishop's Palace preserves memories of Sant'Alfonso Maria de' Liguori, the Hall of the Stemmes with the effigies of 68 bishops and a nape of 1997 by Giuseppe and Marco Ferrigno.

Three estimated 350-450-year-old cypress trees, near the banks of the Adige, in a public park; the largest is about 22 meters tall with 4.80 meters in circumference. Several times reported in the FAI census   •The Places of the Heart • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

In the hamlet of Castiglioni, about 420 meters between the woods, stands next to a monastery first Benedictine and then Franciscan; the parish church is mentioned in a document of 1599 and since 1963 is entrusted to the Capuchins of Offida. At the altar there is the statue of Saint Bernardino, very venerated, and numerous ex-vote; near are the ruins of a fourteenth-century church. Celebrations on May 20th and September 8.
The walls on the Piave.
Stone stairs and intact village.

Small village on Monte Barro of restored ancient buildings, some noble, other rural. The oratory of San Martino, with a single nave with an elegant arched porch, has as a altarpiece a canvas of Sant'Anna; at the entrance of the hamlet a large wall painting depicts St. Martin on horseback. On the day of San Martino is held the Office of the Secchia and blesses bread for families; near is the viewpoint of Punta Crabbia on the lake.

In the Castle of Charles V, in the barracks Undercampana and in the Tower Helping: tiles and ceramics of the historic center, coins, hunting daggers and swords of the eighteenth-nineteenth century, ceramics of Gerace, Seminara and Squillace, three colubs recovered at sea and the coats of arms of noble families.
Get into the huts six thousand years ago.

The municipality is known for the hamlet of Castelponzone, an ancient walled village linked to the Ponzone and the tradition of hemp rope, with sixteenth-century porticos, the church of Saints Faustino and Giovita, the Old Church and the Museum of Cordai.

The most important complex of the territory: dates back to the 10th century, it was given to the abbey of Montevergine around 1174 and since 1229 it entered the new farmhouse of Fontanelle, whose castle and fortifications are documented since 1094.
An isolated village between the meadows with views of two lakes.
Prepositural church with bell tower in the center of the village, which preserves a fresco of Ceresa.

In Badu Mela, on the northern slopes of Mount Deu, in the cork woods, dates back to the Middle-Recent Bronze (1700-1400 BC). In the territory also the sacred source of Li Paladini (II millennium BC) and the nuraghe Agnu flanked by a dolmen.
The great memorial of the fallen abroad.
Small tour €9, reduced €8; big tour €26, reduced €23
Home mosaics, not religious: another face of Ravenna.
Residence of the artist Asger Jorn on the hills of the village, with paintings, ceramics, sculptures and murals.

Palazzo di fine 18th century attributed to Carlo Andrea Pellizzari, today seat of the Municipality. On the stairs the tombstone to the fallen for the freedom of Giacomo Manzù (1957) with verses of Salvatore Quasimodo; in the council hall the frescoes of Luigi Vacca of 1810 with the Apotheosis of Enea. Napoleon stayed there several times.
The sea told in the plain.
The masterpiece of Gio Ponti.
The cultivation of lemons on Garda.
Small village near Drena with stone houses leaning against each other, inhabited by just 10 people.
Parish church with an ovoid plan with four chapels, rebuilt in 1777 instead of a church of 1528.
The round of the doors and rues.
The Templars in Perugia.
The only medieval castle in Sardinia still habitable, full of relics.
A trapezoidal building in the old town, built almost certainly in the early eighteenth century as the second residence of the notaries Trua, near the church of Sant'Antonio.
In the workshops of the dye shops of the former Cottonificio di Torre, interactive routes on natural phenomena and physical laws in six thematic areas.
Ponte del III secolo a.C. sul riu Mannu, on the border with Planargia and Montiferru.
The valley floor walk.
Juvarra's masterpiece.
The seventeenth-century church, together with the former convent of the Augustinians, was present in Morrovalle since 1308; most of the paintings of the Civic Art Gallery come from his works.
The green on the Noncello.

Surrounded for two thirds by a protected oasis of over 400 hectares, Castellaneta overlooks the Gravina Grande, one of the deepest in Puglia, in whose caves the peasants fled from the pirate raids; the historic center has the Cathedral, the Bishop's Palace and the medieval districts Sacco and Muricello, and the village is famous as home of Rodolfo Valentino, to which is dedicated a museum. On the coast, the fine sandy beaches and the pine forest of Castellaneta Marina.

The site of the most important Bronze Age of the area, of the fourteenth century BC, on a hill of 800 meters between oaks and holm oaks: pentalobed nuraghe of about 450 m2 with basalt mast of 14 meters of diameter and four towers, a village of about forty huts and an antemural about 70 meters long and tall 3, with walkway, almost intact. Parking is possible at the Scuderie Costa di Foresta Burgos and you can walk up for about 1 km.

An easy walk of about 10.5 km in 7 stages, in about 3 and a half hours, from Colonno to Cadenabbia di Griante: it follows at times the shore and the ancient Via Regina and crosses Ossuccio, Lenno, Mezzegra and Tremezzo, touching Villa del Balbianello, Villa Carlotta, Villa Mainona and the Park Levels.
Shopping like Parmesan cheese.

Marinar village among the most beautiful villages in Italy, grown with coral fishing: squares on the beach, the parish church of San Matteo with two majolica bell towers, the Saracen tower and Capo Mele with the Madonna delle Penne.
The royal forest of the Bourbons.
The Novecento italiano in a collection of country.
Five museums in one building.

In the Rabato, built in 1370 by Baron Giovanni Chiaramonte on the site of a mosque of about 875, of which it incorporates elements; renovated in 1585, it has a Renaissance portal and a marble baptismal font of 1495.
The carruggi and the lime kilns.
More stone giants.
Gothic and Borgna frescoes in the mother church.
The Liberty jewel described by Giuseppe Dessì.
From the Napoleonic wars to Francesco Baracca.
The Romanesque bell tower and the canvas of Giolfino.

Birthplace of the Renaissance painter Giovanni Battista Cima, gathered around the hill of Giano with the castle tower that houses the civic museum; along the portico Contrada Grande line up the Duomo with the Hall of the frescoed Battuti, Palazzo Sarcinelli and Piazza Cima with the Accademia Theatre. The municipality is in the buffer zone of the UNESCO site of the Prosecco hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene (2019).
An ancient wood between paths and fairy tales.

Villa of the early twentieth century with park, home of the Piccolo di Calanovella family: Casimiro, photographer and author of ... Magic watercolors, the poet Lucio and the botany Agata Giovanna. The cousin Giuseppe Tomasi of Lampedusa stayed there in the summer and wrote pages of the Gattopardo. The museum, opened in 1978, exhibits paintings, ceramics, ancient weapons, books, family portraits, photographs and cameras, letters of Tomasi di Lampedusa and a fortepiano linked to Lucio Piccolo. Hours: Monday-Friday 10-13 and 16-18, Saturday 10-13, Sunday closed.
The Bourbon symbol in the center of the city.
Among the best preserved monuments of Abruzzo.
From Solimena to Arcuccio inside the Norman cathedral.
The alley parallel to the sea.
1 h

Beaches of white, pink and green quartz grains, called "chicchi di riso" in the marine protected area Sinis Peninsula - Island of Mal di Ventre (about 26,000 hectares, established in 1997). The sand must be left on the spot.

Village on the Po in Mantovano, with the medieval towers of the castle, palaces and residences Liberty and an archaeological museum; around, the nature reserves of the Paludi di Ostiglia and the Isola Boschina and the cycle path of the former railway Treviso-Ostiglia.

In the palace built between 1668 and 1672 as a seminary, next to the Sasso Caveoso: sections of sacred art, Camillo d'Errico collection and contemporary art with the works of Carlo Levi, including the canvas "Lucania '61" .

Ice amphitheatre at about 1,000 meters, the greenest valley of the Park, between Monte Amaro (1,862 m) and Monte Dubbio, united by the Serra delle Gravare. Paths lead to the five springs of the torrent Fondillo, to the Briganti Refuge, to the Grotta delle Fate and to the Passaggio dell'Orso; from the Forest Museum the ascent to Monte Amaro takes about two and a half hours. In the reserve area of the valley there is the largest of the old beech woods of the Park inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage Site; in 1994 and 1996 there was dug a necropolis with more than one hundred concentric tombs. You can go on horseback or donkey, archery and rent mountain bikes.
A river castle with the Bacchiglione Museum.
The baroque church that closes the east side of Saint Francis of Assisi square, erected on a site occupied by an ancient pagan temple and a Franciscan church of the fourteenth century.
A huge museum in a park.
Green waters and paths in the Carnic mountains.

In the seventeenth century Palazzo Campeis, about thirty rooms on three floors tell the life and traditions of Carnia from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century: the traditional house with kitchen, rooms and dining room, carpenter's shops, blacksmith, battirama-octanaio and weaver, watches, ceramics, spinning and weaving, the hut, the world of cramârs, portraits, costumes, carnival masks, musical instruments and popular religiosity; outside the courtyard with loggia and garden with agricultural tools. The whole ticket includes the exhibition "Stories of herbs" until December 31, 2026; museum accessible with elevator. From October closed on Monday; it is part of the CarniaMusei network.

Rectangular building dated 1729, in Coletta locality about 1.5 km from the center on the road to Erbezzo, once used to transform milk: it preserves the original tools for butter and cheese and in summer it hosts workshops as a day as a housewife. Section of the ethnographic museum, open during the summer; guided tours by telephone reservation.

Borgo built in the Renaissance according to the model of the ideal city, on a project attributed to Maffeo Vegio da Como, with perpendicular roads set on the cardoon and decuman of an ancient Roman camp; it was small capital of the Pallavicino until the entrance into the Farnesian domains in 1587. Palazzo Pallavicino is private and can only be seen from the outside. Every first Sunday of the month there is the antiques market and the things of the past.
Three thousand years of peasant life in the plain.
Country of rose stone on the two sides of the landslide of the Toc.

The Morellino di Scansano DOCG, made from Sangiovese grapes, is one of the most famous red wines in Tuscany; wineries in the village and surroundings offer tastings, and Scansano is a stop of one of the wine roads of the Maremma. At the end of September the Grape Festival closes a month of tastings and open wineries.
Beach equipped to the west of the port, with shallow waters and a cove suitable for children; Green Flag 2022 according to Visit Sicily.
The castle overlooking the village.

It tells the life of the population in the twentieth century through the ancient tools to make wine of the Society Worker and the area, with attention to how we supported each other during the war and to the network of mutual help. Visit by reservation; accessible.

University city on a hill between the valleys of Potenza and Chienti, famous for the Sferisterio and its summer opera festival, with Piazza della Libertà, the Civic Tower and the museums of Palazzo Buonaaccorsi and Palazzo Ricci.
The cuisine of the lake offers roast corone, breaded tinca fillets, fried pike fillets or pike baked and eel hunter or wine.
Portals and masks in stone between the alleys.

Small single nave church with rustic façade on the promontory of San Sivino, a rocky spur near the lake; inside arches with all sixth hold the beams of the exposed roof. In the south wall is set the stone of the covenant, tied to the legend of a miller who around 1200 would sell the soul to the devil: there you can still see an engraved cross and the footprints of the devil's hand and foot.
A gathered cloister.
A relatively recent church that houses a martyrdom of San Lorenzo di Jacopo da Ponte (16th century).
The abbey of Gioacchino da Fiore, heart of Sila.
An 8,000-year-old canoe.

In the heart of Grecìa Salentina, where the griko is still spoken (the name itself means "good morning") Calimera preserves the main church of San Brizio, the House-museum of Rural Civilization and Grika Culture, the Greek funeral stele of public gardens and, just outside the village, the church of San Vito with its pierced stone; on the outskirts the Natural History Museum of Salento.
Snorkeling among red rocks a stone's throw from the village.
A quiet alpine lake with breathtaking views.

Karst cave on the edge of the residential district, about 160 meters long, of which about sixty accessible: used for funeral and religious purposes between 3200 and 2800 BC, gives the name to the culture of Ozieri, the first widespread throughout Sardinia.

Inaugurated in 2000 in the ancient hospitable of San Giacomo, it tells in three rooms the role of chestnut in the life of the mountain: tools for the care of chestnut trees and the processing, characteristics and diffusion of the species, diseases and grafts, the reconstruction of a chestnut grove and a section on chestnut in the Second World War with relics and documents. A flat path with 13 informative stages crosses the chestnut groves of Monte San Giacomo up to the woods of the Birch; in front, the Museum-Laboratory of Borlengo with a room to learn how to do it. Audioguides available.

Convent on the Monticello, beyond the Vallone di Sava, founded in the sixteenth century on medieval Franciscan roots: it preserves paintings of the eighteenth century, a Franciscan cloister and wooden sculptures of Nicola Fumo, native of Saragnano. It hosts the FRAC museum.
With the baptistery it forms the Romanesque nucleus of Agrate.
Masterpiece of the European Romanesque, where in 1155 Frederick Barbarossa was crowned.
The reason for the name "Santiago d'Italia."
The medieval market square at the end of Via Rialto, in the oldest part of the city.

Exposed houses of granite of barbaric type, many with wooden balconies, arranged amphitheatre on a slope at almost 800 meters of altitude. In 1388 Gavoi participated, with other centers of Barbagia, in the signing of the peace treaty between Eleonora of Arborea and John I of Aragon.

Housed in the town hall, it exhibits prehistoric finds of Cavaion, of the pond of Cà Nove and the nearby municipalities: ceramics, bronzes, dagger blades, bone and stone artifacts, amber, tablets and frame weights. It also preserves the remains of a necropolis and a Roman villa.
The ascent of the noble palaces towards the cathedral.

The only intact water mill in the municipality: the building is from the seventeenth century, it was part of the farm of the Palazzaccio, sixteenth-century villa of the Counts Orsetti, and it worked until the eighties. It preserves the original 19th century machines for grinding wheat, corn and chestnuts; from the eighteenth century the same water operated the mantics of the Galgani ironworks. It can be visited with educational activities.
Nature of gorge between Secchia and Po.
Walls at sunset.
Explores and on-board instruments on the lake shore.

Inaugurated on June 12, 1975 with Aldo Moro, in the Villa municipale exhibits the original frescoes of the crypt, detached and restored at the Central Institute of Restoration in Rome and mounted in the original layout, with the reconstruction of the plant: among these the Madonna and Child between the archangels Gabriel and Michael (first half of the XII century), St George on horseback, Christ blessing on throne, the saints Cosma and Damiano and the Archangel Michael.

Medieval village of the 14th century, 430 meters in the eastern Greek Sila, with narrow streets and passages and five historical churches; not far, about 8 km from the Ionian, the archaeological park of Castiglione, fortified Brettii with walls, towers and the East Gate.
Yesterday's Mamoiada, over the masks.
Casale Cathedral.
The prehistory of Tuscia in a Farnesian fortress with a panoramic terrace.
The cryptoporic under the municipality.
Medieval streets and a panoramic terrace on the Riviera del Conero.
Recommended guided tour, to be booked at the Tourist Office (tel. 0941 1946000).
In 1790, with the chapel of St. Nicholas founded by the De La Crête, ancient lords of Doues, who are buried there; the parish is already mentioned in 1176.
Large lake formed by the bends of the river Sesia, indicated as one of the most picturesque and less polluted places of Lomellina, with very varied flora and fauna; it is a nesting site.
The hill of the refuge from Barbarossa, with a wide view on clear days.

The other two Luras dolmen: Alzoledda, inside the town, is rectangular with trapezoidal chamber, over 2,5 meters long and over 1,5 meters tall, with the background wall formed by a single slab; Billella, between the Vermentino and Nebbiolo vineyards, is about 2,5 meters long and 80 cm high, with the cover slab shaped to fit the supports.
Probably a Lombard foundation, remodeled in the 12th century: the thirteenth-century Christ judge in the apse and paintings of Bernardino and Giulio Campi.
A full ride of the village.
View of the calanchi and the rooftops of the village.

Public pebble beach about 300 meters long in the gulf of the low lake, between Desenzano and Padenghe, framed by Monte Corno and the hills of Valtenesi; not equipped, with free access at every hour, with parking at a charge of about 100 meters and dogs allowed on the leash.

Centre for the reproduction and study of endangered species, with attention to Italian and European fauna and rarest cats; participates in conservation programmes. It is located in the peat bog of Conturbia, a protected regional area between ponds, woods and wetlands, where the excavations for peat have brought to light remains of stilts, ceramics and worked flints. According to the card of the Municipality is open from 1 March to 30 September, 10-17 hours, closed on Friday and from December to February.

At the entrance of the Piancastagna hamlet, the Shrine recalls the fighting, the killings of civilians and the fires of the raking of October 7-10, 1944. On October 10, about sixty partisans of the Ligurian-Alessandrin division led by the captain of the Domenico Lanza     .Mingo , gold medal of the military valor, stopped the German columns with four machine guns; Mingo fell covering the retreat, and with him seven other partisans. In the autumn the Festa della Montagna is held in the hamlet.
The diocesan museum is located in the Bishop's Palace.
Entering the House of Verism.
A restored early medieval church.
The fortress of the village and the wines of Etna.
Karst nature and orchids a stone's throw from the village.

A city founded in 1935, designed by engineer Riccardo Morandi for the workers of the BPD explosive factory, with the church of Santa Barbara, more than 6 km of air-raid shelters excavated in the pozzolana and the Archaeological Museum of the Tolerian territory; on the plateau remain the ruins of the Old Castle.
Remains of a noble villa of the end of the III century AD, rich in mosaics, with finds such as bracelets, coins, glass and amphorae.
Water jump from clear waters, reachable by car.
The Etruscans at the gates of Rome.
A limestone monolith about 9 meters high, in an oak wood near the parish church of Rocca Santa Maria, which contains hundreds of marine fossils; it is reached with a steep path.
Among the oldest churches in the city, with origins around the year 1000: a single nave with recently restored fifteenth-century frescoes. Opening by reservation through Pro Loco or Tourist Office.
The ancient heart of the city of Blessed Jacopo.
The chestnut millennial.
The Gothic-Aragonese of the Meilogu with a portal-retablo in stone.
private property, not open to visits: you can see only from the outside
The pantheon of Montefeltro outside the walls.
The red domes symbol of Palermo.
The most scenic Baroque façade in the centre.
The oldest of the five chapels, at 1430 meters on a height above the village.
A mountain village transformed into an open-air gallery.
Norman ruins overlooking the sea.
The tomb of the discoverer of the Mississippi springs.

On the edge of the village, founded in 1576, enlarged in the seventeenth century and reconsecrated in 1621, it has bare façade with a short frescoed porch, oculus and bell tower; in the single nave wooden altars and canvases, among which those of the main altar (Madonna della Salute, San Lorenzo and Santo Stefano) attributed to Baccio Ciarpi. On the access ramp there is a stylophorus of the XIV-XV centuries; the monastery around the cloister is today little more than a ruin.
The archaeology of the lower Valdarno in the historic centre.

In the former Pretura, managed by the association              • The New Myrtle • • The New Myrtle • exhibits more than 1000 pieces on disappeared crafts and daily life of a century ago: glasses of the Glass Fairy • • the original furnishings of the Pharmacy Laus • documents of the Pretura and the workshops rebuilt of blacksmith , shoemaker , oraio and maniscalco , with tools for wine and oil. Open Saturday, Sunday and holidays.
One of the gates of the city walls of the seventeenth century.
A medieval monastery.

Built on land of the Spadalonga family, at the foot of the town where the medieval market was held.

Neoclassical church built in 1833-1838 on a project by the engineer Talucchi, decorated at the beginning of the twentieth century by Mgr. Vallero with paintings of the school of Reffo and the pupils Siffredi and Guglielmino.

The most famous patrician villa of Frascati, begun in 1598 by Giacomo Della Porta and completed around 1620 by Maderno and Fontana: frescoed rooms of the seventeenth century, central water lilies, chapel of San Sebastiano and park with fountains and terraces; called \"Belvedere" for the view of Rome. Park open on weekdays.
The Vesuvian countryside before the cars, with the real animals.
A medieval canal to follow by bike.

The Ceyrat viewpoint is the highest point of the village, with views of the roofs, the volcanic lake and the sea; the Terrace of the In love, under Palazzo Ruspoli, looks at the lake and takes its name from the myths of Diana and Virbio and Numa Pompilio and the nymph Egeria.
Open to visitors only in spring and autumn (Visit Lazio)
The Roman tombstones of Interpromium next to the abbey.
The civil memory of the Belice earthquake.

Symbol of the village, rest of the medieval fortifications: it has the current appearance since 1903, after the demolition of part of the walls and the civic tower. The two towers of the entrance are joined by a covered walkway; the cylindrical one, crenellated, carries the clock built in 1849 by Pietro Mei, still working and loaded by hand. From the high view of the valleys of Misa and Esino.
The sixteenth-century parish church of the village.

Ethnographic Museum and documentation centre on the cimbrian people, of Bavarian-Tyrolean origin, allocated in Lessinia between the XII and XIV century; Giazza is the closest area to the original language and traditions. The multi-storey itinerary presents language, family life, work, architecture, religiousity and popular beliefs, with art and cimbri crafts; the center organizes demonstrations and courses every year. Open Saturday and Sunday 15-18.
The smallest kingdom in the world in the middle of the sea.

Parishyard dedicated to Giulio d'Orta, patron saint celebrated on 31 January: documented from the 14th century (a tomb inscription is 1386), consecrated in 1557, has the current appearance from the expansion desired in 1926 by Don Testori; presbytery with Venetian marble mosaics of 1932, imposing ciborium and organ Mascioni opus 1175 of 2006. In 1936 the demolition of the old bell tower revealed a fresco of the Holy Trinity. The new bell tower, completed in 1948, is 93 meters high, third of Lombardy: about 250 steps up to the view on Valle Olona, Monte Rosa, Resegone and skyline of Milan, climbable only in organized visits (FAI, April 2026).
Isolotto formed by the river Churches and the Canal Naviglio, which cross the country; it is frequented mainly in summer for the coolest temperature of the water.

Started in 1589 on a project by Battista Sormano, with the dome of Giovanni Cortese and the facade of Guglielmo Calderini; it preserves a heritage of ecclesiastical goods of particular importance.

It is the oldest church in the village, with Romanesque bell tower and simple and elegant façade, reached through narrow cobbled streets and low arcades. It was a parish until 1507, then passed to the Friars Minor Reformed Observants of St. Francis, who expanded and built a convent and cloister with a series of sundials.

Medieval village perched on the Ruffi Mountains above the Aniene valley, about 58 km from Rome, known as the village of artists and models: from the nineteenth century there were northern European painters and then Kokoschka, Pirandello and Silone, and the Civic Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art preserves about 700 works; in Piazza delle Ville there is the fountain of Arturo Martini.

Church linked to archaeological finds of Roman times, which preserves evidence of Verona's Romanesque art. It is included in the virtual tour of the historical sites of the Municipality, with audio guide in Italian, English and German.

Top of 1,092 m in the middle of the park, destination of an excursion of about two hours from Hermits; at the top the small church of the Madonna di Caravaggio, with nineteenth-century frescoes of more painters including the comasco Gambini.

Open-air museum in the woods, in an area of the Campo dei Fiori Park, with wooden sculptures made from trunks or branches broken by the local sculptor Sergio Terni: at the entrance the Guardiano del Bosco, then a squirrel with the acorn, the Witch of Cerro, the Dea Berta with his duck, a spider, a gnome, a viper, an owl and a dove, with other strains in processing. The route is flat, no longer than 800 meters long, very easy and suitable for children; from Caldana you climb to Cerro with path 17 and you can continue to Orino.

In the thirteenth century Palazzo del Capitano del Popolo, in front of the Pieve, the collection of the antiques founder of the Antique Fair: objects from prehistory to the twentieth century, even outside Europe.

Among the largest military works in Europe (over 500 m long, about 25,000 sqm), commissioned in the 16th century by Philip II of Spain in place of an Aragonese fortress; inside galleries, gun squares, cisterns, barracks, the church of St. James and the remains of the Governor's Palace. It was the last Bourbon stronghold to surrender on March 20, 1861. The museum, opened in 1988 in the former artillery stores, exhibits weapons from the Renaissance to the battles of 1806 and 1860-61 and historical maps.

Small church in panoramic position on the shortcut to Taormina, perhaps the oldest in the village, founded after the arrival of San Pancrazio in Taormina; it preserves an eighteenth-century fresco and has been restored.

Built in 1283 on an existing building and preceded by the monument to St. Francis of 1927, it is famous for its portico with scenic vaults and a giant crib; in the Hall of Audiences, since 2005, the art gallery of the Diocesan Museum.
Savinese ceramics inside a Siena fortress.

In the west of the village, it dates back to 1221 and is one of the oldest religious buildings dedicated to St. Bartholomew.
Reachable on foot from Borgosesia, it keeps the caves of prehistoric finds exposed to the Museo Conti; for trekking you go up to the village Fenera San Giulio and follow the signs to Cima Bastia.
The Walser story in a sixteenth-century house-fortress.
View of the But valley from a tower of the thirteenth century.
The fifteenth-century portal of the convent.

Opened in 2004 at the former Consorzio Tabaccoltori near the station: cultivation, care in the towers, manufacture and social history of the tobacconists of the high valley of the Tiber.
At Villa Maria heirlooms, photographs, scores and pianos by the composer Pietro Mascagni.
A golden baroque altar and 16th century frescoes in a small church in the valley.

Medieval fortress of the thirteenth century that has preserved its original appearance except the moats, on a rock overhanging: scenic round corner tower, entrance with drawbridge, Palacium connected to the mast, inner courtyard and late fourteenth-century bifore on the south and west facades. The Batajera, a square-plan porch, was the ancient entrance. An independent audioguide (QR code or PIN, in Italian, English, German and Piedmontese) is accessible all year round and includes the exterior and courtyard of the castle; from May to October guided tours on Sundays at 15, 16 and 17.
The square of the Humanistic University.

Of medieval origin and restored over the centuries, it is the main church of the village, with a simple façade of Baroque influence and bell tower; inside marble altars, devotional statues and a fresco of the Assumption of the Virgin.
It combines with the visit of the archaeological area.

The first stone was laid in 1582 by the bishop of Cremona Nicolò Sfondati; the current façade is in 1941, the work of the Soresian architect Giulio Carotti. He preserves works by Luigi Miradori called the Genovesino, Giacomo Miradori, Giovanni Battista Trotti called the Malosso, Giovanni Giacomo Pasini and Ermenegildo Lodi, and an organ Serassi-Balbiani (1810-1887); the nineteenth-century bell tower, designed by L. Voghera and completed by C. Visioli, hosts a concert of 12 bells.

The Gargassa stream has recorded conglomerates and brooks of the Oligocene (about 28 million years ago), forming canyons, ponds, spires and towers. Ring of 7 km, about 4 hours, difference in altitude 180 m, difficulty EE, from the sports field in Gargassino (SP for Tiglieto, about 3 km): you meet the ford under the tower "Muso del Gatto" , the Houses Vereira with traces of the pre-industrial production of glass, a sulphuric source and the "Balcony of the Lady" .

Through the gorges you enter the Vallone di Santo Spirito, which climbs up to the summit of Monte Amaro in the Majella National Park: a long and tiring climb. In the valley live the chamois all year round.
private villa, not accessible, open only for receptions (Metropolitan city of Palermo)
The waterfall you can see from downtown.

About 8 km of coast on the Ionian coast, in the Gulf of Taranto, alternate cliffs and soft sand coves: from Luogovivo to La Fontana, from Le Canne to Montedarena and from the Capparone Hospital to Lido Silvana. This last stretch is dominated by the Torre Castelluccia, linked to the fear of Saracen incursions, and preserves specimens of juniper cuddly; swimming you reach a rocky islet. Largely low floors, suitable for families, with bathing establishments and accommodation facilities.
Monet's bridge.

Built at the end of the eighteenth century, it was originally inhabited by fishermen and then bought by the Caetani family.

Only the perimeter walls remain of the thirteenth-century church: nave and transept have become an open-air theatre, while the space below houses the Ciarlatano Museum.

One of the most beautiful lakes in Lake Maggiore, overlooking the Borromeo Gulf and the islands, with colorful facades, arcades, terraces and cafes: here lived Arturo Toscanini from 1927 to 1952.

We were blessed set in a rocky ridge of Monte Scalambra at 1,100 meters; according to legend the saint defeated the devil, whose fall left the mark of the devil. The patron's feast is September 29th. The first paragliding flight started in 1978 from Monte Scalambra.
Medieval irrigation channel still in use, from Veynes to Roisan, for walks in the sun.

Section of the Museum of the Mòcheni valley dedicated to the wood supply chain: the route follows the cutting of trees and the transport of trunks along the slopes of the valley to the sawmill on the Balkof river, in operation until the end of the fifties to make tables for families in the area. Around larch and fir woods, pastures and huts. Open on Sundays at 15-17.30, only in July and August.

Invillino, about 1.5 km from the center, was for centuries the administrative and economic nucleus of the municipality and preserves houses with the characteristics of the minor Carnic architecture. On the hill of Santino, high above the Tagliamento valley, the excavations of the University of Monaco (1964-72) documented a Roman settlement of the first century, iron and glass processing activities in the late Imperial era and a fortified village of the VI-VII century (the Longobard castle of Ibligine, then covered). On the hill stands the Pieve di Santa Maria Maddalena, one of the oldest in Carnia, with three documented construction phases and present form of the fifteenth century (probably 1431); its wooden altar of Domenico da Tolmezzo is today at the Diocesan Museum of Udine.

Paintings, statues, furnishings, vestments and silvers from the 16th to the 20th century, linked to devotion to the patron and founder Costabile Gentilcore: cups, pissides and patenes dated from 1586 to 1895, an ostensory and a crown of the eighteenth century, parchments of the sixteenth century, portraits of canons, Neapolitan nativity figures from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, a pivial of about 1700 and statues including a wooden Madonna of the sixteenth century.
Built on the ruins of the old acropolis, several times rebuilt and covered in Baroque style in the eighteenth century; it houses a wooden crucifix and a bust of Christ carved in stone.

It preserves the relics of the saint; ancient, was restored in the early nineteenth century by an architect who probably followed the advice of Canova, with stucco decorations and paintings of the seventeenth century. You can reach it from Via Roma before the arch of Porta Romana; on the piazza Palazzo Santacroce, today hotel.
Panorama at altitude up to a sanctuary among the highest in Europe.
The house of my prisons.

Benedictine abbey about 850 meters at the foot of the Amandola mountain, 5 km from the village: documented from 1044, deeply modified between 1295 and the fifteenth century, with bell tower rebuilt in 1461. The original structure remains the right wing, some arches of the cloister and fragments of the apse; single nave interior with trussed ceiling and single nave crypt on a single central pillar. For the timetables, contact the Municipality.

The monumental four-arched stone bridge, erected by the Dorias, lords of the village from 1547 to the eighteenth century, joins the village on the left bank to the religious complex on the right. The village, in 1164 a fief of Malaspina for Barbarossa's concession, had at the end of the seventeenth century a mint with the effigy of Violante Doria; every year a balloon festival recalls Sophie Blanchard, landed here in 1811 after a balloon accident.
The clear waterfall.

The Benedictine abbey of the 8th century, an influential religious center of southern Tuscany: the crypt under the presbytery has columns carved with human and animal faces of over a thousand years ago.

In Piazza della Vetreria remains the chimney, the only remaining of the Fajella Glassworks of the early nineteenth century, considered the first industrial glassworks in Italy; the nearby buildings, restored, house bars and restaurants.

It is annexed to the parish church and collects over 120 sacred objects (sinks, candlesticks, glasses, lamps, monstrances and reliquaries) from Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Neapolitan and French schools, furniture in noble metals from the 16th to the 19th century and liturgical vestments from the 16th to the 18th century. Open on the fourth Saturday and Sunday of the month, 9.30-12.30 and 15.30-18.

Late Baroque chapel founded in 1772, already home to the Confraternity of San Girolamo, marks the entrance to the historic center among the olive trees, with facade and porch overlooking the valley and churchyard with stone cross; it preserves a pipe organ of 1797, today not working.
Medieval ruins with panoramic views of the morainic hills.

Historical stop of the Via Francigena at the confluence of Magra and Aulella, with the abbey of San Caprasio founded in 884 and its museum on the pilgrimage, and the Fortress of Brunella that houses the Museum of Natural History of Lunigiana; in the territory the villages of Bibola and Caprigliola and the mechanical nativity scene of Pallerone.

The ancient Tamburù street covers every year the flower carpets of the Corpus Domini Infiorata, born in 1927; the symbol of the village is the fountain of Piazza Ricci surmounted by an obelisk.
The nineteenth-century frescoes of the Ivaldi brothers.
Born after the floods of 1973-74, from 1990 at Cascina Vigna in the city park: minerals, plants and animals, with the entomological collection as the most important nucleus; visits by appointment.
In the medieval palaces of Piazza Cavour, the collection of contemporary art donated to the Fondazione San Patrignano and the great fourteenth-century Last Judgement by Giovanni da Rimini.

A bishop's city that gives its name to the gulf, perched on a hill overlooking the Costa degli Aranci and dominated by the Norman Castle; it is known as the "Città della Ceramica" for the shops of the historic center and houses the cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783, and the diocesan Museum in the Bishop's Palace.
The Etruscan door of the fourth century BC, still in use.
open only Sundays and holidays from March to November, times vary with the weather

Built by the Scaligeri between XIII and XIV century on Roman and Romanesque remains and then rebuilt in Venetian style; in 1618 Verona bought it as a residence of the Captain of the Lake and is National Monument since 1902. Today it hosts exhibitions, concerts and the library: ground floor and garden are open with free entrance, the first floor can be visited at events.

Erected around 1355 by Bernabò Visconti, lord of Milan, and Queen of the Scala as a hunting residence and convivial encounters, she is among the best examples of fortified Visconti architecture of the fourteenth century. Square plan with four corner towers around a large courtyard, arcades on the ground floor and loggias on the upper floor; a recent restoration brought to light the original painted decorations with floral, geometric and polychrome motifs. Today it is the municipality and hosts the library in the ancient stables, exhibitions and events; open Friday morning, Saturday and Sunday morning and afternoon.

The towers of the city of the hundred towers are: the Sineo Tower (35 m) in front of the cathedral with the triphores on top, the Bonino Tower on via Maestra and the Asthesian Tower (30 m). They're private, they look up from the outside.
The civic tower, rest of the ancient castle of bishops-conti, next to the 13th-century Bishops' Palace, now auditorium.
Ancient building site for the repair and construction of boats, with hut roof and trusses supported by ten brick pillars.
Sunsets with views to Corsica.

Pink granite, pine forests and coves.
Church of the thirteenth century with the façade in travertine partly designed by Michelozzo in the first fifteenth century, between Gothic and Renaissance.

Church built at the beginning of the fifteenth century in the place where a shepherd found an image of the Virgin.
Fauna and minerals of the territory in a civic museum.
The frescoes of Spain on the mountains.

The Roman open-air city near the centre: the remains of the forum with the civil basilica, the river port with the long row of warehouses and docks embedded in the walls of the fourth century and the late antique markets.
The village on the river at the foot of the capital.
A bridge of 2,000 years.

One of the oldest churches in Modenese, probably built in the middle of the 7th century on the Via Bibulca, with a hospice for pilgrims; the Romanesque building of the 11th century, largely restored, has three naves and three semicircular apses and a holy waterworks with sirens of the Master of the Metops.
Two churches within walking distance, between the fourteenth and eighteenth centuries.

On the cliff that dominates the city, called the "Acropolis of Tyrol": the church of Santa Croce was the diocese's cathedral for about 400 years, until the bishop was transferred to Brixen around the year 1000, and is one of the oldest pilgrimage sites in Tyrol. The Benedictine nuns remained there for over 335 years, until November 2021. You can visit the Chapel of Graces, the church of the monastery, Santa Croce and the church of Our Lady with archaeological documentation; you can only walk up, in 30-40 minutes.

Fortified village built in the 13th century (Mons Cauri) on the traffic to the sea along the ridge streets, with cobbled streets and the remains of the castle of the 12th century. The island is very close to Ventotene, reachable by boat, with the Bourbon prison built in 1795 by Ferdinando I delle Due Sicilie and active until 1965. Land at Marinella (the only sheltered), Burrone, Punta dei Sighi and Bath Giulia.
Titian, Crivelli and Lotto in a few steps.

Consecrated in 1455 by Cardinal Nicolò Cusano and enlarged around 1500, he served travellers heading beyond the Tauri to Salzburg; his cemetery welcomed those who died in the pass and the miners of Predoi. Next to the large boulder "Schliefstein" .

In the medieval village of Civitella del Lago, overlooking the lake of Corbara, it collects the painted eggs or carved by artists, amateurs and students for the National Competition Exhibition "Ovo Pinto" which is held every Easter since 1982, tradition of Roman origin still alive in central Italy.
Double porch.
About 4 kilometers of beach to the north, with a bike path that connects Casabianca to San Tommaso.

Maremma's seaside village enclosed by ancient walls on the Poggio Petriccio hill, with panoramic castle and canal port on Bruna; in the territory the Etruscan city of Vetulonia with necropolis and museum, and the wet area of the Diaccia Botrona with the Casa Rossa Ximenes.

Entitled to Victor Salvi, it presents itself as the first and only museum in the world dedicated entirely to the harp, with its history and its sound universe.
Trapani corals.

Rural chapel of Renaissance origin, patronage of the University of Valle, modified from 1840 with works for the Holy Camp; closed to worship in 1987 for injuries at a time, it was reopened after the work started in 1997. The original rustic style was enriched with frescoes, stuccoes and bas-reliefs, with an elegant facade and an imposing bell tower; in spring and autumn a procession brings the statue of the Madonna between the chapel and the parish.
The miraculous statue.
The Black Madonna of the Varaita Valley.
The history of Sinnai from Neolithic to the Middle Ages, with the god Bes.

Villa Liberty, home of the politician, historian and jurist Bortolo Belotti, opened to the public in 2017: the study with original furnishings and the archive, also linked to friendship with D'Annunzio, and 26 paintings from the sixteenth to the twentieth century donated by the family to the Municipality. The park of about 5,000 square meters houses sculptures by Nino Galizzi.

Country on the right bank of the Oglio, whose name would come from "guado d'Oglio": of the castle of Gonzaga, demolished in 1705, remains the Preda Pescadura, while the main street is marked by the sixteenth-century portico of 30 arches wanted by Ludovico Gonzaga, under which the Giacometti Theatre and the Center of Audiovisual Communication Oreste Coni are located.
In the center of ancient aristocratic palaces overlook narrow alleys, among which stands the mother church of St. Nicholas.
Two centuries of stories of soldiers and decorated.

It is the highest point in Albugnano, at about 550 meters, with 360 degrees views of the Asti hills and the mountains in the background. Here stood a medieval castle dismantled in 1401, of which minimal traces remain; it houses the Park of the Remembrance with the cippi of the fallen of the world wars.

Art city divided between the Upper City, closed by the Venetian Walls UNESCO heritage, and the modern Lower City: Old Square and the Campanone, Santa Maria Maggiore and the Colleoni Chapel, the Carrara Academy and the places of Gaetano Donizetti.
The two rivers between which the city rises: the Tanaro flows next to the Citadel and Borgo Rovereto.

The old town is enclosed inside the medieval walls, while outside the walls the streets widen fan-wide. At the end of September the Festa del Borgo recalls its historical atmosphere, together with the festival of civraxu.

From Piazza Roma, a panoramic terrace, you can reach the Town Hall with the fourteenth-century civic tower and the church of San Biagio of the fifteenth-century; in the public gardens there are traces of the walls of the castle with three towers, then Porta San Biagio, the Monteguarnieri Park, Piazza Risorgimento and the remains of Porta San Lorenzo embedded in the walls.
Five generations of artists in a home laboratory.
Wooden statues and furnishings in a neoclassical church linked to the patron saint.
Protected area with reeds and water lilies and nature trail, equipped with visitor center; it is touched by the MTB tour of the three lakes (about 25 km) that from Garda passes through Lake Ledro.
Quiet walks with the profile of the Matterhorn reflected in clear water.
Built between 1885 and 1895 for the maintenance of trains, among the most important examples of 19th century industrial architecture in the city, today hub of contemporary culture.
The rare blooms of Baldo.
An Italian theater with original stage cars.
It exhibits some of the finds found in the territory, inhabited since the Roman age (the name comes from the Latin Quadrivium).
The most beautiful Renaissance square in Cremasco.

A stone's throw from Piazza del Plebiscito, it owes its name to the eighteenth-century market; in the center the fountain existing since 1335, redesigned in 1621 by Filippo Caparozzi with four lions in pepper, and the House of Peace with the inscription of 1503.
Romanesque and castle remains in a hamlet of Valnerina.
Built in 1605 and then very remodelled, with columns in Lecce stone and triumphal arches with floral decorations.

Bad Egart is the oldest spa house in Tyrol, with a source documented since 1430. The route includes the thermal caves, portraits and objects of the Habsburg monarchy, a Biedermeier kitchen, objects of Tyrolean folk history and a garden with works of art; the special exhibition on Sisi and Francesco Giuseppe exhibits over 4,000 objects.
Medieval castle of private property, with interiors not always visitable; at its feet the fortified village of Frapporta, with narrow alleys.
A fresco venerated by montevarchini.

Spa park of more than four hectares, between clearings and denser areas connected by avenues, with exotic species such as calocedar, sequoia and cryptomeria next to beech trees, hippocastans, plane trees and lindens; it preserves a chapel, an artificial hill, a circular kiosk belvedere and a fountain with spout. The first initiatives to exploit the source date back to 1860, the plant in the green is documented from 1875 and the complex was completed in the early twentieth century with Grand Hotel and Palace Hotel; since 1972 it is of the Autonomous Province of Trento and has been recently recovered.
At sunset the most beautiful landscape of the delta.
times between MiC card (seasonal, closed on Mondays) and italia.it; check before visiting
Monastery built in 1600 that houses a valuable organ; inside the monastic structure there is the church of Santa Maria.
The last rest of the castle of Arcello.
The cycle of wheat and bread in the house of a peasant family.
Three-nave parish church of the seventeenth century, frescoed in 1852 by the Ivaldi brothers called "Mut" .
The shrine rises above the village.

At 974 meters between woods, reeds and meadows, you can reach on foot from the center and a pedestrian path follows its banks connecting to the lake of the Piazze; you practice SUP, kayak and dragon boat, in summer you swim and in winter you ice skate. It has the Blue Flag; near the banks the eighteenth-century capital of the Crucifix, recently restored.
The big park of the city.

In the highest part of the village, the convent has a first settlement of the mid-15th century but it is largely late seventeenth century. The gallery contains paintings from the Mannerist and Caravaggio school: the Trasverberazione di Santa Teresa di scuola bolognese, paintings from Luca Fiammingo, Maddalena penitente and Christ at the Mount of Olives of Cerrini, Christ crowned with thorns and Emmaus dinner of the Caravaggio school, works by Lucas de la Haye and Giovanni Della Miseria; the San Giuseppe carpenter of Gerrit van Honthorst was stolen. The MiC card (2020) does not indicate opening days.

Prepositural built between 1856 and 1861 on a project by Giacomo Moraglia, with façade of Camillo Boito, on the site of a church mentioned in 974, of which remains the late dogotic bell tower in terracotta begun in 1458. Dome of 27 meters frescoed by Luigi Cavenaghi (1887-1891), seventeenth-century paintings of Morazzone and Daniele Crespi, eighteenth-century copy of the Shroud in crypt donated by the Savoys in 1710, altar and ambo by Claudio Parmiggiani of 2018.
A courtyard building with a roof garden.
Inside the Archaeological Park, in Borgo Croce, documents with historical documents, photographs, films and panels the Italian countries rebuilt elsewhere after an earthquake.
Tower on a small height, indicated as a panoramic point on the coast.
The hamlet on the Maremma sea.
In the Quadrilatero, the Baroque church preserves the Complaint on Christ who died in terracotta (second half of the fifteenth century), seven figures in life size.

Church of the patron saint with three naves, built at the beginning of the seventeenth century by popular initiative on the site of three previous churches, with sandstone portal of master Luca Murena from Nicosia; inside the base of the Madonna of the Audience dated 1477 and the chapel with the Vara of the saint. The bell tower has a dome of colored stones. Feast on January 15th and the first Tuesday of July.

Artificial basins of the high valley reachable by road: Camplicioli da Alpe Russi with a hairpin bend up to the dam, with a wide view of the valley; Lake Cavalli da Cheggio, about 6 km of challenging ascent from Antronapiana on the SP 141, framed by Pizzo Andolla and Weissmies (last dirt track). The descent road from Campliccioli is very narrow and with blind curves.

Memorial in Piazza Parolini designed by engineer Giancarlo Maroni, author of the Vittoriale di Gardone Riviera, conceived as an ascendant shrine: a large staircase rises to the monolith    .Pilo of the Heroes with the names of fallen.

It rises to the north of the town of Tomb on the site of an ancient centa; an octagonal chapel, perhaps of the X-XI century, was incorporated as an apse in the fourteenth-century church and in 1571-1572 Giulio Urbanis frescoed the vault (frescoes restored in 2013). The current building, with a single nave with Ionic pilasters, was built by the foreman Sebastiano Lotti of Bertiolo and inaugurated in 1764; the bell tower is from 1830. In the Great War she was sheltered for prisoners, then restored after the earthquake of 1976.
Michele Ciampanti's 15th century triptych.
The power of the Serenissima.

Medieval village of the Alta Val di Cecina linked to the copper mine of Camporciano, active until 1907 and in the nineteenth century the largest in Europe, today Museo delle Miniere. In the village the Belforti Tower, the fourteenth-century Palazzo Pretorio with the Documentation Centre of the museum and the church of San Biagio; in the surroundings the medieval villages of La Sassa and Querceto and the route of the old railway of the mines.
A scientific garden in the city.

A marked route \"intrigued with partisan history" that connects Valloriate to Paraloup, with totems that tell the story along the way; it touches the villages Sapè and Mutta, which had mountain schools, and isolated buildings such as "chabot" and "ports" with the peaks Tajarè, the Alpe and Beccàs of Midday as panoramic points.

On the hill on the right bank of the Tagliamento, overlooking the narrow river, ancient way of transit; the lords of Pinzano, vassals of the Patriarch of Aquileia, are mentioned in 1164 and in the thirteenth century the castle had walls, mast and a church of St. Nicholas. Damaged by the 1348 earthquake, conquered by the Savorgnan in the fourteenth century, it lost its military function; since 1809, passed to Antonio Moro and other owners, it was used mainly as a stone quarry. Today the oval plateau, of about 175 m of perimeter, is covered with ruins; the restorations have brought to light an embankment with underground cellars and Roman and medieval finds.

It is home to the 16th century abbey church, reopened about a decade after the earthquake of 1783 without the ancient bell tower, the churches of San Giovanni and Santa Maria del Carmelo (cited in 1597) and the houses of the families Votta and Fabiani.

Romanesque single nave church with hut roof, semicircular apse and bell tower leaning behind the apse; the walls are in river pebbles with brick and stone inserts, and the two terracotta portals of the south side suggest a dating after the mid-twelfth century. The Virgin has the traits of an elderly mother with popular features, with Christ lying on her knees; the scannello depicts St. Michael, St. John the Baptist, St. Thomas Aquinas and Averroes. Damaged by the earthquake of 1783, the restoration of 1968 at the Opificio delle Pietre Dure in Florence gave it its white color.
Wall of the thirteenth century on Tuscan models, with four doors and 36 towers; remain short stretches in course Trinità, Via Torre Tonda and Piazza Sant'Antonio.

Medieval manor to guard the area, destroyed and then rebuilt by Federico Barbarossa in the twelfth century; it remains the fifteenth-century tower of entrance, in front of the parish, the western tower of the fifteenth-century called Torre Castellana or Torre Grossa and part of the walls, which enclose the most evocative stretch of the village. It belonged to Toriani, Visconti and Belgiojoso, with a share of the monks of the Certosa of Pavia; the Belgiojoso lived there until about 1960, then the property passed to the parish. Twenty domus de janas of the Neo-Eneolithic (IV-III millennium BC, first phases of Ozieri's Culture) excavated in an outcrop of trachytes about 10 meters high. The Cape Tomb, about 250 m2 and 18 rooms, is among the largest hypogeas of the Mediterranean: re-used as a rock church dedicated to Sant'Andrea, it preserves Christian frescoes with scenes of the New Testament; next to the hut tomb, with conical ceiling with ray and votive cups, and the chamber tomb with two pillars and double sloping ceiling, plus the monolith of the sacred tower. According to the MiC open from March to October every day without appointment, from November to February by reservation (tel. 348 5642611). Since 2025 it is part of the UNESCO site of the domus de janas.

Medieval village of the Lepini Mountains between Mount Calvello and the valley of the Amaseno, about 116 km from Rome, dominated by the Baronial Castle where in 1274 St. Thomas Aquinas stayed and which today houses the Civic Museum of the landscape; around, Piazza Duomo with the monument to the saint, the church of Santa Maria Assunta, Santa Reparata and the birth palace of Pope Leo XIII.

The Porta Grande, an ancient sixteenth-century access on the south side of the walls, separates the districts under the Windows and the Courtyard; the Via dei Finestroni, one of the oldest in the village, has lava stone flooring and arched houses. In the village also Palazzo Orsini, seat of the town hall, built in 1727 by Cardinal Orsini, then Pope Benedict XIII.

Example of the late Renaissance in Brescia and among the most important Renaissance architectures in the province, with Venetian paintings of the seventeenth century and the version of the Last Supper of Tiepolo.

In the hamlet on the right bank of the Arno, a hydraulic complex that from the fourteenth century barred the river between Castelfranco and San Romano, operated the municipal mills and allowed the passage of the boats; a grand-ducal customs collected tolls. In 1833 it was the only 'callone' still standing along the river.

Built in 1494 with the support of the Municipality of Perugia as a vote against the plague, entirely in sandstone with façade of Domenico Bertini and a Latin cross plan with a single nave; inside the frescoes of Papacello, the rounds of the prophets and the Epiphany of Domenico Alfani on sketches of Rosso Fiorentino and a coronation of the Virgin of G.B. The 1-1,5-hour visit usually begins with the short documentary "Stava 19 July" (in English on request). A dome of about 13 for 5 km that stands out in the Treviso plain, with a karst character with numerous dolines (up to 74 per km2); the highest point is the Collesel Val dell'Acqua (371 m), where stands the church of Santa Maria della Vittoria. On the slope towards the Piave many places recall the Great War: here the Battle of Solstice was fought (15-23 June 1918), which started the Austro-Hungarian retreat.

One of the smallest Romanesque churches in Sardinia, erected in the middle of the thirteenth century in marl, sandstone and basalt: two naves, one apse, and on the façade an architrave with five anthropomorphic figures, one upside down, unique in the Sardinian medieval sculpture. Inside two niches with wooden statues of St. Michael.

The village of the Barbagia di Ollolai, between Gennargentu and Supramonte, famous for the Mamuthones and Issohadores who leave for the first time on 17 January, for Sant'Antonio: the Museum of Mediterranean Masks and the Museum of Culture and Work, the necropolis of Istevene, from 2025 UNESCO Heritage, the stele of Sa Perda Pintà and the alleys of the center with murals and sculptures.
The tunnels in the tuff under the village.
The church of the Marquises with the Madonna holding the keys of the village.

A fortified village remained almost intact.

In the Benedictine cloisters of San Vitale: tombstones, avori, icons, armor, ceramics and the cycle of fourteenth-century frescoes of Santa Chiara. For the Ministry it is the largest and most heterogeneous museum in Romagna.

Fortified complex founded in the thirteenth century and enlarged in the fifteenth century, with courtyard, well, cellar, oratory and dorm; today it houses the Municipal Historical Archives and the CEDRAV, center of anthropological documentation of Valnerina. In the church a Visitation of 1573 by Camillo Angelucci da Mevale, seventeenth-century paintings and frescoes of the fifteenth century (Annunciation, Crucifixion and Saints, Christ in glory with angels), some close to the Master of Eggi; in a room of the monastery a universal Judgment of the first half of the fifteenth century.
Sixtus V, which is also in London.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione del Touring, once called Favale, dominated by the castle of Morra on the gorge of Sinni, where in the sixteenth century lived the poetess Isabella Morra; to her is dedicated since 1993 one of the first Italian literary parks, while on Mount Coppolo remain the walls of the ancient Lagaria.

It is located in the eighteenth century former Palace of Justice, born as a convent with the adjoining church of the Souls of Purgatory. About 1,500 exhibits and thousands of photographs, videos and oral documents tell the cycles of wheat, wine and oil, shepherds and breeders, charcoal makers, woodcutter and hunters and pastoral aesthetics; there are also a naturalistic section curated by the Nebrodi Park Authority, one on the traditional culture of Mistretta, touch screen and an immersive hall.

The medieval castle in ruins on the brooch of the Violes, on the road to La Morra: inaccessible, you can admire the cylindrical tower from afar; the legend wants that in 1713 the vault of the salon collapsed during a dance.

Last rest of Mels Castle, built between 1026 and 1045 and granted by the Tirol counts in fiefdom to the Waldsees; burned in 1262 and partly destroyed in 1352 by the patriarch Nicolò of Luxembourg, stood on the hill north of the town with quadrangular plan, crenellated wall and three terraces. The ancient square tower remains, partly rebuilt after the 1976 earthquake, with fourteenth-century houses along the belt; the church annexed to St. Andrew was consecrated in 1056.
The nineteenth-century fountain of the village.
Tertenia's most heartfelt party.
The oldest part of the fortifications.

Country of the inland Catanzaro with the mother church of the Immaculate in the central square, the Museum of the village born from the collection of the master Francesco Scerbo and the Route of the Mills along the stream Fosso-Acquafredda, between ruins and waterfalls.
A monastery saved from the waters, with a De Chirico.

Central site is the Tanzgasse, with burials and remains of ceramic production; there were found a place of worship of the Copper Age with a megalithic structure of large stones and a figurative stele (menhir). The first communities of farmers and breeders date back to the fifth millennium BC and the area was frequented from the Neolithic to the Middle Ages; among the findings bones, gold and ceramics. The excavations are still underway.
A little above Lake Fraturno, on the Morella Hill, the remains of Castel del Lago, a medieval fortress and one of the fortified castra of the Lucretili Mountains.
Three hundred frescoes and an altar in Juvarra.

Holiday village in a panoramic position just a few steps from the eastern shore of Lake Orta: Palazzo Tornielli with the contemporary art museum and the Neogothic Park, the house-museum of Antonio Calderara in Vacciago, the sanctuary of the Madonna della Bocciola, the fourteenth-century parish church and the paths of the Quadrifoglio towards Monte Mesma.
The fortress of the Marquises.

Ancient copper mine, one of the largest in Italy about six centuries ago: a small train leads into the mountain and the guided tour of the gallery of Sant'Ignazio, excavated by hand, shows tools, machinery and a copper vein; in the mountain there is also the climate center of Predoi.
