The mountain house for trekking and climbing.
The palace that Pius II donated to Cardinal Rodrigo Borgia, future Alessandro VI, today seat of the Diocesan Museum with paintings, fabrics and liturgical objects of the territory.

The oranges, perhaps planted by the Camaldolese monks already in the twelfth century, are the heart of the agricultural identity of the country, greened by the abundance of water at the foot of Montiferru; a short distance from São Paulo are the Pernis-Vacca and La Vega gardens.
The 16th century church of the village of Valera.
One of the best preserved Roman theatres in Marche, still in summer use.

In 1651 Camillo Pamphilj, Pope Innocent's nephew X, bought the manor and, demolished in 1652 the Sforza castle, started in 1654 the new palace (completed around 1670) on a project attributed to the Jesuit Benedetto Molli, then followed by Antonio Del Grande: 365 rooms, a facade with 7 windows like the days of the week and another with 12 months. On the noble floor, between 1657 and 1661, Pier Francesco Mola, Gaspard Dughet, Guillaume Courtois called the Burgundian, Francesco Cozza and Mattia Preti frescoed the four rooms of the Elements, the four chamber of the Continents, the Prince's Hall with the walls trompe-l'oeil and two chapels. The museum combines this artistic section with an archaeological one, with finds and plastics from the 4th century BC to the 4th century A.D. emerged from the excavations for the High Speed; free entrance, with route accompanied by the operators (reservation recommended on weekends); the municipality indicates Tuesday-Friday 9-13, Saturday and Sunday 9.30-13 and 16-20.
Another medieval church of the territory.
The stuccoes of Pietro Piazzoli.
Venue of the Di Vico family: here Giacomo, the last of the family, was captured, beheaded in Soriano nel Cimino in 1435.

A small civic museum that houses and exhibits tools and tools of peasant and craft life; it is also a cultural center with conferences and field researches on popular songs, flora and fauna, sayings, food and crafts.
View from the Bradano to the sea.
Then a ride to the ceramists' shops.
A small medieval village that can be reached from Laigueglia.
The 12th century civic palace.
A pilgrimage church overlooking the plain.
The Torelli castle on the Val d'Enza, transformed into a courtyard by Pomponio Torelli, with frescoes, furnishings and the loggia on the Reggian bank.

Cited from the end of the thirteenth century as the seat of the vicar of the prince bishop of Trento, who went up to the valley twice a year to administer justice; renovated in the sixteenth century by artists of the Buonconsiglio yard, prison since the beginning of the nineteenth century, purchased by the Magnifica Comunità in 1850 and reopened as a museum-pinacoteca on July 5, 2012. He painted paintings of the School of Fiemme (XVII-XIX century) in chronological order; in the nineteenth-century prisons the incisions of the prisoners remain. Guided tours every day, even theatricalized.

Set in a characteristic barn of the village of Cima Rest, it is divided into three rooms: the barn on the upper floor, the barn and the caséra on the lower floor. The exhibits, mostly tools of agricultural, craft and dairy work, are chosen for their symbolic and cultural value and show how the interiors of these buildings once presented themselves.
Next to the Villa Reale, wanted by Niso Fumagalli, founder in 1964 of the Italian Rosa Association, seat of international competitions since 1965; over 400 varieties.
The municipality indicates it as the most important architectural monument of Adrano; the monastery was erected in 1596.

Village at the foot of the Carnic Alps where the Livenza and the Gorgazzo are born, with the eighteenth-century castle on the hill, the church of San Giacomo of 1262 and, on the border with Caneva, the UNESCO Palù di Livenza building site.
The rural civilization of Friuli, with garden and rose garden.
A landscape of clear rocks for excursions in the Metalliferous Hills.

It rises on the foundations of the first parish church of the village, erected in the middle of the twelfth century by the Benedictine monks of Lerino of the Cenobe of Bergeggi and then named after Saint Eugenio; the current church was erected in 1650 by the will of the Altarese glassmaker Matteo Buzzone.

Pre-Roman settlement mentioned by Virgilio for its olive groves, entered the Roman orbit in 290 BC and became municipium in Augustian age, with hole, thermal baths and cisterns; in 146 BC. Lucio Mummio sent three votive dedications. The elliptical amphitheatre (94 x 66 m), partly dug into the rock, was rebuilt at the behest of Trajan as attested by two inscriptions of 115 A.D., and under the arena runs a tunnel turned once connected to the hole.

Borgo dell'alta valle del Cesano at the foot of Monte Catria, founded in the thirteenth century by the free Municipality of Gubbio as a garrison on the road between Umbria and the Adriatic. In its territory stands the Camaldolese monastery of Santa Croce di Fonte Avellana, cited by Dante in Paradise, and the early Christian crypt of San Biagio.
A forest and a 16th century villa.

In the upper Graveglia Valley, less than 20 km from Lavagna, the manganese deposit in the Monte Alpe diaspers was the most important in Europe; it has given numerous rare and new minerals. Museum since 2000, owned by the Aveto Park Authority since 2009: more than 8 of the more than 25 km of galleries are equipped for the visit, reached with the mining train, with routes of different lengths and difficulties and guided tours. Visitor center with bar, multimedia room, mineral collections, picnic area, guesthouse and self-guided paths. Tel. 0185 338876.

Monastic complex founded in 1073 by the Benedictines of Cluniac and passed to the Vallombrosans in 1090, around which the medieval village developed. The Romanesque church and the bell tower are from the 12th to the 11th century, the cloister is Renaissance and the complex also has baroque elements. Agnolo Firenzuola was abbot for a few years.
The myth of Nuvolari.

In 1584 Luigi retired to pray in a 16th century Gonzaga country house; since 1846 he has been a member of the College of Virgins. It preserves a spring source of Etruscan times and traces of a Roman villa with mosaic with white and black tiles of the I-II century AD and a circular underground room of about 6 meters.
Renaissance Basilica built on a Romanesque structure, of which remain the bell tower and traces of walls.

One of the most important coastal wetlands, managed by the WWF: the chessboard of the tanks, made from the ancient coastal pantani, is dotted with windmills, the Dutch-style star ones with six wooden blades and the American ones with sheet metal blades, used to move water between the tanks and grind the salt. There are flamingos, spatulae, big white herons, garzettes, swamp falcons and small limits, to be seen especially in autumn (September-November) and in spring (February-May); the Via del Sale, to be followed also by bike, connects Trapani to Marsala.
A castle of the Vallesina.

Built from 1680 to 1723 on the site of a Byzantine basilica of the IX century: a Latin cross with a single nave with four chapels, a baroque façade with two bell towers; it houses the Madonna of the Snow of the sixteenth century, a marble triptych by Antonello Gagini and three bronze portals by Giuseppe Niglia.
For the Renaissance portal and the paintings of Spain.
The cathedral with polychrome marbles and the Bell Tower, today symbol of the city, in the historic center.

Borgo perched on Mount Ginestro above Palestrina, with the Rocca dei Colonna on the ancient acropolis, polygonal walls of the 6th century BC and views of the Sacco valley and Rome; here Luigi Comencini turned in 1953 "Pane," love and fantasy" .
The hermitage-monastery of Celestine V set in the mountain.
The symbol of Avellino.

Palatine chapel of the Longobard court of the second half of the eighth century, then church of the Benedictine women's monastery: inside six female figures in stucco to high relief little bigger than the real, frescoes, floor in opus sectile and a wooden choir of the fourteenth century.
The balcony on the two bays.
The 4000 steps.
The Mastio-prison of the legends of the village.
The parish priest of the country.

On the plateau of Monte Pallano, on the road between Tornareccio and Colledimezzo, a settlement lived from the 4th century BC to the 2nd A.D., fortified outpost under control of the Val di Sangro during the Sanniti wars. The excavations have brought to light, next to Fonte Benedetti, a large late-Hellenistic square on three sides, identified as a forum, with shops and houses, and at least three temples recognized by the architectural terracotta. The visit starts from the Documentation Centre at Lake Nero; guided tours by reservation.
Monastery and ancient church founded in 1590 by the Capuchins on a donated land, next to the sanctuary of Blessed Angel.
The sunset on lava rocks.

Founded in 1983 on the initiative of Pro Loco after a collection of over 3,000 objects started in 1978, he received a mention at the European Museum of the Year Award. Six sections (farm art, textile fibers, terracotta, wood, iron, costumes) with a wooden wine press and a working 18th century lathe, a Calabrian frame, a 12th century host mold, a rebuilt forge and traditional costumes from different countries along the steps. It is located in the seventeenth-century Palazzo Aceti-Amoroso; the Parco delle Serre presents it in the Museum Polo La Filanda. Hours according to the municipality: Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 9-12, Sunday 16-18.
High altitude woods.
The sanctuary of the blessed.
Medieval frescoes in the ancient mother church.
Farmland of the valley of the river Pora, in a basin shaped like a glass with the villages of Carbuta and Eze, linked to contemporary art with the museum of the Casa del Console.
Archaeology re-emerged with reclamation.
A door signed Giulio Romano.
Beaches of the natural reserve of the Bandite di Scarlino, reachable only on foot for paths.
The underground church under the collegiate.
Since 1992 the protected area of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, the wildest of the Piedmont Alps, with bivouacs, shelters and fauna of chamois, deer and wolves; Verbania is part of it.
The village of the calderai and their jargon, the \'baccaiamentoÂ .
visit only with guide on reservation, private entrance (Visit Lazio)
The frescoes of Antoniazzo Romano.

Città della Piana was born from the union of the farmhouses of Radicena and Jatrinoli, named "Città del Libro 2024" and known for the late spring Infiorata; among the places to visit italia.it indicates the Romanesque Cathedral with rose window and two bell towers, the baroque Villa Zerbi by Filippo Frangipane, Contestabile Palace and the monumental Cemetery of Radicena.
Eight different waters in one hill.
The prehistory camuna to measure of child.
A bay of clear and grainy sand with clear and shallow waters, sheltered from the mistral, closed by the promontory with the tower of Coltellazzo and a cliff rich in marine life.
The Jesuit college church.
An ancient itinerary between archaeology and woods of the Val di Vara.
At the foot of the staircase of the Mother Church, with Gothic arch; on the door of the sacristy a plaque with Gothic inscription of 1375, the oldest text of the country.
It is the oldest of the monuments of Ravenna still in use as a sacred space.
The seafaring heart of the country.
Nineteenth and twentieth centuries inside the castle.

Abbey of Santa Maria di Farfa, founded in the middle of the sixth century, privileged by Charlemagne in 775 and known for the scriptorium of the IX-XI centuries; national monument since 1928 and stage of the Via di Francesco. The basilica has a fourteenth-century portal with frescoed bezel of 1508, three Renaissance aisles with the Universal Judgment of Henrik van der Broek (1561), grotesque school pumpkin (1576) and a golden coffered ceiling with the Orsini coat of arms. Around the hamlet of the shops was born for fairs, with wooden architraves of 1480 and a 17th century frame still active.
Short paths.

In the Palazzo Cupane, acquired and restored by the Municipality in 1990, the museum was created from the private collection of clothes and accessories by the architect Giuseppe Miraudo and was inaugurated in the years 1993-97. It preserves over a thousand pieces (1,500 according to the card) including dresses, even evening and wedding dresses, accessories, costumes and underwear of Sicilian fashion from the eighteenth to the early twentieth century; some pieces were exhibited in Brazil and the USA. Open Monday-Friday 9.30-12.30, Saturday and Sunday 16-19.
